candidates.fulltext: IntroductionExposure to respirable occupational dusts remains a persistent global health crisis, particularly in mining, construction, and manufacturing [1, 2]. Occupational dusts such as coal mine dust, crystalline silica (e.g. quartz), and asbestos fibres exhibit distinct physicochemical features that shape characteristic patterns of injury and disease. Despite regulatory advances, coal workers’ pneumoconiosis, silicosis, asbestosis, and asbestos-related malignant mesothelioma remain major occupational health concerns, with increasing absolute burdens or regional resurgence reported in many settings [3–6]. As such, defining how particle physicochemistry shapes the molecular pathways underlying the transition from exposure to chronic inflammation, fibrosis, and malignancy is essential for strengthening risk assessment, refining regulatory guidelines, and informing therapeutic development.To address these gaps, this review synthesizes the pathogenic “chain of events” triggered by inhalation of respirable occupational dusts, with particular emphasis on how dust surface chemistry and reactivity shape the initiating injury and downstream disease trajectory. We position the alveolar macrophages (AMs) as the central sentinel and trigger of injury, linking classical concepts of phagocytosis-associated membrane/lysosomal damage to contemporary molecular mechanisms, emphasizing the cell death pathway related adverse outcomes. We then trace how macrophage-derived signalling propagates to structural cells, including epithelial cells and fibroblasts, and how recruited immune populations enhance or modulate disease progression. Finally, we discuss how these mechanistic insights can inform the development of targeted therapies to interrupt key pathogenic nodes. Among all the industries, mining, construction and manufacturing are the industries that recorded the highest numbers of dust-related occupational diseases [7–9]. As a result of their wide application in major sectors (building, (coal) mining, construction, tunnelling and engineered stone manufacture), respirable asbestos, crystalline silica (e.g. quartz) and coal mining dust are the top three regulated dusts given their crucial role in contributing to severe respiratory disorders, inflammation and complications in individuals [10]. Most of the diagnosed occupational diseases are a combination of different conditions [11]. Globally, occupational exposure to airborne particulate matter, gases and fumes was estimated to account for approximately 519,000 deaths in 2016 (95% uncertainty interval [UI]: 441,000–609,000), including 21,500 deaths from pneumoconiosis, 37,600 deaths from asthma, and 460,100 deaths from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The corresponding DALYs were approximately 0.58 million for pneumoconiosis, 2.3 million for asthma, and 10.7 million for COPD [12]. From 1990 to 2019, there was a 61.5% increase in global incidence of cases of pneumoconiosis with the highest incidence recorded in China (136,755 cases), followed by India (11,670 cases) and the United States (10,014 cases), respectively [14]. candidates.fulltext: IntroductionThe word “sarcoidosis” derives from the Greek sarx (flesh) and -oid (resembling). Caesar Boeck introduced it in 1899 for skin lesions that histologically resembled sarcoma [1]. The designation was descriptive rather than aetiological, reflecting microscopic appearance. More than a century later, “sarcoidosis” continues to be used for a condition whose cause remains incompletely understood [2, 3]. When a specific trigger is identified for a previously idiopathic condition, nomenclature has often shifted from descriptive to aetiological, as when “Salem sarcoid” was reclassified as chronic beryllium disease (CBD) once the beryllium lymphocyte proliferation test (BeLPT) identified the trigger [4]. This review examines whether a comparable transition may be appropriate for silica-associated granulomatous disease.Some basic distinctions should be established at the outset, as “silica” is used loosely in the clinical literature. Silica denotes silicon dioxide (SiO2) itself, whereas silicates (e.g. kaolin, talc, mica, asbestos) combine silicon–oxygen tetrahedra with cations; the two behave differently in tissue and are distinguished under polarised light, silicates being strongly birefringent. Silica occurs in crystalline forms (quartz, cristobalite, tridymite), classified by the International Agency for Research on Cancer as carcinogenic and responsible for classical silicosis, and in amorphous forms (raw diatomaceous earth, fumed and colloidal silica, engineered nanosilica) traditionally regarded as less fibrogenic. That dichotomy has weakened. Pathogenicity tracks surface reactivity more closely than crystallinity and, above all, the number and density of nearly free silanols (NFS), which are surface Si–OH groups too distant from their neighbours to hydrogen-bond and therefore free to interact with cell membranes [5, 6]. NFS are generated when quartz is freshly fractured and are lost as the surface ages or is heated, which is why newly cut engineered stone is more toxic than the same mass of weathered dust and why some amorphous silicas are membranolytic while others are inert [5]. Amorphous forms are not automatically benign; granulomatous lung disease has been described after exposure to amorphous silica in light-bulb manufacture [7], and calcination converts amorphous diatomite into cristobalite [8]. Surface chemistry, dose rate and the immunomodulatory as well as pro-inflammatory actions of particles are therefore relevant throughout [9].Sarcoidosis is increasingly understood as a heterogeneous syndrome with several potential triggers rather than a single idiopathic entity; mycobacterial antigens (mKatG), Cutibacterium acnes, beryllium, metals and organic dusts have all been implicated [10, 11]. The American Thoracic Society (ATS) 2020 clinical practice guideline identifies three diagnostic pillars, as follows 1) a compatible clinical presentation, 2) histological evidence of non-necrotising granulomatous inflammation and 3) exclusion of alternative causes of granulomatous disease [12]. The third pillar raises a conceptual difficulty, as identifying silica exposure in a patient with sarcoid-type granulomas may itself constitute an alternative cause. In practice, such patients are often still labelled as having sarcoidosis, which affects occupational disease recognition.The distinction has practical consequences, as sarcoidosis (International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision (ICD-10) D86) is not included in the International Labour Organization (ILO) list of occupational diseases [13], whereas silicosis (ICD-10 J62) can, in some jurisdictions, support occupational disease recognition [14, 15]. These implications are discussed further below.Three broad positions can be identified. The first regards silica-triggered granulomatous disease as a “silica-induced sarcoid-like reaction” (SISLR), a response to a recognised agent that by definition would not meet current criteria for sarcoidosis [16]. The second treats sarcoidosis as a syndrome with multiple potential triggers, including silica [17]. The third, outlined in a 2025 multinational case series [18], proposes the hybrid term “silicosarcoidosis”, which has been the subject of ongoing discussion regarding its implications for occupational disease recognition [19]. In this narrative review, we consider whether a continuum model – that is, a model implying a range of conditions within a continuum – may help to integrate these positions. By “continuum” we mean that the fibrotic and granulomatous responses to silica are two ends of a single graded reaction to one agent, with intermediate and shifting presentations between them, rather than separate diseases that happen to co-occur; SISLR corresponds to the granulomatous end. We prefer “continuum” to “spectrum”, which now carries connotations from an unrelated literature. candidates.title: Prognostic assessment of acute exacerbation of interstitial lung disease: From conventional models to artificial intelligence-driven models.
candidates.abstract: Acute exacerbation of interstitial lung disease (AE-ILD) is a life-threatening clinical event associated with poor prognosis. Accurate outcome prediction is important for treatment planning and resource allocation. This review evaluates evidence on prognostic risk factors and clinical scoring systems and discusses the application of artificial intelligence (AI) into the key stages of model development for AE-ILD prognostication. Conventional prognostic approaches enable rapid risk stratification but have limited capacity to integrate heterogeneous data and account for clinical complexity. AI-driven approaches have been preliminarily applied to clinical and imaging data for prognostic assessment. However, direct AE-ILD-specific evidence is limited, and the incremental prognostic value of existing AI models over conventional approaches remains uncertain. Multimodal integration, independent external validation, and model interpretability remain major research gaps. Addressing these gaps through representative multicentre studies may enable AI to reinforce conventional prognostic assessment and promote more individualised risk stratification in AE-ILD.

candidates.title: Assessment of pneumoconiosis by dusty job type among underground coal miners participating in the Coal Workers' Health Surveillance Program,1991-2024.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Exposure to respirable coal mine dust causes coal workers' pneumoconiosis (CWP). Despite regulatory efforts, progressive massive fibrosis (PMF), the most severe form of pneumoconiosis persists, particularly in Central Appalachia. This study evaluated pneumoconiosis prevalence among underground coal miners by occupation during 1991-2024.
METHODS: The study analyzed data from 30,319 underground miners in the Coal Workers Health Surveillance Program (CWHSP) from 1991-2024. Pneumoconiosis was identified from chest radiographs using standardized classifications. Disease prevalence was compared across mining occupations and geographic regions, with adjustment for underground mining tenure.
RESULTS: Continuous miner operators (CMOs) and roof bolters experienced the highest prevalence of disease. Compared with miners who never held these occupations, adjusted prevalence of CWP was higher among CMOs (PR = 1.8; 95% CI: 1.6-2.0) and roof bolters (PR = 1.4; 95% CI: 1.3-1.6). PMF prevalence was also elevated among CMOs (PR = 3.0; 95% CI: 2.3-4.0) and roof bolters (PR = 1.4; 95% CI: 1.1-1.9). CWP prevalence was 8.4% in Central Appalachia versus 1.5% in the rest of U. S., while PMF prevalence was 1.3% versus 0.1%. After adjustment for tenure, Central Appalachian miners had 3.9 times the prevalence of CWP (95% CI: 3.4-4.5) and 10 times the prevalence of PMF (95% CI: 5.7-17.5).
DISCUSSION: CMOs and roof bolters experienced the highest prevalence of pneumoconiosis, consistent with their classification as MSHA-designated "dusty" occupations. Markedly higher disease prevalence across all occupations in Central Appalachia indicates persistent hazardous dust exposures and underscores the need for continued prevention and surveillance efforts.

candidates.title: Lifetime Endogenous Estrogen Exposure Predicts Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis Risk in Postmenopausal Women Based on a Nationwide Population Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conflicting results exist regarding the association between endogenous estrogen exposure and the risk of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). We aimed to investigate the relationship between lifetime endogenous estrogen exposure and the development of IPF among postmenopausal women.
METHODS: Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service database for the period between 1 January 2009 and 31 December 2022, we analyzed a total of 1,388,645 postmenopausal women without previous history of IPF in 2009. The exposure was lifetime endogenous estrogen exposure (duration between the age of menarche and the age of menopause). The primary outcome was new-onset IPF. Participants were followed until the date of new IPF diagnosis, death, or 31 December 2022.
RESULTS: During the median follow-up period of 12.4 (interquartile range, 12.1-12.7) years, 0.13% of postmenopausal women developed IPF, with an incidence rate of 0.109 per 1,000 person-years. There was a dose-dependent inverse relationship between endogenous estrogen exposure and the incidence of IPF (0.144/1,000 person-years for < 30 years, 0.104/1,000 person-years for 30-39 years and 0.101/1,000 person-years for ≥ 40 years). Multivariable Cox-regression analysis showed that the risk of developing IPF was dose-dependently decreased as endogenous estrogen exposure increased (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75-0.96 for 30-39 years; aHR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.61-0.96 for ≥ 40 years compared to < 30 years).
CONCLUSION: Among postmenopausal women, lifetime endogenous estrogen exposure showed a protective role from developing IPF.

This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic value of sphingolipid-related genes in IPF and to identify potential sphingolipid-associated biomarkers.

In vitro experiments demonstrated that CCDC80 knockdown attenuated fibroblast proliferation, migration, and fibrotic activation.

candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The long-term risk of clinical new-onset pulmonary fibrosis (PF) and its various downstream impacts following SARS-CoV-2 infection remain incompletely characterized in existing literature.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort was analyzed using Montefiore Health System electronic health record data over 4.5 years (March 2020-August 2024). New-onset PF and subsequent downstream impacts were identified by diagnostic ICD-10 codes. Covariate balance was assessed and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) models were used to estimate PF risk and logistic and Poisson regression models were used to assess post-PF secondary outcomes. candidates.title: Local and systemic SP-D in IPF and SARD-ILD.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surfactant protein D (SP-D) is recognized as a potential biomarker for non-invasive evaluation of interstitial lung disease (ILD). Alterations in local and systemic cytokines associated with alveolar injury may mirror the underlying pathological processes in ILD. The study aimed to examine the correlation between plasma and sputum SP-D levels, lung function, and disease severity in patients suffering from ILD.
METHODS: SP-D concentrations were evaluated in plasma and induced sputum samples from 34 healthy controls and 84 ILD patients, including 54 with systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease-ILD (SARD-ILD) and 30 individuals with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Associations with pulmonary function were examined.
RESULTS: ILD patients showed significantly higher SP-D than controls. Both plasma and sputum levels were elevated in IPF and SARD-ILD, with plasma SP-D higher in IPF. Plasma and sputum SP-D were moderately correlated with ILD patients (r = 0.2497, P < 0.05). Plasma SP-D was inversely associated with lung function, including reduced forced vital capacity (r=- 0.3778, P = 0.0002) and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (r=- 0.4248, P < 0.0001). These associations were significant in SARD-ILD and showed a non-significant trend in IPF. No clear link was found between sputum SP-D and pulmonary function.
CONCLUSIONS: Both plasma and sputum SP-D levels were elevated in ILD patients; however, only plasma SP-D demonstrated a strong negative correlation with pulmonary function. This suggests that plasma SP-D, likely reflecting leakage from the injured lung interstitium into circulation, may serve as a practical tool for non-invasive disease severity assessment in routine clinical practice, potentially aiding in risk stratification and monitoring of disease progression.

candidates.title: [A CASE OF BCG-ASSOCIATED INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA WITH Mycobacterium bovis BACTEREMIA SUCCESSFULLY TREATED WITH CORTICOSTEROIDS ALONE].
candidates.abstract: We report a case in a 65-year-old man receiving intravesical BCG therapy for superficial bladder cancer. He was admitted due to a prostate abscess accompanied by fever, liver dysfunction, and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). During antibiotic therapy, he developed interstitial pneumonia with acute respiratory failure, which rapidly improved after steroid pulse therapy. Mycobacterium bovis (M. bovis) was isolated from blood and sputum cultures taken at the diagnosis of interstitial pneumonia, suggesting the involvement of hematogenous dissemination of BCG. Despite the absence of anti-tuberculosis therapy, repeat blood and sputum cultures were negative at discharge. Isolation of M.bovis from the blood culture is extremely rare. The clinical improvement and bacterial clearance observed following treatment with corticosteroids alone, despite the presence of bacteremia, suggest that the primary pathophysiology of this complication may be a hypersensitivity reaction rather than bacterial proliferation. We report this case as an instance of transient hematogenous dissemination and a severe systemic reaction following intravesical BCG therapy.

candidates.title: Combined Pulmonary Fibrosis and Emphysema: Current Status and Future Perspective.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema (CPFE) is a clinical syndrome defined by the coexistence of upper-lobe emphysema and lower-lobe pulmonary fibrosis. It is characterized by clinical, functional, and radiologic features that differ significantly from isolated idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
SUMMARY: This review summarizes recent advances in CPFE, focusing on etiologic classification, clinical and radiologic features, diagnosis and treatment, prognostic evaluation, and emerging perspectives in artificial intelligence (AI). Based on current research, we summarize the etiologic classification of CPFE into four types: smoking-related, systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease-associated, occupational- and environmental-related, and idiopathic. These types differ in epidemiologic characteristics, imaging patterns, and disease progression. Consequently, future research is expected to focus on mechanism-driven phenotyping and quantitative imaging analysis, where AI may provide additional value in disease identification, risk stratification, and dynamic prognostic assessment.
KEY MESSAGE: This review proposes a novel framework for CPFE, integrating etiologic subtyping and a diagnostic algorithm to guide precise management, and highlights AI-powered strategies for future personalized interventions.

candidates.title: Exogenous tryptophan aggravates experimental lung fibrosis through activation of AKT-mTORC1 pathway.
candidates.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is marked by aberrant lung remodeling and excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation. Previously, we observed elevated tryptophan (TRP) levels in the lungs of IPF patients, but its role in fibrogenesis remained unclear. This study examines whether TRP modulate the severity of lung fibrosis by measuring ECM component expression in TRP-treated lung fibroblasts. The activities of key TRP metabolism enzymes, tryptophan hydroxylase (TPH-1) and indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO/TDO), were also assessed in IPF lung. Exogenous TRP administration in bleomycin-exposed mice significantly exacerbated lung damage and fibrosis. TPH-1 levels were elevated in lung tissues and primary fibroblasts of IPF patients compared to controls, while IDO/TDO expression showed no significant differences between two groups. TRP treatment increased fibroblast proliferation and upregulated collagen, fibronectin, and α-smooth muscle actin expression, whereas TRP deprivation reduced these ECM component levels. Additionally, TRP upregulated the AKT-mTORC1 and TGF-β1 signaling pathways in IPF fibroblasts. These findings indicate that elevated TRP levels contribute to IPF pathogenesis and suggest that targeting the TRP pathway could offer therapeutic potential for lung fibrosis including IPF.

candidates.title: Immune-driven remodeling in calcific aortic valve disease: mechanisms and immunotherapeutic opportunities.
candidates.abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a prevalent degenerative valvular disorder in the aging population, for which no pharmacological therapy has proven effective in halting or reversing disease progression. Over the past decade, CAVD has been increasingly recognized not as a passive degenerative process of calcium deposition, but as an active, inflammation-driven disease characterized by osteogenic remodeling. This process is initiated and sustained by endothelial injury, lipid retention, immune cell infiltration, and phenotypic transition of valvular interstitial cells. Growing evidence indicates that innate and adaptive immune responses may contribute to disease amplification. Innate immune cells propagate local inflammatory signaling through inflammasome activation, extracellular vesicle communication, protease release, and neutrophil extracellular trap formation, while adaptive immune cells further shape disease progression by sustaining cytokine networks that promote fibrosis and osteogenic reprogramming within the valvular microenvironment. Based on these mechanistic insights, this review further discusses emerging translational strategies aimed at targeting key pathogenic processes in CAVD, including modulation of inflammatory signaling, restoration of adaptive immune homeostasis, regulation of extracellular matrix remodeling and antifibrotic pathways, inhibition of VIC osteogenic differentiation, as well as development of patient stratification and local drug delivery approaches. Collectively, these strategies may provide a conceptual framework for earlier, non-surgical interventions for CAVD.

candidates.title: Case Report: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis presenting as a multiple sclerosis mimic.
candidates.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) rarely involves the central nervous system and may closely resemble inflammatory demyelinating disease. We report a 32-year-old woman with adult-onset asthma and recurrent sinusitis who presented with bilateral lower-extremity sensory symptoms and neuropathic pain. Brain and spinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated multifocal T2-hyperintense lesions fulfilling dissemination in space and time according to the 2017 McDonald criteria. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed mild pleocytosis, CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands, and eosinophils on qualitative cytological examination. Multiple sclerosis (MS) was initially suspected and intravenous methylprednisolone resulted in partial improvement. Three weeks later, the patient developed palpable purpura, inflammatory arthralgia, and left foot-elevating paresis. Follow-up MRI demonstrated a new enhancing lesion and electrophysiological studies revealed axonal neuropathy. Retrospective review of the initial laboratory results showed that peripheral eosinophilia was already present at baseline, while subsequent evaluation identified eosinophilic gastritis on gastroscopic biopsy and eosinophilic bone marrow infiltration. The diagnosis of EGPA was established based on the clinical presentation, laboratory findings, and histopathological evidence of eosinophilic inflammation, and the patient fulfilled the 2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for EGPA. Treatment with corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide followed by maintenance mepolizumab resulted in sustained clinical stability. This case highlights that EGPA may present with radiological and CSF-findings suggestive of MS and emphasizes the importance of integrating systemic manifestations to avoid diagnostic delay.

candidates.title: Pretreatment neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio is associated with clinical phenotypes and infection-related mortality in microscopic polyangiitis: the multicentre REVEAL cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) remains associated with substantial early mortality despite advances in immunosuppressive therapy, highlighting the need for simple biomarkers that facilitate LR) has been associated with disease activity and prognosis in antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV), its phenotype-specific significance in newly diagnosed MPA remains unclear. We investigated whether pretreatment NLR is associated with clinical phenotype, disease course, and long-term outcomes in MPA.
METHODS: Among 418 patients with MPA enrolled in the multicentre REVEAL cohort between 2005 and 2025, 340 newly diagnosed treatment-naïve patients fulfilling the 2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria were included. Patients were stratified into tertiles according to pretreatment NLR. Baseline characteristics, temporal outcomes, and survival were compared. Infection-related mortality was further evaluated after stabilised inverse probability weighting (IPW).
RESULTS: Higher pretreatment NLR was associated with greater disease severity, including higher Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (P < 0.001) and Five-Factor Score (P = 0.03), more frequent diffuse alveolar haemorrhage (P = 0.015), poorer renal function (P = 0.003), and more intensive remission-induction therapy, including methylprednisolone pulse therapy and rituximab. In contrast, interstitial lung disease was more common in patients with lower NLR (P = 0.001). Despite these baseline differences, disease activity, glucocorticoid tapering, and cumulative organ damage became comparable after treatment initiation. Pretreatment NLR was not associated with relapse-free survival (P = 0.44) but was associated with poorer overall survival (P = 0.012) and higher infection-related mortality (P = 0.002). After adjustment using IPW, the association with overall survival was no longer statistically significant, whereas the increased risk of infection-related mortality remained significant (HR 3.47

candidates.title: [Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis: a disease easily underestimated by rhinologists].
candidates.journal: Lin chuang er bi yan hou tou jing wai ke za zhi = Journal of clinical otorhinolaryngology head and neck surgery
candidates.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis commonly presents with asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with or without nasal polyps as early hallmark manifestations. Owing to its rarity, EGPA remains underrecognized in clinical practice, leading to substantial diagnostic challenges and delayed diagnosis. This review systematically summarizes the epidemiology, immunopathological mechanisms, and recent advances in the diagnosis and management of EGPA, with a particular focus on sinonasal involvement. This review highlights the pivotal role of rhinologists in identifying early warning signs and implementing appropriate diagnostic pathways. By adopting a rhinology-oriented perspective, this review aims to facilitate earlier recognition of EGPA, reduce diagnostic delay, and ultimately improve patient prognosis and long-term outcomes.

candidates.title: Post-ARDS Pulmonary Fibrosis: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Management.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a severe inflammatory lung injury caused by various factors, including infection, trauma and shock. The predominant pathological alteration in its late stages is pulmonary fibrosis (PF), characterised by progressive extracellular matrix deposition, architectural destruction and functional impairment. Particularly in COVID-19-induced ARDS, PF incidence has markedly increased, making it a major sequela impacting patients' long-term quality of life.
METHODS: This review systematically examines post-acute lung injury (ALI)/ARDS PF through three perspectives: pathogenesis, prediction and treatment.
RESULTS: Mechanistically, the fibrotic process involves epithelial injury and mesenchymal transition, fibroblast activation with aberrant extracellular matrix remodelling, dysregulated inflammation with immune cell involvement and clinical management-related factors. For prediction, various biomarkers (including growth factors, matrix proteins and inflammatory markers) and imaging features (particularly high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics) demonstrate clinical value. Integrated multiparameter models incorporating artificial intelligence show promise for early identification and risk stratification of high-risk patients. Therapeutic strategies encompass anti-inflammatory approaches (e.g., corticosteroids and antioxidants), antifibrotic agents (pirfenidone and nintedanib), cell-based therapies (mesenchymal stem cells and exosomes) and emerging genetic/RNA interventions. However, specific preventive and therapeutic approaches tailored to the post-ALI/ARDS PF population remain inadequate in clinical practice.
CONCLUSIONS: Future research should focus on elucidating underlying mechanisms, refining early-warning systems, exploring personalised treatments and facilitating clinical translation. The ultimate goal is to transition from traditional supportive care to proa

candidates.title: Effect of pirfenidone on the short- and long-term outcomes in pulmonary infection-related acute respiratory distress syndrome: a prospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pirfenidone, approved for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), slows lung function decline and reduces fibrosis, including in post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis. Its early use in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains uncertain. This study evaluated the effects of early pirfenidone administration on short- and long-term outcomes in pulmonary infection-related ARDS.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 97 ARDS patients were consecutively recruited and assigned to Pirfenidone (n = 29), Glucocorticoid (n = 38), or Control (n = 30) groups according to the severity and clinical course of the disease by the attending clinical team, all receiving standard care. Short-term outcomes included 28-day mortality, ICU length of stay, and hospital length of stay. Long-term outcomes at 3 and 6 months included chest CT fibrosis score, pulmonary function [forced vital capacity (FVC) and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO)], SpO2/FiO2 ratio, modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea score, and Activities of Daily Living (ADL) score. Safety was assessed via adverse events and laboratory parameters.
RESULTS: At 6 months, the Pirfenidone Group had significantly lower chest CT fibrosis scores than the Glucocorticoid Group [3.0 (0.0-6.5) vs. 6.0 (4.0-8.0), p < 0.05], which was comparable to that of the Control Group. FVC, SpO2/FiO2, and ADL scores at 3 and 6 months were significantly higher in the Pirfenidone Group compared with both Glucocorticoid and Control groups (all p < 0.01). Long-term outcomes improved relative to baseline (p < 0.05). Short-term outcomes, mMRC scores, and safety indicators showed no significant differences among groups (p > 0.05). No severe drug-related adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSION: Early pirfenidone administration in pulmonary infection-related ARDS enhances long-term functional recovery and reduces fibrosis without increasing safety risks, although it does not significantly impact short-term outcomes. These

candidates.title: Sarcopenia affects the outcomes and tolerability in patients with interstitial lung disease receiving nintedanib: a retrospective study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nintedanib is approved for various interstitial lung diseases (ILDs). Although sarcopenia, which is characterized by a loss of skeletal muscle mass, is known to affect the outcome of ILD, the outcome of patients with sarcopenia receiving nintedanib remains unclear.
METHODS: Fifty-six patients with ILD who were initiated on nintedanib between 2015 and 2023 were included. On CT images obtained prior to the introduction of nintedanib, the thoracic skeletal muscle area at the T4 level was measured to estimate the skeletal muscle index (SMI). Patients with an SMI in the lowest quartile were defined as the sarcopenia group, and the remaining patients as the non-sarcopenia group. The times from the start of nintedanib to all-cause death (overall survival: OS) and the first acute exacerbation (exacerbation-free survival: EFS) were compared between the two groups. Dose reduction and discontinuation rate of nintedanib were also evaluated. The cut-off date was determined to be 5 years.
RESULTS: Whereas age, sex, and serum levels of albumin and Klebs von den Lungen-6 did not differ between the two groups, forced vital capacity (%FVC) (63.7% vs. 72.7%), diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (%DLco) (41% vs. 55.9%) and body mass index (20.6 vs. 25.2 kg/m2) were significantly lower in the sarcopenia group (n = 14) than in the non-sarcopenia group (n = 42). The OS was significantly shorter in the sarcopenia group (26.5 months vs. not reached, P = 0.03). Similarly, EFS was significantly shorter in the sarcopenia group (15.8 vs. 44.6 months, P = 0.002). In the multivariate Cox proportional hazard models adjusted for age and sex, %FVC and baseline sarcopenia were significantly associated with OS (%FVC: hazard ratio (HR) 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93-0.98, P = 0.005, sarcopenia: HR 3.37, 95% CI 1.27-8.93, P = 0.01). Likewise, %FVC, %DLco and sarcopenia were significantly associated with EFS (%FVC: HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-0.98, P = 0.0004, %DLco: HR 0.96,

candidates.title: Integrative network toxicology and machine learning reveal the potential role of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural in exacerbating pulmonary fibrosis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF), a ubiquitous furan derivative formed during the thermal processing of carbohydrate-rich foods, represents a widespread dietary exposure. However, its potential contribution to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains unclear. This study investigated the molecular links between 5-HMF and IPF using an integrated computational and experimental approach.
METHODS: IPF-related genes were identified through transcriptomic analysis combining differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Candidate targets were obtained by intersecting IPF-associated genes with predicted 5-HMF targets. Functional enrichment analysis, ensemble machine learning, and SHAP interpretation were performed to prioritize candidate targets, while molecular docking was used to explore potential 5-HMF-target interactions. A bleomycin-induced mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis was further used to evaluate the effects of 5-HMF on fibrotic lung injury and the transcriptional expression of prioritized candidate genes.
RESULTS: A total of 1,776 IPF-associated genes and 143 predicted 5-HMF targets were identified, yielding 12 overlapping candidate targets. Enrichment analysis implicated these genes in fibrosis-related pathways, including chemical carcinogenesis-receptor activation and estrogen signaling. Machine learning analysis prioritized seven core targets (CA2, CA4, ESR2, F10, HSP90AA1, PLA2G1B, and PTPRB), all of which accommodated 5-HMF in their orthosteric pockets in blind docking, albeit with weak, non-selective Vina scores (-4.5 to -5.4 kcal/mol). In vivo, 5-HMF significantly exacerbated bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis, as demonstrated by aggravated lung injury, increased collagen deposition, and elevated expression of Hsp90aa1, Pla2g1b, Ca4, F10, Acta2, and Col1a1.
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that 5-HMF may exacerbate fibrotic lung injury through multiple fibrosis-related molecular targets and pathways. The

candidates.title: The prognostic value of erythrocyte sedimentation rate in all-cause mortality of patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: Based on inpatient hospital records.
candidates.abstract: BackgroundIdiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic progressive interstitial lung disease with a high mortality rate. Reliable biomarker can enable clinicians to judge the development and prognosis of IPF.ObjectivesThis study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) for predicting all-cause mortality in IPF.DesignThis retrospective cohort study enrolled patients hospitalized with IPF between January 1st, 2015 and May 31st, 2023.MethodsData was collected regarding patient demographics, laboratory analysis results, and the following pulmonary function parameters: the forced expiratory volume in one second percentage of predicted (FEV1 %pred), forced vital capacity percentage of predicted (FVC %pred), diffusing capacity divided by the alveolar volume (DLCO/VA), DLCO, DLCO %pred. All-cause mortality data were collected throughout the 18 months follow-up period.ResultsA total of 510 IPF patients recruited for the final analysis, 131 (25.7%) died during follow-up. IPF patients who died were older, had a higher white blood cell, lactic dehydrogenase, fibrinogen and ESR. In addition, IPF patients who died had a worse pulmonary function, as evidenced by lower FEV1 %pred, FVC %pred, DLCO %pred and DLCO/VA (P<0.05). Logistic regression analysis showed that ESR was an independent risk factor for IPF patients who died, with OR=1.024, 95% CI=1.002-1.048 (P<0.05). Based on the receiver operating characteristic curve, ESR could predict all-cause mortality in IPF patients, with an area under the curve of 0.645 and a 95% CI of 0.591-0.700 (P<0.05). The optimal ESR cut-off value was determined to be 21.5 mm/h. Cox regression analysis revealed that IPF patients with an ESR ≥ 21.5 mm/h had a significantly higher all-cause mortality risk, with a hazard ratio of 5.406 and a 95% CI of 1.177-24.825 (P<0.05).ConclusionESR is a promising biomarker for predicting all-cause mortality in IPF patients.

candidates.title: Severe ARDS and secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis complicating a flare of adult-onset Still's disease: a case-based review.
candidates.abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a rare systemic inflammatory disorder in which parenchymal lung disease is an increasingly recognised complication, and macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) - that is, haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) secondary to an autoinflammatory or autoimmune condition (MAS-HLH) is a well-established one. Both carry disproportionately high morbidity and mortality. Although AOSD-associated lung disease and MAS-HLH are increasingly recognised as co-occurring manifestations of the same hyperinflammatory process, their combination, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) as the most severe form of lung involvement, remain under-reported. We report a 42-year-old woman with a background of AOSD who developed severe ARDS in the context of a five-week interruption of conventional synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) around incision and drainage of a perianal abscess with complicating fistulous disease and a flare during that period. She developed severe hypoxaemic respiratory failure requiring intubation on the day of admission and later prone positioning, subsequently complicated by development of MAS-HLH, evidenced by hyperferritinaemia, hypertriglyceridaemia, fever and bone marrow-confirmed haemophagocytosis. Her disease trajectory was further complicated by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and cytomegalovirus (CMV) reactivation. Management required sequential multi-target immunomodulation with corticosteroids, anakinra, ruxolitinib, tocilizumab and rituximab. She was mechanically ventilated for 19 days in intensive care and discharged from ICU on day 34 and from hospital following clinical stabilisation on day 73. This case illustrates that AOSD-related pulmonary disease can present as fulminant ARDS rather than the more indolent infiltrative patterns typically described and may be associated with other manifestations of AOSD including MAS-HLH. candidates.title: Treprostinil: Mechanism of Action, Clinical, and Translational Science.
candidates.abstract: Treprostinil is a synthetic prostacyclin analogue with a tricyclic benzindene structure that confers markedly enhanced metabolic stability relative to native prostacyclin, enabling delivery by four distinct routes-intravenous, subcutaneous, inhaled, and oral-that together constitute a mainstay of pharmacotherapy for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Herein, we review the mechanism of action, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) characteristics, and clinical development of treprostinil, with primary emphasis on its well-established role in PAH, including detailed dosing and PK data across all four approved routes, and secondary emphasis on its recently approved role in pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and its investigational, plausible-future role in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) without a pulmonary hypertension requirement. Treprostinil activates the Gαs-coupled prostacyclin (IP) receptor to generate a sustained nuclear cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signal that is qualitatively distinct from earlier prostacyclin analogues, underlying both its established vasodilatory, antiproliferative, and antiplatelet effects in PAH and a mechanistic hypothesis of antifibrotic activity relevant to IPF. Treprostinil also engages the prostaglandin EP₂ and DP₁ receptors and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors, and inhibits transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)-driven extracellular matrix synthesis through mechanisms only partially explained by cAMP magnitude. Across the four approved routes, treprostinil exhibits route-specific pharmacokinetics-near-complete subcutaneous bioavailability with a 4-hour terminal half-life, oral bioavailability of approximately 17% with extensive first-pass CYP2C8 metabolism, and inhaled systemic bioavailability of approximately 64%-72%-that inform the distinct dosing and titration strategies detailed in this review. In a plausible, still-investigational extension of this pharmacology

candidates.title: Multisystem Langerhans cell histiocytosis with hypothyroidism and sclerosing cholangitis: a case report and review of the literature.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare disease caused by a disorder of dendritic cells. LCH mainly occurs in children and the damage of tissue is caused by proliferative dendritic cells which also provides important evidence for the diagnosis of this disease. In most LCH patients, only a single organ in the body is affected; however, multisystem involvement may occur, commonly affecting the bone marrow, liver, lungs, and central nervous system. In this report, we describe a case of multisystem LCH involving the skin, lungs, thyroid gland, liver, nails, and spleen.
CASE INTRODUCTION: A 20-year-old Han Chinese man was admitted into the liver disease department with complaints of anorexia, fatigue, and jaundice. Physical examination revealed extensive cutaneous lesions, nail lesions, macular sclera, and bilateral goiter. Lymphocytic thyroiditis was diagnosed based on fine-needle aspiration biopsy of the thyroid gland and corroborating clinical features-including the characteristic skin rash. Liver biopsy confirmed sclerosing cholangitis (SC). Response to treatment with Etoposide (VP-16), Prednisone acetate tablets, cyclophosphamide, and vinblastine was excellent. However, the erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) was initially elevated above the normal reference range. With disease remission, the corresponding ESR levels decreased.
CONCLUSIONS: LCH in this case involved not only the skin and thyroid, but also the liver, lungs, nails and possibly the spleen. Currently there are no standard treatment options and treatment needs to be individualized. It is rare that LCH with sclerosing cholangitis is the first presentation, and we should be vigilant to whether other organs are involved. An elevated ESR may be a valuable indicator of disease activity in patients with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

candidates.title: Managing trastuzumab deruxtecan-related adverse events in patients with metastatic breast cancer: insights from a worldwide survey of the Hermione EDUcational project.
candidates.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has shown remarkable efficacy in phase III trials in patients with HER2-positive early- and late-stage breast cancer and HER2-low/ultra-low metastatic breast cancer (mBC). However, toxicities remain prevalent and clinically relevant, leading to dose reductions/interruptions or discontinuation.
METHODS: A survey was conducted across oncologists in 13 countries worldwide to collect experiences in managing T-DXd-related toxicities, focusing on nausea/vomiting, fatigue, and interstitial lung disease (ILD) as key areas of clinical concern.
RESULTS: Ninety-nine experts participated in the survey. Nausea and fatigue were the most common toxicities, reported by 91.9% and 94.9% of respondents, respectively. 5-HT3 receptor antagonists, NK1 receptor antagonists, and corticosteroids were "very often" prescribed for prophylaxis. The frequency of use of second‑generation 5‑HT3 receptor antagonists varied among respondents. Most frequently, they employed an NK1 receptor antagonist combined with corticosteroids and 5‑HT3 receptor antagonists. Forty-four percent of respondents prescribed 4‑drug regimens incorporating NK1 receptor antagonists and olanzapine to all patients with nausea/vomiting above grade 1 in the first cycle, 35% reserved them for high‑risk patients, and 21% used them for all patients from cycle one. For all respondents, patients receiving T‑DXd experienced fatigue, with 65% observing it in more than 60% of patients, and most considered nausea/vomiting and fatigue to moderately or significantly affect daily activities and quality of life. ILD was reported as rare or occasional and was generally monitored using computed tomography.
CONCLUSION: Real-life management of T-DXd-related toxicities is complex and needs an ongoing comprehensive evaluation of patients before, during and after therapy, with a highly trained/skilled multidisciplinary team.

candidates.title: Anti-Ro52/TRIM21 seropositivity in interstitial lung disease: effect modification by disease subtype and myositis-specific antibody context.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-Ro52/TRIM21 shows contradictory prognostic associations in interstitial lung disease (ILD), protective in some cohorts and adverse in others. We evaluated whether it acts as an independent predictor or a phenotypic marker and whether its effect is modified by disease subtype and myositis-specific antibodies.
METHODS: We retrospectively identified 538 adults with radiologically confirmed interstitial lung disease (228 anti-Ro52-positive) from a 2010-2020 single-center cohort. Cox proportional-hazards models were sequentially adjusted for demographic, smoking, malignancy, and pulmonary-function covariates. Pre-specified effect modification by connective tissue disease (CTD) status and myositis-specific antibodies was assessed by likelihood-ratio interaction tests with false-discovery-rate correction. Robustness to missing data was supported by multiple imputation (m = 20) and a missing-not-at-random (MNAR) tipping-point analysis.
RESULTS: Ro52 positivity was associated with younger age, CTD predominance, and lower complement levels. Pre-specified effect modification was suggested: anti-Ro52 trended toward lower mortality in CTD-ILD (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.49-1.07, P = 0.104) but did not independently increase mortality within the anti-MDA5-positive subgroup (HR 1.73, 95% CI 0.66-4.54). Instead, the adverse prognostic effect of anti-MDA5 was numerically greater among anti-Ro52-positive than Ro52-negative patients (MDA5 HR 10.57, 95% CI 3.60-31.03 vs. 2.56, 95% CI 0.97-6.74), although the formal interaction term did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.055). The fully adjusted (Model 6) HR was 0.72 (95% CI 0.52-0.99; P = 0.045); further adjustment for CTD status (Model 7) attenuated the association to non-significance (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.54-1.04, P = 0.091), and IPCW weighting and time-varying-age analyses were likewise non-significant; malignancy independently predicted mortality (HR 1.81, 95% CI 1.15-2.88; P = 0.012).
