candidates.title: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cellular fractions reflect individual histopathological features in interstitial pneumonia.
candidates.abstract: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cellular analysis is an adjunctive diagnostic tool in interstitial pneumonia (IP), yet its relationship with individual histopathological features remains unclear. We retrospectively compared BALF cellular fractions with 24 histopathological features in 67 IP patients who underwent BALF and surgical lung biopsy at a single center (2005-2020). False discovery rate correction was applied (q < 0.05), followed by multivariable logistic regression and Kaplan-Meier analysis. BALF lymphocyte proportion was negatively associated with fibroblastic foci (13.0% vs 29.0%, q = 0.002) and positively with bronchiolitis (q = 0.029), intraluminal organization (q = 0.002), and epithelioid cell granulomas (q = 0.012). On multivariable analysis, fibroblastic foci were independently associated with a lower likelihood of BALF lymphocytosis (odds ratio 0.23, p = 0.018), and this association persisted after exclusion of patients with a usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) or probable UIP pattern and of patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Intraluminal lymphocyte proliferation was also associated with BALF lymphocytosis, although this estimate was based on few patients. Patients with fibroblastic foci had poorer survival (p = 0.003), whereas survival did not differ when patients were stratified by BALF lymphocyte proportion. ROC analysis identified a BALF lymphocyte cutoff of 18.5% for the presence of fibroblastic foci (AUC 0.76), and adding BALF lymphocyte proportion to the high-resolution computed tomography pattern improved discrimination of fibroblastic foci (AUC 0.847 versus 0.686). Neutrophil and eosinophil proportions showed no significant associations after correction. BALF lymphocyte proportion is associated with several histopathological features in IP, most strongly with fibroblastic foci, and may provide complementary information where surgical lung biopsy is not feasible.

candidates.title: Glycolysis in pulmonary fibrosis: From drivers to therapeutic opportunities (Review).
candidates.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a chronic and progressive interstitial lung disease with a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options. Current antifibrotic therapies only slow disease progression, underscoring an urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies. In recent years, metabolic reprogramming, notably the shift towards aerobic glycolysis (the Warburg effect), has emerged as a key driver of PF pathogenesis. This review comprehensively examines the central role of glycolysis in fueling the fibrotic cascade. It summarizes the major risk factors and fundamental pathogenic mechanisms of PF. The review then delves into the molecular mechanisms by which profibrotic signals, such as TGF‑β1, remodel cellular metabolism. The upregulation and pathogenic roles of critical glycolytic nodes are detailed‑including glucose transporters, hexokinase 2, phosphofructokinase‑2/fructose‑2,6‑bisphosphatase 3, pyruvate kinase M2 and lactate dehydrogenase A‑in activated fibroblasts, injured epithelial cells and pro‑fibrotic immune cells. Furthermore, the interplay between glycolysis and key signaling pathways (TGF‑β1, hypoxia‑inducible factor‑1α, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Hippo, AMP‑activated protein kinase and sirtuins) that form feed‑forward loops to sustain the fibrotic process is discussed. Furthermore, therapeutic strategies targeting glycolytic enzymes and upstream metabolic checkpoints are highlighted, summarizing preclinical evidence for small‑molecule inhibitors and non‑coding RNAs as emerging regulators of glycolytic reprogramming. By consolidating current knowledge on glycolysis‑centric metabolic underpinnings of PF, this review underscores the promise of metabolism‑based interventions and discusses challenges for translating these findings into effective therapies.

candidates.title: Pathological regulatory roles of lysine acylation modifications in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Review).
candidates.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic, progressive and fatal interstitial lung disease pathologically defined by progressive fibrosing remodeling of the pulmonary interstitium and irreversible destruction of normal alveolar architecture. IPF has a complex pathogenesis involving three consecutive stages: Initial alveolitis, chronic fibrosis and end‑stage lung tissue destruction. Metabolic reprogramming is considered a key pathological feature throughout the disease process. Changes in the availability of intracellular metabolites caused by metabolic reprogramming may further influence the dynamic balance of acetylation modifications, thereby linking metabolic dysregulation to the fibrotic phenotype. However, its relationship with key pathological regulatory networks remains to be further elucidated. The present review summarizes seven acylation modifications in IPF, namely, lactylation, succinylation, acetylation, β‑hydroxybutyrylation, palmitoylation, citrullination and formylation, including their stage‑specific roles, crosstalk and therapeutic potential. The review further examines the links between different acylation modifications and metabolic reprogramming and fibrotic progression, identifies key regulatory nodes such as SIRT3 and establishes an integrated regulatory network of acylation modifications in IPF. By integrating the dynamic changes and crosstalk among distinct acylation modifications, the present review aims to advance our understanding of the metabolic‑acylation regulatory mechanisms underlying IPF and provide a theoretical basis for therapeutic approaches targeting acylation homeostasis.

candidates.title: Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy and Perioperative Complications Associated with Pulmonary Toxicity.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is widely used in multimodal cancer treatment and can improve surgical conditions and patient prognosis. However, NAC-related pulmonary toxicity may impair respiratory function and warrants attention during perioperative risk assessment.
METHODS: This narrative review summarizes evidence on chemotherapy-associated pulmonary toxicity, focusing on underlying mechanisms, clinical characteristics, diagnostic strategies, and perioperative anesthetic management. Direct clinical evidence from patients receiving NAC is distinguished from findings in other treatment settings and experimental models.
RESULTS: Several chemotherapeutic agents, including bleomycin, methotrexate, taxanes, gemcitabine, and cisplatin, as well as selected targeted therapies, have been associated with drug-induced lung injury, often presenting as interstitial lung disease. Clinical and experimental evidence implicates mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, immune-mediated injury, inflammatory activation, and alveolar-capillary barrier disruption. Advanced age, pre-existing lung disease, reduced diffusing capacity, metabolic abnormalities, smoking history, and multi-agent treatment may indicate increased susceptibility, although their relevance varies by drug and treatment setting. Evidence from broader perioperative settings and experimental models suggests that mechanical ventilation, excessive oxygen exposure, and surgical stress may aggravate existing pulmonary injury.
CONCLUSION: NAC-related pulmonary toxicity merits consideration in perioperative assessment, but direct evidence linking it to perioperative outcomes remains limited. Pulmonary function testing and clinically indicated imaging can inform individualized risk assessment. Lung-protective ventilation, appropriate oxygen therapy, individualized anesthetic management, and postoperative respiratory support draw largely on evidence from other populations; their effectiveness specifically in pati

candidates.title: Multimodal imaging and clinical evolution of an optic nerve head granuloma with prominent overlying vessels in ocular sarcoidosis: a case report and literature review.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcoidosis is a multisystem granulomatous disorder of unclear etiology, histopathologically characterized by noncaseating granulomas. Ocular involvement is among the most common extrapulmonary manifestations, whereas optic nerve involvement occurs in fewer than 5% of cases. Direct granulomatous infiltration of the optic nerve represents the rarest form of optic nerve involvement. We report a rare case of a sarcoidosis-associated optic nerve head granuloma with prominent overlying vessels and describe its multimodal imaging features, clinical course, and treatment response, with a review of the clinical spectrum of sarcoid optic nerve head granulomas reported in the English-language literature.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 31-year-old woman presented with floaters in the left eye. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes. Fundus examination of the left eye revealed a white elevated optic nerve head lesion with fine tortuous surface vessels, accompanied by vitreous inflammatory haze, retinal periphlebitis, and candle-wax drippings. Fundus fluorescein angiography demonstrated early filling of lesion-associated vessels with marked late leakage, and optical coherence tomography angiography detected abnormal flow signals corresponding to the lesion. Additionally, chest computed tomography revealed bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, and transbronchial lung biopsy demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and no definite necrosis. The overall findings supported the diagnosis of sarcoidosis. The lesion initially progressed after the patient declined corticosteroid therapy, but gradually regressed following systemic corticosteroid treatment, with parallel disappearance of the lesion-associated abnormal flow signals. At the final follow-up, the lesion had completely regressed, leaving only a thin gliotic membrane, while visual acuity remained 20/20 throughout the entire follow-up.
CONCLUSION: Although rare, sarcoid optic nerv

candidates.title: Pharmacological advances of alkaloids from Traditional Chinese Medicine against pulmonary fibrosis: focus on anti-inflammatory mechanisms.
candidates.journal: Journal of traditional Chinese medicine = Chung i tsa chih ying wen pan
candidates.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a fatal respiratory disease characterized by abnormal repair of the pulmonary interstitium and scar formation. Currently, only nintedanib and pirfenidone are approved for clinical use, but their efficacy is limited, and they have significant side effects. The sustained inflammatory microenvironment promotes fibroblast activation and collagen deposition via unresolved inflammation, representing a central pathological mechanism in PF progression. Therefore, anti-inflammatory effects are key in relieving and treating PF. Alkaloids derived from Chinese herbal medicine have become a new hotspot in anti-PF research because of their good anti-inflammatory properties and advantages in multitarget and multipathway approaches. This review elucidates that PF is triggered by multiple factors, such as genetics, the environment, drugs, and infection, and reveals the core mechanism of its pathogenesis from the perspective of the roles of various cell types involved in PF. In this review, we focus on the experimental efficacy and mechanisms of alkaloid drugs that mitigate pulmonary fibrosis through anti-inflammatory actions. We review the research progress of experimental models and signaling pathway regulatory mechanisms to provide a reference for subsequent research. Finally, this review analyzes the transformation bottlenecks faced by alkaloids when applied to PF, such as low active ingredient content, poor target selectivity, and insufficient toxicological and clinical data. Strategies such as structural optimization, nanodelivery, multiomics validation, and real-world research are proposed to overcome these challenges, providing a reference for the development of highly efficient and low-toxicity anti-PF drugs.

candidates.title: Bufei Huoxue capsules enhance lung function in pneumoconiosis: a multicenter, randomized clinical trial.
candidates.journal: Journal of traditional Chinese medicine = Chung i tsa chih ying wen pan
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To clarify the efficacy and safety of Bufei Huoxue (BFHX) capsules for the treatment of pneumoconiosis.
METHODS: This multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial enrolled patients with pneum-oconiosis from five centers between June 2020 and June 2023. Participants were randomized 1∶1 to receive oral BFHX capsules or matched placebo (4 capsules, thrice daily) for 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was the change from baseline in forced vital capacity percent predicted (FVC%) at 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included changes in forced expiratory volume in 1 s percent predicted (FEV1%), 6-min walk test (6MWT) distance, COPD assessment test (CAT) score, Modified British Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scale score, and serum biomarkers at weeks 8 and 24. Safety was assessed through adverse events and laboratory analyses. Efficacy was evaluated in both the full analysis set (FAS) and per-protocol set (PPS), with blinding maintained throughout the trial.
RESULTS: In total, 162 patients were included in the study. For the primary outcome, the change from baseline in FVC% at 24 weeks was significantly greater in BFHX group than placebo group [BFHX-placebo least squares (LS): 5.65 ± 2.01, 95% confidence interval (CI) (1.68, 9.62), P = 0.0056]. A significant difference of FVC% was also observed at week 8 [BFHX-placebo LS: 3.50 ± 1.72, 95% CI(0.11, 6.90), P = 0.0434]. Significant improvements in secondary outcomes were also observed at week 24, including FEV1% [BFHX-placebo LS: 5.33 ± 2.51, 95% CI(0.37, 10.3), P = 0.0352], 6MWT distance [BFHX-placebo LS: 22.7 ± 8.76, 95% CI(5.40, 40.1), P = 0.0105], CAT score [BFHX-placebo LS: －2.14 ± 0.85, 95% CI(－3.82, －0.46), P = 0.0130], and mMRC score [BFHX-placebo LS: －0.34 ± 0.10, 95% CI(－0.54, －0.13), P = 0.0014]. The mMRC score also showed improvement at week 8 [BFHX-placebo LS: －0.25 ± 0.11, 95% CI(－0.47, －0.02), P = 0.0308]. Results were consistent in both the per-protocol and full analysis sets. No

candidates.title: Analysis of Factors Associated With Interstitial Lung Disease in Treatment-Naïve Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients and Development of a Classification Nomogram.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) is a serious extra-articular manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and contributes substantially to morbidity and mortality. Early identification of RA-associated ILD (RA-ILD) remains challenging, and reliable biomarkers for risk stratification are lacking.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify cytokine-related factors associated with RA-ILD and to develop an exploratory classification model for assessing the presence of ILD in patients with newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve RA.
METHODS: A total of 66 newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve RA patients were enrolled, including individuals with and without ILD confirmed by high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT). All patients were disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD)-naïve and had not received glucocorticoids or biologics prior to enrollment. Plasma IL-22 concentration was measured by ELISA; other cytokines (IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17A, IFN-γ, and TNF-α) were quantified using a multiplex bead-based immunoassay. Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, and radiological findings were collected. Feature selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and Boruta algorithms, followed by multivariable logistic regression to identify independent factors associated with RA-ILD. A nomogram was constructed based on selected predictors, and its performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and cross-validation.
RESULTS: Patients with RA-ILD exhibited distinct cytokine profiles compared with those without ILD. Multivariable analysis identified age, smoking, lower mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC), higher plasma TNF-α levels and lower plasma IL-22 levels as independent factors associated with RA-ILD. The nomogram exhibited good discriminative performance, with a fivefold cross-validated AUC of 0.851 (95% CI: 0.755-0.947); the apparent AUC in the full sample was 0.

candidates.title: Pirfenidone reduces fine particulate matter-induced epithelial to mesenchymal transition in lung epithelial cells through regulating mitochondrial fission and autophagy.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epidemiological studies have shown that fine particulate matter (PM) is closely associated with increased morbidity and mortality from lung diseases. However, the mechanisms by which PM affects alveolar epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), such as mitochondrial dysfunction, remain unclear, and therapy options require further investigation.
METHODS: Human type II alveolar epithelial cells (A549 cells) were exposed to 100 µg/mL PM to investigate EMT induction. In an animal model, mice were exposed to PM via intratracheal injection to simulate air pollution exposure.
RESULTS: PM exposure reduced the expression of the epithelial marker E-cadherin while increasing the expression of mesenchymal markers vimentin, α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), and transforming growth factor β1 (TGF-β1). Furthermore, the expression of EMT-related transcription factors Snail and Slug was upregulated, accompanied by a morphological shift in A549 cells from cubic to spindle shapes and enhanced cell migration. PM also promoted mitochondrial fission and induced the accumulation of LC3B and p62 proteins. Treatment with the antifibrotic drug pirfenidone (PFD) effectively reduced PM-induced EMT-related protein expression and cell migration. These effects are achieved by reducing mitochondrial fission, increasing autophagosome accumulation, and related autophagic degradation. The lungs of PM-treated mice showed increased expression of EMT-related proteins, significant blood cell infiltration, and alveolar wall thickening. PFD treatment significantly improved these conditions and reduced collagen deposition.
CONCLUSION: PM induces increased mitochondrial fission and incomplete autophagy (characterized by autophagosome accumulation and impaired flux), leading to EMT. PFD treatment can also effectively reduce PM-induced EMT formation by modulating these pathways.

candidates.title: Diagnostic ambiguity and in-hospital mortality determinants: a decadal analysis of interstitial lung disease hospitalization trends in Ecuador (2015-2024).
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Interstitial Lung Diseases (ILDs) comprise a group of complex disorders characterized by pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis. ILDs represent a challenge in Latin America, yet nationwide longitudinal data remains fragmented. In Ecuador, the clinical landscape of ILD has been shaped by evolving diagnostic capabilities and systemic disruptions caused by recent public health emergencies. We investigated the decade-long evolution of ILD hospitalizations and mortality in Ecuador, examining how diagnostic precision-or the lack thereof-shapes patient survival.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 10,458 hospital discharges from 2015 to 2024 using the National Institute of Statistics and Censuses database. Cases were classified using ICD-10 codes: J84.1 (fibrosis), J84.8 (other specified), and J84.9 (unspecified). Age-standardized hospitalization and mortality rates were calculated. Multivariable logistic regression was utilized to identify independent predictors of in-hospital death, adjusting for sociodemographic factors, institutional settings, and ICD-10 classifications.
RESULTS: Analysis revealed a mean age-adjusted hospitalization rate of 6.16 per 100,000 inhabitants. Hospitalization rates exhibited a "U-shaped" trajectory, plummeting during the 2020 pandemic shock (3.52 per 100,000) before rebounding in 2022 (7.08 per 100,000). While population-wide mortality stabilized post-pandemic, individual risk of death per admission was statistically associated with temporal variations during 2022-2023 (aOR: 1.797; p = 0.001). Crucially, diagnostic ambiguity was independently associated with a higher likelihood of in-hospital mortality: patients coded as "unspecified" (J84.9) or "other specified" (J84.8) ILD faced significantly higher odds of death (aOR: 1.26 and 1.56, respectively) compared to those with established fibrosis. Furthermore, 27.2% of fatalities occurred within 72 h of admission, highlighting severe barriers to timely intervention. Rural mortal

candidates.title: [Age-period-cohort analysis of pneumoconiosis mortality in China based on the Global Burden of Disease Database 2021].
candidates.journal: Zhonghua lao dong wei sheng zhi ye bing za zhi = Zhonghua laodong weisheng zhiyebing zazhi = Chinese journal of industrial hygiene and occupational diseases
candidates.abstract: Objective: To assess the age, period, and cohort effects on pneumoconiosis mortality among population aged 15-94 years old in China from 1980 to 2021, and to predict the mortality trends over the next decade, thereby providing data support for the formulation of prevention and control strategies for pneumoconiosis. Methods: From May to September 2024, based on the Global Burden of Disease Database 2021 (GBD 2021), pneumoconiosis mortality data and related demographic data among the Chinese population aged 15-94 years from 1980 to 2021 were extracted. And the age-standardized mortality was calculated using the 2020 Seventh National Population Census as the standard population. Joinpoint regression analysis was applied to assess temporal trends in pneumoconiosis mortality. The age-period-cohort model was used to estimate age, period, and cohort effects. Pearson correlation analysis was performed to examine the associations between age-standardized mortality with gross domestic product, per capita disposable income, per capita health expenditure, and work-related injury insurance fund expenditure. Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) Model and Grey Model[GM (1, 1) ] were constructed to predict the age-standardized mortalities of pneumoconiosis from 2022 to 2031, and model performance was evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) . Results: From 1980 to 2021, the age-standardized mortalities of pneumoconiosis in China showed an overall decreasing trend, with an average annual percent change (AAPC) of -2.21% (P<0.001). Joinpoint regression identified four statistically significant turning points in 1992, 1999, 2004, and 2007. The age-period-cohort model indicated that mortality risk of pneumoconiosis increased with age, peaking in the 85-89 years age group (effect coefficient=2.155, P<0.001). The period effects of 1987-1991, 1997-2001, 2002-2006, 2007-2011 and 2012-2016 were statistically significant (P<0.05). The coh

candidates.title: Serum KL-6 Levels at Acute Exacerbation in Patients With Interstitial Lung Disease.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Serum KL-6 is widely used to monitor interstitial lung disease (ILD), but its short-term behavior around acute exacerbation (AE) and its prognostic value at AE onset remain unclear. This study evaluated serial KL-6 changes before AE and their association with survival.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis or progressive pulmonary fibrosis who underwent KL-6 measurement at two hospitals between May 2015 and June 2025. KL-6 at AE onset was compared with values one month earlier, the highest value during the preceding year, and maximum values in patients without AE. Associations with post-AE survival were assessed.
RESULTS: Among 409 patients with ILD, KL-6 was measured at onset in 109 AE episodes among 97 patients; 142 patients without AE had at least one measurement. Median KL-6 at AE onset was higher than the median maximum value in patients without AE (1,100 vs. 690 U/ml, p=0.0001). However, paired analyses showed no significant difference between KL-6 at AE onset and the value one month earlier (n=32, p=0.092) or the highest value during the preceding year (n=58, p=0.145). KL-6 at AE onset did not differ among patients who died within 30 days, died between 30 and 90 days, or survived beyond 90 days (p=0.4307). A high KL-6 level (≥1,100 U/ml) was not associated with survival.
CONCLUSION: Although KL-6 levels were higher in patients with interstitial lung disease experiencing AE compared to patients without AE, they did not consistently increase immediately before AE and had limited prognostic value at AE onset.

candidates.title: [Reference guide for the clinical management of adult Langerhans cell histiocytosis (key points from the first edition, 2025)].
candidates.journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology
candidates.abstract: According to the registry of the Japanese Society of Hematology, adult histiocytic neoplasms are extremely rare, with approximately 40 cases reported annually, and the most common among them is Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH). Lesions may involve multiple organs, including bone, skin, lung, the central nervous system, and the endocrine system. Without a hematology perspective, the neoplastic nature of LCH may not be apparent, resulting in missed diagnoses. Central diabetes insipidus, anterior pituitary dysfunction, and LCH-associated neurodegeneration, once developed, often result in irreversible impairment. Because delayed therapeutic intervention can result in permanent organ damage, it is essential for hematologists to understand the "minimum initial management" required to protect patient outcomes. This review summarizes the key points of diagnosis and initial management in adult LCH based on the first edition of the Adult LCH Clinical Reference Guide (2025).

candidates.title: Indirect immunofluorescence in ANCA testing: past achievements, current indications, and future perspectives.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) are important biomarkers for the diagnosis of ANCA-associated vasculitis. ANCA are, however, also detected in many other inflammatory disorders. ANCA, as detected by IIF, has revolutionized the diagnostic process of small-vessel vasculitis, whereas its role in other autoimmune disorders has been supportive.
AREAS COVERED: A comprehensive review of the available literature was conducted using PubMed to identify English-language studies on ANCA testing published up to June 2026. The search included studies evaluating ANCA testing in different forms of vasculitis, connective tissue diseases, inflammatory bowel disease, autoimmune hepatitis, and other relevant diseases. Case series were included, whereas individual case reports were excluded. The literature was prioritized according to its relevance to the scope and objectives of this review.
EXPERT OPINION: Whereas the development of high-quality immunoassays for PR3-ANCA and MPO-ANCA has replaced the IIF method as a screening test for a diagnosis of AAV, there are several conditions in which the IIF test is still valuable. This is true for patients who are suspected of drug-induced vasculitis, cocaine abuse, and/or endocarditis. Furthermore, in patients with connective tissue disorders, autoimmune liver diseases, inflammatory bowel disease, and some other diseases, IIF testing is valuable in certain circumstances as well.

candidates.title: An Elusive Diagnosis of Strongyloides Infection Masquerading as Daptomycin-Induced Eosinophilic Pneumonitis.
candidates.abstract: Daptomycin-induced eosinophilic pneumonitis, characterized by peripheral eosinophilia, bilateral pulmonary infiltrates and respiratory symptoms, is a recognized adverse drug effect. However, these findings overlap significantly with pulmonary strongyloidiasis, in which transpulmonary larval migration provokes a similar eosinophil-rich inflammatory response. Failure to distinguish between these entities carries serious consequences, as untreated Strongyloides infection can progress to hyperinfection syndrome with high mortality. We describe a middle-aged male with alcoholic liver cirrhosis who developed peripheral eosinophilia, bilateral pulmonary nodules, migratory consolidative opacities, and pleural effusions while receiving daptomycin for polymicrobial bacteremia. The findings were initially attributed to daptomycin-induced eosinophilic pneumonitis, and the drug was discontinued. However, given clinical suspicion for a parasitic etiology, Strongyloides testing was pursued. Stool ova-and-parasite examination and bronchoalveolar lavage were both negative; however, Strongyloides serology returned positive, confirming the diagnosis. The patient improved both clinically and radiographically following treatment with ivermectin and albendazole. The negative stool and bronchoalveolar lavage results further underscore the suboptimal sensitivity of conventional diagnostic methods and the essential role of serologic testing. Clinicians evaluating eosinophilia with pulmonary infiltrates in patients receiving daptomycin should systematically consider parasitic etiologies, including Strongyloides serology, before attributing findings solely to a drug-related cause.

candidates.title: Targeted DNA Sequencing Reveals Distinct Rare-Variant Profiles in Pulmonary Hypertension Associated with Chronic Lung Diseases.
candidates.abstract: The mechanisms underlying the development and severity of pulmonary hypertension (PH) in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and interstitial lung disease (ILD) remain poorly understood. To investigate the contribution of genetic factors, we performed targeted sequencing of PH-related genes in 63 patients with COPD, 51 with ILD, and 38 with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH), stratifying COPD and ILD patients according to PH severity, assessed by right heart catheterisation. Patients with ILD-associated PH harboured fewer genetic variants than those without PH, whereas an opposite trend was observed in COPD-associated PH. Variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in PAH-associated genes (BMPR2, BMPR1B) were identified in two out of 28 patients with severe COPD-PH and in one with nonsevere ILD-PH (SMAD9). VUS in extracellular matrix-related genes (THBS1, LOXL2) were also identified in four patients with severe COPD-PH, and in inflammatory-related genes (TNFAIP6) in two patients with ILD-PH. Pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in PAH-associated genes were exclusive to IPAH. We conclude that there is limited genetic overlap between COPD-PH and ILD-PH, with a stronger genetic contribution to PH in COPD, particularly in its severe form, where a subset of patients carries VUS in PAH-associated genes or genes involved in vascular remodelling.

candidates.title: Mechanisms and Clinical Translational Prospects of the Microbiota-Gut-Lung Axis in Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease.
candidates.abstract: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD) is one of the most severe pulmonary complications of connective tissue diseases, featuring rapid progression and heterogeneous prognosis. Early recognition and prognostic prediction remain substantial clinical challenges. Accumulating evidence indicates that the microbiota-gut-lung axis participates in key pathological cascades, including autoimmune dysregulation, chronic inflammatory activation, and tissue fibrotic remodeling, which provides new insights into the pathogenesis of autoimmune-mediated lung diseases. This review systematically summarizes regulatory mechanisms of CTD-ILD involving gut dysbiosis, intestinal mucosal barrier impairment, disturbed metabolism of short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and tryptophan, and systemic immune imbalance. We further compare evidence and pathological discrepancies of gut-lung-axis disturbance across CTD subtypes: systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD), rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease (RA-ILD), systemic lupus erythematosus-associated interstitial lung disease (SLE-ILD), idiopathic inflammatory myopathy interstitial lung disease (IIM-ILD), and primary Sjögren's syndrome-associated interstitial lung disease (pSS-ILD). We also highlight the translational potential of gut-lung axis-related biomarkers for screening and assessment, summarize targeted interventions and integrated Chinese-Western therapeutic regimens, and pinpoint major evidence gaps and methodological limitations. This review refines the inter-organ regulatory framework of CTD-ILD and offers scientific references for mechanistic investigation, precise clinical evaluation, and novel therapeutic development.

candidates.title: Updates on the Translational Value of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis Models Across Species: Deeper Insights Through Comparative Pathology.
candidates.abstract: Over the past few decades, advances in comparative pathology have strengthened the potential translational value of animal models of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF). The integration of human-relevant diagnostic biomarkers into preclinical studies, such as advanced imaging techniques and standardized histopathological methods, has improved the comparability of experimental findings with human disease. Naturally occurring fibrotic lung diseases in some breeds of companion dogs and cats and induced disease models in laboratory rodents show varying degrees of similarity to human IPF. They represent valuable comparative medicine tools to better understand disease mechanisms and test new therapies, each with advantages and limitations. Critically evaluating their complementarity is essential for gaining reliable insights into disease processes through preclinical animal studies and for developing effective treatments. This comprehensive review aims to update current knowledge of these animal models of IPF, focusing on comparative pathology, imaging, and histological features and evaluating their respective strengths, limitations, and translational relevance within the conceptual framework of "One Health, One Medicine, One Pathology". By exploiting convergent pathophysiological processes across species, this interdisciplinary collaborative paradigm aims to promote the effective use of model organisms in biomedical research and foster mutual benefits for both humans and animals.

candidates.title: Mesenchymal Stromal Cells for Heart Diseases: Current Perspective and Future Directions.
candidates.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide and continue to impose a substantial clinical burden despite major advances in pharmacological and interventional therapies. Because the adult myocardium has limited regenerative capacity, irreversible cardiomyocyte loss frequently leads to adverse remodeling and progressive heart failure (HF). Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are among the most extensively studied cell therapies for cardiac repair because of their immunomodulatory, pro-angiogenic, anti-inflammatory, and anti-fibrotic effects, mediated predominantly through paracrine signaling. This review summarizes the current evidence for MSC-based therapy in ischemic heart disease (IHD), coronary and microvascular disorders, myocardial infarction, HF, myocarditis, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and valvular heart disease (VHD). We discuss MSC sources, preclinical and clinical evidence, manufacturing and dosing, delivery routes, biomaterial-assisted transplantation, preconditioning, genetic modification, and imaging for cell tracking and treatment monitoring. Although MSC therapy has shown a favorable safety profile and regenerative potential, clinical efficacy remains variable because of limited cell survival, poor myocardial retention, and heterogeneous treatment protocols. Further optimization of manufacturing, delivery, and patient selection, together with well-designed randomized trials, is required to establish standardized protocols and support clinical translation.

candidates.title: miR-146b-5p Suppresses Btg2 to Promote Fibroblast Proliferation and Is Associated with Prrx2 and Myh10.
candidates.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis is a chronic progressive lung disease characterized by abnormal proliferation and activation of fibroblasts. However, the regulatory mechanisms of miRNAs and their target genes on fibroblast proliferation during silicosis (silica-induced pulmonary fibrosis) remain incompletely understood. A mouse silicosis model was established by dynamic dust inhalation, and lung tissues were collected at 7, 14, 28, and 56 days after dust exposure, followed by multi-time-point miRNA sequencing and transcriptome sequencing. Using integrated omics, bioinformatics analysis, and molecular interaction validation, the key miRNAs and their target genes regulating fibroblast proliferation were screened and verified. The results showed that time-series clustering and H&E staining confirmed successful modeling of the transition from acute inflammation to chronic fibrosis induced by SiO2. Differentially expressed miR-146b-5p during SiO2 stress may affect the cell cycle of fibroblasts by regulating Btg2. Mechanistically, IP-MS combined with Co-IP identified interactions between Btg2 and Prrx2 or Myh10, suggesting their potential involvement in this regulatory process. These findings provide new experimental evidence for the molecular mechanisms of silica-induced pulmonary fibrosis in a mouse model, and may offer insights for understanding the pathogenesis of human silicosis.

candidates.title: Non-Invasive Distal Airway Proteomics by Particles in Exhaled Air (PExA) Sampling Demonstrates Shared Proteomic Features with Matched Bronchoalveolar Lavage.
candidates.abstract: Repeated molecular sampling of the distal airways is constrained by the invasive nature of bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL), limiting its use in healthy control populations, longitudinal studies, clinical trials and occupational screening. Particles in exhaled air (PExA) sampling offers a non-invasive approach to distal-airway sampling, although whether it captures the same proteins and relative protein abundance as BAL has not been established. We performed the first proof-of-principle high-dimensional proteomic comparison of matched BAL and PExA samples collected from three individuals with silicosis using the SomaScan 11K platform. Within individuals, PExA and BAL shared a substantial subset of detectable proteins and showed similar cross-protein signal patterns, with Pearson correlation coefficients ranging from 0.48 to 0.71. Analytes recurrently detected across all three PExA samples were strongly enriched among those consistently detected in BAL and included pulmonary surfactant proteins and mediators associated with epithelial injury, alveolar macrophage function, inflammation and fibrosis. The PExA findings also showed substantial overlap with an independent published PExA-only proteomic dataset. These proof-of-principle findings show that non-invasive PExA sampling can capture a biologically meaningful subset of the matched BAL proteome. PExA may therefore offer a practical approach for repeated molecular profiling of the distal airways and warrants further evaluation for respiratory biomarker discovery and disease monitoring.

candidates.title: Isolated necrotizing scleritis revealing silent pulmonary granulomatosis with polyangiitis: A case report of rare diagnostic clue.
candidates.abstract:
RATIONALE: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) is a rare, life-threatening vasculitis characterized by necrotizing granulomatous inflammation. Isolated necrotizing anterior scleritis as the sole initial manifestation is distinctly rare. The presence of a clinically silent pulmonary mass without ear, nose, and throat or renal involvement makes this presentation exceptional and diagnostically challenging.
PATIENT CONCERNS: A 31-year-old man presented with recurrent unilateral necrotizing anterior scleritis resistant to corticosteroids and immunosuppressants, without systemic symptoms.
DIAGNOSES: This single-patient case report, prepared in accordance with CAse REport guidelines, revealed mildly elevated anti-proteinase 3 antibodies (25 AU/mL) in laboratory tests. Chest computed tomography unexpectedly showed a 5-cm solitary pulmonary mass. Histopathology demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and vasculitis, confirming GPA.
INTERVENTIONS: The patient was treated with pulsed intravenous methylprednisolone followed by monthly cyclophosphamide, then transitioned to rituximab maintenance therapy.
OUTCOMES: He achieved marked improvement in ocular inflammation and visual function, with no new systemic manifestations during follow-up.
LESSONS: This case illustrates a rare diagnostic pathway in which isolated, treatment-resistant necrotizing scleritis led to the detection of clinically silent pulmonary GPA. It highlights the importance of considering systemic vasculitis in atypical or refractory scleritis and underscores the critical role of tissue biopsy when serologic findings are mild or nonspecific. Furthermore, this first documented Middle Eastern case adds educational value for ophthalmologists and rheumatologists, illustrating that early multidisciplinary evaluation and timely rituximab therapy can prevent irreversible ocular damage and systemic progression.

candidates.title: Anti-GBM/ANCA double-positive crescentic nephritis in an elderly patient presenting with heart failure-like symptoms: A case report.
candidates.abstract:
RATIONALE: Anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) antibody disease and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis represent the 2 leading causes of rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN). The coexistence of these conditions is rare, typically progresses rapidly, and has a poor prognosis. Elderly patients often present with nonspecific systemic symptoms, increasing the likelihood of misdiagnosis and treatment delay.
PATIENT CONCERNS: A 74-year-old woman presented with a one-month history of intermittent shortness of breath, worsening progressively over ten days, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She denied hemoptysis, gross hematuria, rash, or arthralgia.
DIAGNOSES: Initial assessment suggested heart failure. However, laboratory results revealed severe renal impairment (creatinine: 1025.99 μmol/L). Renal biopsy demonstrated crescent formation in over 80% of glomeruli, with immunofluorescence showing linear immunoglobulin G deposits along glomerular capillary loops. Serological testing revealed markedly elevated anti-GBM antibody (>400 RU/mL) and MPO-ANCA (108.4 RU/mL) levels, together with a perinuclear ANCA (P-ANCA) pattern on indirect immunofluorescence, supporting the diagnosis of anti-GBM glomerulonephritis with concomitant MPO-ANCA positivity.
INTERVENTIONS: Treatment included methylprednisolone pulse therapy, cyclophosphamide, and 3 plasma exchange sessions. Additional supportive measures comprised hemodialysis, antihypertensive therapy, and management of renal anemia.
OUTCOMES: Although the patient's uremic symptoms improved markedly, renal function did not recover. She was discharged on hemodialysis and was subsequently transitioned to maintenance peritoneal dialysis. By January 2026, the anti-GBM antibody level had decreased markedly to 4.27 RU/mL, below the positive cutoff, and MPO-ANCA had also become negative. candidates.title: Serum SPP1 levels are associated with disease severity and 1-year mortality in primary Sjögren's syndrome-associated interstitial lung disease.
candidates.abstract: Clinical significance of serum secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1) in primary Sjögren's syndrome-associated interstitial lung disease (pSS-ILD) remains unclear. In this study, we analyzed the GSE47460 lung tissue expression profile to validate SPP1 upregulation in ILD and performed GSEA to explore the potential mechanisms. A retrospective clinical cohort of 88 pSS-ILD patients and 40 healthy controls (HC) was established, with patients stratified into stable disease (SD, n=60) and acute exacerbation (AE, n=28). Serum SPP1 levels were measured by ELISA, and correlations with pulmonary function were analyzed. ROC curves, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and Cox regression models were used to evaluate its predictive value. SPP1 was upregulated in ILD lung tissues, with GSEA revealing enrichment of nucleotide metabolism in the high-expression group. Serum SPP1 levels were significantly elevated in pSS-ILD patients compared to HCs [37.69 (27.25-73.42) vs. 20.11 (15.68-23.72) ng/mL, P<0.001], and further increased in the AE group [85.90 (48.67-122.45) vs. 31.45 (25.87-42.02) ng/mL, P<0.001]. SPP1 levels correlated negatively with DLCO% predicted (r = -0.426, P<0.01, q = 0.013). The AUC for distinguishing AE was 0.891, and for predicting 1-year mortality was 0.712. Using a cut-off of 40.41 ng/mL, higher SPP1 levels were associated with worse survival (P = 0.002), and multivariate Cox regression identified SPP1 as an independent risk factor for 1-year mortality (HR = 1.016, 95% CI: 1.006-1.025, P = 0.001). Collectively, these clinical findings demonstrate that serum SPP1 levels correlate with disease severity and may serve as a predictor of poor prognosis in pSS-ILD.

candidates.title: [Immunophenotype of RF-IgA-positive patients with primary Sjögren syndrome without concomitant rheumatoid arthritis: Dissociation between B-cell activation and inflammatory cytokine levels].
candidates.journal: Zhong nan da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Central South University. Medical sciences
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Primary Sjögren syndrome (pSS) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by excessive B-cell activation. Rheumatoid factor (RF) is frequently positive in patients with pSS; however, the clinical significance of RF subtypes, particularly immunoglobulin (Ig) A rheumatoid factor (RF-IgA), remains unclear, and previous studies have often not strictly excluded patients with concomitant rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This study aims to investigate the immunophenotypic characteristics of RF-IgA-positive patients with pSS without concomitant RA and to analyze the relationship between RF-IgA and disease activity.
METHODS: A total of 153 patients with pSS who presented to the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, the Second Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, between January 2021 and December 2025 were included, comprising 30 RF-IgA-positive patients and 123 RF-IgA-negative patients. Flow cytometry was used to determine the proportions of peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets, including CD19⁺ B cells, CD4⁺ T cells, CD8⁺ T cells, and CD16⁺CD56⁺ natural killer (NK) cells. Serum levels of interleukin (IL)-6, IL-10, IL-17A, interferon (IFN)-γ, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, and IL-1β were measured using a cytometric bead array. Immunoglobulin and complement levels were measured by immunoturbidimetry. Anti-Sjögren syndrome-related antigen A (SSA)/60 kD, anti-SSA/52 kD, and anti-Sjögren syndrome-related antigen B (SSB)/La antibodies were detected by indirect immunofluorescence. Disease activity was assessed using the European League Against Rheumatism Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI), and the incidences of complications were compared between the 2 groups. Spearman correlation analysis was used to evaluate the correlations of RF-IgA levels with the percentage of CD19⁺ B cells and serum IgA and IgG levels in the RF-IgA-positive group.
RESULTS: The percentage of CD19⁺ B cells was significantly higher in the RF-IgA

candidates.title: Targeting protective renin-angiotensin system pathways in pulmonary emphysema: Preclinical evidence for resolving inflammation and restoring lung homeostasis.
candidates.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide and still lacks effective disease-modifying therapies. Current pharmacological treatments primarily alleviate symptoms and reduce exacerbations, but have limited ability to prevent progressive lung destruction or promote tissue repair. Increasing evidence indicates that beyond the classical cardiovascular functions of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS), it additionally plays a central role in regulating pulmonary inflammation, oxidative stress, extracellular matrix remodelling, cellular senescence and endogenous repair mechanisms. Experimental studies have shown that both pharmacological inhibition of the ACE/Ang II/AT1 axis and activation of the protective AT2 receptor and ACE2/Ang-(1-7)/Mas pathways attenuate multiple pathological processes involved in COPD progression. In this review, we comprehensively discuss the current preclinical evidence supporting pharmacological manipulation of the RAS in experimental models of pulmonary emphysema, highlighting the anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-fibrotic, pro-resolutive and regenerative mechanisms associated with these therapeutic strategies. We further discuss emerging evidence indicating that activation of protective RAS pathways not only suppresses inflammation, but also promotes tissue repair through modulating autophagy, inflammasome activation, cellular senescence and endogenous regenerative signalling. These findings collectively position protective RAS modulation as a promising disease-modifying strategy for COPD and provide a strong rationale for future translational and clinical studies aimed at restoring pulmonary homeostasis.

candidates.title: Differential Diagnosis of Early-Stage Pulmonary Sarcoidosis With Normal Serum Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Activity Using Peripheral Blood Indicators: Machine Learning Models Development and Validation.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early-stage pulmonary sarcoidosis with serum angiotensin-converting enzyme (sACE) activity within the normal range is difficult to distinguish from other pulmonary diseases with similar radiographic characteristics.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML)-based diagnostic models for differentiating early-stage pulmonary sarcoidosis using indices from routine peripheral blood tests.
METHODS: From May 2014 to May 2021, a total of 1142 patients with atypical initial pulmonary imaging findings were enrolled. After applying strict inclusion and exclusion criteria, 420 cases were divided into sarcoidosis and nonsarcoidosis groups (including mediastinal lymph node tuberculosis [MLNT], lung cancer, lymphoma, and pneumoconiosis), then stratified by sex and randomly split (7:3) into training and validation sets. Features were selected via univariate analysis (P<.10), the Boruta algorithm, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression. Six ML algorithms-logistic regression (LR), random forest, support vector machine (SVM), extreme gradient boosting, k‑nearest neighbor, and naïve Bayes-were compared using area under the curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, Brier score, calibration assessment, and decision curve analysis. Shapley Additive Explanations was used for interpretability. The selected models were deployed as an interactive Shiny web application.
RESULTS: After stratification, the male group comprised 224 cases (sarcoidosis n=42; MLNT: n=39; lung cancer: n=106; lymphoma: n=9; pneumoconiosis: n=28), and the female group comprised 196 cases (sarcoidosis: n=100; MLNT: n=39; lung cancer: n=49; lymphoma: n=4; pneumoconiosis: n=4). Models were selected based on comprehensive evaluation of multiple performance metrics, including AUC, accuracy, specificity, F1-score, and Brier score. candidates.title: Translation and cross-cultural adaptation of the Palliative Care Knowledge Scale (PaCKS) into European Portuguese and its measurement properties in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and interstitial lung diseases.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: No instruments exist to assess palliative care knowledge among Portuguese with chronic respiratory diseases.
AIM: To translate and cross-culturally adapt the Palliative Care Knowledge Scale (PaCKS) into European Portuguese and explore its measurement properties in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and interstitial lung diseases (ILD).
METHODS: Translation and cross-cultural adaptation procedures were followed. Internal consistency (Cronbach's α); test-retest reliability [intraclass correlation coefficient with 95% confidence interval (ICC2,1 [95% CI]), standard error of measurement (SEM/SEM%), minimal detectable change at 95% confidence level (MDC95/MDC%) and Bland-Altman method]; floor/ceiling effects; and, construct validity [convergent/divergent, correlation (Spearman's - rs) with the Bristol COPD Knowledge Questionnaire (BCKQ)/modified Medical Research Council dyspnoea questionnaire/lung function] were evaluated.
RESULTS: Two forward translations/back-translations were conducted. Five experts approved the prefinal version. Cognitive debriefing involved 12 participants. Measurement properties were analysed in 102 people with COPD and 54 with ILD (73.1% male; 67.6 ± 10.0 years). PaCKS score was 11.0 [9.0-12.0] and 10.0 [8.8-11.0] in COPD and ILD, respectively. Internal consistency was acceptable (αCOPD = 0.76; αILD = 0.80). The test-retest reliability was good in COPD (ICC2,1 0.84 [0.77-0.89]) and ranged from good to excellent in ILD (ICC2,1 0.89 [0.78-0.94]). SEM/SEM% and MDC95/MDC% were 1.0/9.6% and 2.8/26.6%, and 1.0/10.1% and 2.7/28.0% in COPD and ILD, respectively. The Bland-Altman method did not suggest systematic bias, with 95% limits of agreement of approximately ±3.0. No floor/ceiling effects were observed, except for a ceiling effect in COPD (20.6%). The PaCKS/BCKQ correlation was significant, positive and moderate (rs = 0.40, p < 0.001) in COPD. Other correlations were non-significant and ranged from negligible to weak.

candidates.title: Efficacy and Safety of Inhaled Treprostinil in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic interstitial lung disease with high morbidity and mortality. Inhaled treprostinil showed pulmonary vascular and lung-function signals in pulmonary hypertension associated with Interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and was subsequently tested in IPF trials.
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the efficacy and safety of inhaled treprostinil in adults with IPF.
METHODS: PubMed, Google Scholar and the Cochrane Library/CENTRAL were searched for records published from January 2000 to 2026. A random-effects meta-analysis used the DerSimonian-Laird tau squared and inverse-variance weighting methods. Continuous outcomes were pooled as generic inverse-variance effects from reported estimates and 95% confidence intervals. Hazard ratios were pooled on the log scale. Safety outcomes were pooled as risk ratios from event counts.
RESULTS: The searches identified 1552 records. After deduplication, 379 records were screened and 85 full-text reports were assessed. Eleven reports were included in the systematic review. TETON-1 and TETON-2 were the two direct-IPF randomized trials within the coordinated TETON program eligible for primary meta-analysis. Inhaled treprostinil improved absolute forced vital capacity (FVC) change at 52 weeks compared with placebo (MD 111.28 mL, 95% CI 77.61 to 144.95, p < 0.001; I squared 8.5%). Clinical worsening was reduced (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.57 to 0.84, p < 0.001; I squared 0.0%). Acute exacerbation was lower in pooled analysis (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.30 to 0.91, p = 0.022), while all-cause mortality did not differ significantly (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.47 to 1.05, p = 0.086). Adverse-event discontinuation, cough and headache were more frequent with treprostinil.
CONCLUSIONS: In direct IPF randomized evidence, inhaled treprostinil preserved lung function and reduced clinical worsening at 52 weeks.

candidates.title: Real-World Impact of Mepolizumab in COPD in a US Commercial and Medicare Claims Database.
candidates.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Mepolizumab reduces exacerbations in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and was recently approved in the United States (US) for the add-on maintenance treatment of adult patients with inadequately controlled COPD and an eosinophilic phenotype. Given the limited real-world data on mepolizumab effectiveness in COPD, this study assessed its real-world impact in patients with COPD, prior to US regulatory approval of mepolizumab for COPD.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective, longitudinal analysis from the US Komodo Research claims database (January 2016-June 2024). The first observed mepolizumab claim was defined as the index date. All patients were aged ≥40 years on index date, had ≥2 COPD diagnosis claims in the 12 months pre-index (baseline period) or on index date, and required ≥2 pharmacy/medical claims for mepolizumab from index date to end of observation. Patients with ≥2 asthma diagnosis claims or ≥1 diagnosis claim(s) for cystic fibrosis, lung cancer, interstitial lung disease, or α-1 antitrypsin deficiency during the baseline period or on index date were excluded. Outcomes assessed during the 12 months post- versus 12 months pre-mepolizumab initiation included annualized exacerbation rates, oral corticosteroid (OCS) use, and COPD-related healthcare resource utilization (HCRU).
RESULTS: Descriptive analyses included 693 mepolizumab initiators (58% Medicare), while pre-post analyses included 470 patients with 12 months of pre- and post-initiation data. Annualized rate of moderate/severe exacerbations decreased by 41% (P<0.001) post- versus pre-mepolizumab. Relative reductions of 26% and 33% in rates of OCS dispensing and bursts were observed (P<0.001), and relative reductions of 22-37% in COPD-related HCRU including hospitalizations (P=0.038), emergency department visits (P<0.001), and outpatient visits (P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: In this real-world retrospective study of US patients with COPD, initiation of mepolizumab was associated

candidates.title: Perioperative Antifibrotic Treatment and Early Postoperative Outcomes in Patients With Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis Undergoing Lung Cancer Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
candidates.abstract: Patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) undergoing lung cancer surgery are at high risk of acute exacerbation of IPF (AE-IPF), which is associated with high mortality. Although antifibrotic therapy (AFT) has been proposed as a preventive strategy, evidence remains limited and heterogeneous, particularly regarding early postoperative outcomes. We systematically searched major databases, including PubMed and Ichushi-Web, through August 2025 to evaluate perioperative AFT in patients with IPF undergoing surgery. Eligible studies reported postoperative AE-IPF or mortality within 30-90 days. Risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using common- and random-effects models. Five retrospective cohort studies predominantly evaluating pirfenidone were included. AFT was associated with a lower incidence of postoperative AE-IPF both within 30 days (RR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.07-0.76; I2 = 0%) and 90 days (RR, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.09-0.57; I2 = 0%). AFT was associated with lower mortality at 30 days (RR, 0.12; 95% CI, 0.02-0.91; I2 = 0%) and 90 days (RR, 0.13; 95% CI, 0.02-0.76; I2 = 0%). Sensitivity analyses, including a nationwide database study, supported the association, although the effect was attenuated. Evidence for nintedanib was limited to a small case series. Perioperative AFT, particularly with pirfenidone, was associated with lower rates of AE-IPF and mortality, including within 30 days post-lung cancer surgery. These findings underscore the clinical relevance of early postoperative outcomes and support further prospective studies to clarify the role of perioperative AFT.

candidates.title: Role of gut microbiota in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies: insights from 16S rRNA sequencing and cluster analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The disturbed gut microbiota has been found involved in the immunopathogenesis of various autoimmune diseases (AIDs). However, the clinical and pathogenic role of gut microbiota in Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs) remains unclear. This study employs 16 S rRNA gene sequencing combined with unsupervised cluster analysis to explore the alterations in gut micro-biota in IIMs patients, aiming to elucidate the association between gut microbial composition and the clinical manifestations of IIMs.
RESULTS: Analysis of fecal samples from 77 IIMs patients and 32 healthy controls revealed significant reductions in both the richness and diversity of the gut bacterial community in the IIM group. IIMs patients exhibited a significantly elevated microbial dysbiosis index (MDI) and a decreased abundance of Bacteroidetes. Clustering analysis classified IIMs patients into three distinct microbiota-based clusters, each with unique bacterial compositions and clinical features. Cluster 1 showed a lower incidence of skin symptoms and Cluster 2 had a lower disease activity score and relatively normal immunity indicators. Conversely, Cluster 3 patients exhibited a higher prevalence of interstitial lung disease (ILD). Correlation analyses highlighted specific gut bacteria associated with clinical features, particularly strong negative correlations between core short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs)-producing bacteria, such as Faecalibacterium, Subdoligranulu, and Ruminococcus, and skin manifestations, disease activity, and inflammation indicators.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study revealed significant alterations in the gut microbiota of IIMs patients along with the distinct microbial signatures identified in different patient clusters, underscoring the potential role of gut microbiota in the pathogenesis and clinical heterogeneity of IIMs. These findings provide a novel perspective on the pathogenesis of IIMs and highlight the importance of gut microbiota as a potential therapeutic targ

candidates.title: Impact of Tiered Service Delivery Model on Antifibrotic Adherence and Outcomes Among Patients With Interstitial Lung Disease.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Within England, Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD) services are in the process of adopting tiered 'shared-care' service delivery to address increased demand. There are currently no data evaluating this model. We report on clinical outcomes of our Merseyside shared-care ILD service delivery over 2 years.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of adults with ILD started on antifibrotic therapy through our regional centre from 01/01/2022 to 31/12/2023. Alongside demographics and clinical data, we reviewed mortality and antifibrotic adherence. Patients were grouped on tier status of follow-up site: Tier 3 were Specialist ILD Network Hubs, Tier 2 were specialist centres with ILD nurse access, and Tier 1 were general respiratory centres with remote support from Tier 3 ILD nurses.
RESULTS: A total of 275 patients were commenced on antifibrotic therapy (mean age 72.3, 69% male, 68% on nintedanib), with comparable cohorts across tiers. Twelve-month all-cause antifibrotic discontinuation was 40%, and was associated with increased age (HR 1.04, p = 0.001), but not with tier status of follow-up site (p = 0.084). Twelve-month survival was 79%, and was not significantly different between tiers (p = 0.3). Progressive fibrotic ILD was associated with increased mortality risk, whereas higher BMI and baseline lung function were associated with reduced mortality. Patients on pirfenidone were more likely to have intolerable side effects (HR 1.60, p = 0.029), and patients stopping antifibrotics had a significantly increased mortality risk (adjusted HR 2.18, p = 0.003).
CONCLUSION: This retrospective real-world study suggests that a tiered approach to ILD service delivery-provided non-specialist sites are given appropriate support-can be a safe and effective model.

candidates.title: Systemic sclerosis markedly impairs health-related quality of life: a single-centre tertiary cohort study with literature-based comparison to leading causes of global disease burden.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune condition that significantly impacts the physical and mental health of affected individuals, disrupting their daily life and overall well-being. However, its impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) has not been thoroughly compared to other chronic diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and stroke, the impact of which is clearly established. We explored how SSc influences HRQoL and compared its effect to that of six chronic diseases, considered the global leading causes of disease burden in high-income countries, and three common rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases.
METHODS: We collected HRQoL data from SSc patients enrolled in a cross-sectional observational study at The Leeds Teaching Hospital NHS Trust, UK. We used the Medical Outcomes Study Short Form-36 to measure HRQoL and compared the participants' scores to published data on unipolar major depression, ischaemic heart disease, stroke, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, lung cancer, osteoarthritis, RA, and lower back pain. Mean norm-based transformed scores (NBS) were compared for all eight SF-36 health domains.
RESULTS: The 121 SSc patients (106 female; mean age = 57 years, standard deviation = 12.3), disease duration mean = 9.50 years, standard deviation = 7.4) in our study reported significantly worse perceived general health (mean (x̄) NBS = 32.82) than the other nine diseases reported in the literature. Role limitations due to physical problems (x̄ NBS = 34.77) were comparable to stroke, RA, and lung cancer. Significant impairments were noted in bodily pain (x̄ NBS = 36), similar to osteoarthritis, RA, and lower back pain, as well as vitality (x̄ NBS = 39.69), comparable to RA. Emotional role limitations (x̄ NBS = 41.78) were second only to major depression, similar to stroke and RA.
CONCLUSIONS: We found that SSc has a substantial impact on HRQoL, resulting in significant physical and psychological impairment comparab

candidates.title: Therapeutic advances in pulmonary fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Pharmacological treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) is evolving from two established antifibrotic agents towards a broader pipeline of therapies. Current standard treatment with nintedanib and pirfenidone slows the decline in forced vital capacity, but does not halt disease progression, and long-term use may be limited by tolerability issues. This review summarises major profibrotic mechanisms relevant to drug development and discusses therapies in advanced or emerging clinical programmes, including the recently FDA-approved nerandomilast, positive results from the phase 3 trial of inhaled treprostinil, as well as promising mid-stage, pathway-directed agents targeting a broad range of profibrotic signalling pathways. We also discuss how negative or terminated programmes highlight recurring limitations related to efficacy, safety, trial duration, endpoint selection, and patient heterogeneity. Finally, we outline current shifts in trial design and outcome assessment, including increasing emphasis on patient-centred and composite endpoints alongside physiological measures, and discuss the rationale for add-on and combination approaches in future antifibrotic therapy for IPF and PPF.

candidates.title: Candidate molecular endotypes and dynamic risk prediction in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease: a systematic scoping review.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis (anti-MDA5+ DM) spans pulmonary states from no detectable interstitial lung disease (ILD) to rapidly progressive ILD (RP-ILD). We mapped molecular programs and prediction evidence to determine how recurrent biological states may support dynamic stratification.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Ovid and Embase were searched from inception to 22 August 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR; evidence was synthesized across molecular and prediction domains.
RESULTS: Of 4, 166 records, 2, 317 remained after deduplication, 349 underwent full-text assessment, and 95 sources (80 primary studies and 15 syntheses) were included. Type I/III interferon signaling was the most reproducible program. Myeloid inflammatory-remodeling, adaptive activation with lymphocyte or natural-killer-cell loss, vascular-coagulation injury, and immunometabolic disturbance formed additional overlapping axes aligned with pulmonary-state transitions. Clinical and radiomic models showed strong short-term discrimination; harmonized landmarks, calibration, geographic validation, and decision-timed molecular sampling would strengthen clinical use.
CONCLUSION: The evidence supports an integrated map linking recurrent molecular programs to dynamic pulmonary risk. A calibrated clinical-imaging backbone, augmented by parsimonious molecular modules with incremental value and updated at prespecified landmarks, offers a practical framework for prospective endotype validation and treatment-aware prediction in anti-MDA5+ DM-ILD.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://doi.org/10.37766/inplasy2026.10.0018, identifier INPLASY2026100018.

candidates.title: Diagnostic Yield and Safety Profile of Shape-Sensing Robotic-Assisted Bronchoscopy in Peripheral Pulmonary Nodules 8 mm or Smaller.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Lung cancer screening guidelines generally recommend imaging surveillance rather than tissue sampling for nodules measuring ≤8 mm. Evidence regarding the feasibility, diagnostic performance, and safety of tissue biopsy in this lesion size remains limited. We evaluated the diagnostic performance and safety of shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (ssRAB) for biopsy of peripheral pulmonary nodules measuring ≤8 mm.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center study of consecutive patients who underwent ssRAB between June 2020 and December 2025 for biopsy of nodules measuring ≤8 mm on pre-procedural CT imaging. The primary outcome was strict diagnostic yield, as defined by the American Thoracic Society/American College of Chest Physicians. Secondary objectives included intermediate diagnostic yield, diagnostic distribution, procedural outcomes, and complications. Diagnostic performance according to lesion size (≤ 6 mm vs. 6.1-8 mm) was evaluated separately as a subgroup analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 195 nodules were included in the study. Median lesions diameter was seven mm (IQR 6-8). Strict diagnostic yield was 70.2% (137/195), while intermediate diagnostic yield was 77.4% (151/195). Malignancy was identified in 104 lesions (53.3%). The median ssRAB procedure time was 59 min (IQR 45-83). Pneumothorax occurred in six patients (3.3%), with chest tube placement required in two (1.1%).
DISCUSSION: Shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy demonstrated meaningful diagnostic performance and a favorable safety profile for peripheral pulmonary nodules measuring ≤8 mm, including lesions ≤6 mm. In this selected, higher-risk cohort, our findings suggest that earlier tissue diagnosis can be feasible and may benefit some patients.

candidates.title: CT-guided biopsy of pulmonary ground-glass nodules: core-needle biopsy versus fine-needle aspiration.
candidates.journal: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the diagnostic performance and complication profiles of CT-guided core-needle biopsy (CNB) and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) for pulmonary ground-glass nodules (GGNs).
METHODS: Consecutive patients who underwent CT-guided percutaneous biopsy of pulmonary GGNs between January 2021 and August 2022 were screened. Of 657 patients assessed, 538 were included (CNB, n = 448; FNA, n = 90). Six FNA results classified as atypical cells were considered indeterminate and excluded from binary diagnostic-performance analyses, leaving 532 classifiable cases. Final diagnoses were established by surgical pathology or imaging follow-up of at least 12 months. Diagnostic performance was compared without adjustment, whereas complication outcomes were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW).
RESULTS: Among the 532 classifiable biopsies, the overall accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity were 93.2%, 91.4%, and 100.0%, respectively, based on the available composite reference standard. CNB showed higher unadjusted accuracy than FNA (94.6% vs. 85.7%, P = 0.007) and higher sensitivity (93.2% vs. 82.4%, P = 0.008). In the full cohort of 538 procedures, multivariable analysis showed that CNB was associated with higher odds of intrapulmonary hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 2.91; P < 0.001) and hemoptysis (aOR: 3.07; P < 0.001), whereas no statistically significant association was observed for pneumothorax.
CONCLUSION: CT-guided percutaneous biopsy yielded determinate diagnostic results for most pulmonary GGNs under the available composite reference standard. In unadjusted comparisons, CNB showed higher diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity than FNA but was associated with greater risks of hemorrhagic complications. candidates.title: Long-term follow-up in Israel on Ethiopian migrants who underwent pre-arrival tuberculosis screening.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As tuberculosis (TB) incidence in Ethiopia is 50 times higher than in Israel, Ethiopian migrants (EM) undergo pre-departure TB screening using a medical questionnaire, physical examination, tuberculin skin test (TST), and chest X-ray (CXR). This study aims to characterize EM who developed post-arrival TB in Israel, and evaluate the association between pre-departure screening measures and subsequent active TB in Israel.
METHODS: This cohort study included all EM who underwent pre-departure screening and were followed up in Israel between 2015 and 2024. Pre-departure data were cross-matched with the Israeli national TB registry to identify EM who developed TB during the study period. The association between pre-departure screening results and subsequent post-migration TB was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, negative and positive predictive values (PPV).
RESULTS: Of all 6,919 EM, 98 (1.8%) showed pre-departure CXR suggestive of pulmonary-TB. While in Israel, 40 (0.6%) developed TB during the study period, mostly within the first 2-3 years post-migration. In multivariable analysis, HIV-infection, pre-departure CXR suggestive of pulmonary-TB, and greater TST were associated with post-migration TB diagnosis. The corresponding descriptive sensitivity of TST≥10mm in association with post-migration TB was 75.0% (95% CI:58.8-87.3%) and PPV of 2.1% (95% CI:1.4-3.0%).
