candidates.title: [Pulmonary Sclerosing Pneumocytoma Presenting With Ground-glass Nodule on Chest Computed Tomography:Report of a Case].
candidates.journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
candidates.abstract: A 77-year-old woman indicated multiple ground-glass opacities (GGOs) in the right lung on chest computed tomography (CT). A 11 mm GGO in S4 of the right lung showed a part solid component. Primary lung cancer was suspected, and surgical resection was planned. After CT-guided marking, videoassisted thoracoscopic partial resection of the right middle lobe was undergone. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day three. Histopathological examination showed proliferation of alveolar epithelial cells with mildly enlarged nuclei and small round cells with minimal atypia, leading to a diagnosis of pulmonary sclerosing pneumocytoma. This case highlights that pulmonary sclerosing pneumocytoma can present as an atypical GGO on chest CT.

candidates.title: Assessment of algorithmic performance in PET-CT segmentation of solitary lung tumors.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PET-CT (Positron emission tomography-computed tomography), a nuclear medicine imaging technique is preferably used for lung tumor detection. However, manual image analysis may be time-consuming. To enhance efficiency, many automated segmentation algorithms have been developed. This study aims to develop a radiomics agreement-based method to evaluate segmentation algorithms and to compare the performance of two deep learning-based algorithms nnU-Net (No-new-net Convolutional Neural Network) and RECOMIA (Research Consortium for Medical Image Analysis Lung Cancer "Lung Cancer FDG-PET/CT v1.5") for PET-CT solitary lung tumor segmentation.
METHODS AND RESULTS: PET-CT images of 221 patients at the University of Debrecen's Hospital were collected and anonymized. The predictions of segmented lung tumors done by nnU-Net and RECOMIA were compared with the manual segmented masks via Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Pearson correlation values, based on eight groups of radiomics parameters calculated by PyRadiomics software. The combined p-values were calculated using Brown's method, which were 0.481 and < 0.001 for nnU-Net and RECOMIA, respectively. The absolute values of correlation were summed, which were 37.259 and 16.358 for nnU-Net and RECOMIA, respectively. Altogether, RECOMIA shows statistically greater differences, therefore, it performs worse than nnU-Net does. Statistical analyses with Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) and follow up pairwise t-test further confirmed stronger agreement between extracted radiomics features from nnU-Net predicted masks and manual masks than RECOMIA and manual masks, which validated the proposed comparison method.
CONCLUSION: The superior performance of nnU-Net highlights the importance of training data alignment and model adaptability in achieving accurate and reliable segmentation in medical imaging. However, nnU-Net requirements for training and extra computational demands ma

candidates.title: Comparison of Two Deep Learning Models and Their Combination for 1-year Lung Cancer Detection in Two Screening Cohorts.
candidates.abstract: Purpose To evaluate the performance of Sybil, a Medical Open Network for Artificial Intelligence (MONAI)-based nodule model, and their combination for 1-year lung cancer detection in two screening cohorts: the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) and the Pamplona International Early Lung Cancer Action Program (P-IELCAP). Materials and Methods Baseline low-dose CT (LDCT) examinations from the NLST and the P-IELCAP were analyzed. A prespecified OR-stacked composite model combining Sybil, a MONAI-based nodule model, and a safety-net rule (MONAI-detected nodule > 6 mm with detection confidence > 0.95) was developed and evaluated for 1-year lung cancer detection. Model discrimination was assessed by using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and operating-point performance metrics were calculated. Results A total of 5110 baseline LDCT examinations were analyzed, including 2343 from NLST and 2767 from P-IELCAP, with 65 lung cancers diagnosed within 1 year. Mean age, mean pack-years, and percentage of female participants were 61.6 years ± 5.1 (SD), 57.3 pack-years ± 24.8, and 39.4% (923 of 2343), respectively, in NLST and 56.0 years ± 9.5, 34.4 pack-years ± 21.5, and 28.6% (791 of 2767), respectively, in P-IELCAP. Lung cancer incidence (per 1000 person-years) was higher in NLST than in P-IELCAP (17.7 vs 8.7; P = .006). Mean Sybil 1-year lung cancer probabilities (scaled by 1000 for presentation) were also higher in NLST than in P-IELCAP (16.4 vs 9.9; P < .01). Sybil achieved an AUC of 0.93 in both cohorts, whereas the MONAI-based model achieved AUCs of 0.90 in NLST and 0.79 in P-IELCAP. The composite model missed two of 65 1-year lung cancers while correctly classifying 2731 of 4965 (55.0%) noncancer examinations as negative, yielding a sensitivity of 63 of 65 (96.9%) and a positive predictive value of 63 of 2297 (2.7%). Conclusion For 1-year lung cancer detection with LDCT, the composite AI model achieved high sensitivity while maintaining accepta

candidates.title: Qualitative Insights From Public Interviews in the United Kingdom on the Acceptability of Risk-Based Eligibility Criteria for Lung Cancer Screening.
candidates.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Targeted lung cancer screening programmes in the United Kingdom use multivariable risk models to identify high-risk individuals. However, public acceptability of targeting screening by risk using eligibility criteria, such as age and smoking history, remains unclear, including the psychological and behavioural consequences of eligibility disclosure.
AIM: To explore UK public attitudes toward the acceptability of current risk-based eligibility criteria for lung cancer screening and the anticipated psychological and behavioural responses to eligibility disclosure.
METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted as the second phase of a sequential explanatory design. Semi-structured telephone interviews were held with 28 UK adults aged 45-77 years between January-April 2024. Participants were purposively sampled for diversity in demographics, smoking history, and prior acceptability questionnaire responses. Interviews were analysed using applied thematic analysis informed by the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability.
RESULTS: Criteria were generally acceptable when perceived as evidence-based and logical, particularly age and smoking history. However, participants expected flexibility, suggested expanding inclusion criteria and had concerns about fairness and discrimination especially regarding ethnicity and education. Eligibility was anticipated to motivate screening attendance but also cause worry; the prospect of ineligibility often led to feelings of exclusion, anxiety, and disappointment. Participants emphasised the need for clear, evidence-based communication of the rationale and individual risk, alongside alternative options or support for those who are ineligible.
CONCLUSIONS: Clear and transparent communication of the rationales underpinning eligibility criteria, provided by the screening programme and trusted health professionals, are essential for improving public acceptability and individual understanding of eligibility status. These strategies shou

candidates.title: Case Finding for COPD in Nottingham and District (C FIND COPD). A Pilot Study of Uptake, Acceptability and Diagnostic Yield in a One-Stop Assessment Following Lung Cancer Screening.
candidates.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Several lung cancer screening (LCS) programmes have identified a high prevalence of people with new (often pre-bronchodilator) airflow obstruction, but demonstrable translation into confirmed chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) diagnosis is limited. We evaluated a community-based, one-stop, post-bronchodilator case-finding and initial management pathway following LCS.
METHODS: Participants undergoing low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) as part of a LCS programme who reported respiratory symptoms were invited to attend a community-based assessment. The pathway included post-bronchodilator spirometry, clinical review and initial management delivered within a single encounter. The primary outcomes were uptake and new clinical diagnosis of COPD. Secondary outcomes included symptom burden, relationship to CT findings, socioeconomic variation and participant-reported experience.
RESULTS: Of 2860 invitation letters issues, 529 (18.5%) invitees participated; a further 33 participants self-presented. Of 562 participants overall, 486 completed spirometry, including 407 without a prior COPD diagnosis. Of these, 100 (25%) participants received a new clinical diagnosis of COPD, mainly with mild-to-moderate airflow obstruction. Among participants with a COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score ≥10, Medical Research Council (MRC) dyspnoea score ≥2, or clinician-defined respiratory symptoms, 35%, 34%, and 38%, respectively, had airflow obstruction. Moderate-to-severe CT emphysema was highly specific but poorly sensitive for airflow obstruction. We detected no significant difference in new COPD diagnosis across deprivation quintiles. Participant-reported experience was very positive.
CONCLUSION: A community-based, one-stop pathway following LCS can identify clinically meaningful COPD diagnosis in symptomatic individuals. This single encounter approach addresses a key gap in current LCS-linked pathways, maximising opportunities for case finding and supporting accessible,

candidates.title: Prevalence and Incidental Detection Rates of Thoracic Aortic Dilation and Aneurysm Across Computed Tomography Imaging Modalities in a Veteran Population.
candidates.journal: WMJ : official publication of the State Medical Society of Wisconsin
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prevalence and incidental detection rates of thoracic aortic dilation (TAD) and thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) in computed tomography (CT)-based screening programs (eg, low-dose CT for lung cancer screening) are poorly characterized but could inform opportunistic screening strategies.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort analysis, 9409 consecutive chest CT studies for 6795 unique patients at the Milwaukee Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, were evaluated between January 2023 and January 2025. Radiology reports were reviewed manually. Incidental cases were defined as findings not previously documented in clinical notes or prior imaging. Point prevalence and incidental rates were calculated.
RESULTS: The overall prevalence of TAD and TAA across CT cohorts was 6.1% (95% CI, 5.5%-6.6%) and 1.2% (95% CI, 0.95%-1.5%), respectively. The prevalence of TAD was 8.1% for low-dose CT (95% CI, 7.1%-9.1%), 8.3% for CT without contrast (95% CI, 6.5%-10.1%), and 3.2% for CT with contrast (95% CI, 2.6%-3.9%). The incidental detection rate of TAD was higher for low-dose CT (3.7%) than for CT without contrast (1.9%) and CT with contrast (1.2%).
CONCLUSIONS: Thoracic aortic dilation and thoracic aortic aneurysm are common among veterans undergoing clinically indicated chest CT imaging. Integrating opportunistic aortic assessment into existing CT screening programs deserves prospective evaluation to determine its clinical relevance and impact on downstream management.

candidates.title: Adherence to Cancer Screening Guidelines in Employer-Provided Healthcare Programs: A Survey of Companies in Lombardy (Northern Italy).
candidates.journal: Cancer control : journal of the Moffitt Cancer Center
candidates.abstract: ObjectivesOrganized, population-based cancer screening is recommended by European Union guidelines. Employer-provided screening within Workplace Health Promotion (WHP) programs may differ from evidence-based guidelines. This study aimed to evaluate the alignment between international cancer screening recommendations and screening services offered by companies participating in the Lombardy WHP Program.MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted between April and September 2024 among companies participating in the Lombardy WHP Program. Screening practices for breast, cervical, colorectal, prostate, and lung cancer were compared with the most recent international guidelines. Company characteristics were analyzed using descriptive statistics and univariate logistic regression models.ResultsOf the 308 companies participating in the survey, 95 reported the inclusion of preventive medicine services in their corporate welfare offer. Among these, breast cancer screening was the most frequently offered service (67.4%), followed by cervical cancer screening (57.9%). Both the majority of mammography offers (51%) and Pap test offers (92.6%) were not guideline-adherent, thus resulting in overscreening. Colorectal cancer (41.1%) and lung cancer (33.7%) screening were even less commonly provided by the participating companies. Prostate cancer screening with PSA testing was available in 63.2% of participating companies. Large companies had significantly lower odds of inappropriate mammography intervals (OR 0.11; 95% CI 0.02-0.58).ConclusionCancer screening services offered by companies, compliant with the Lombardy WHP Program, are frequently not aligned with current evidence-based recommendations, with overscreening emerging as a predominant issue. Strengthening coordination between occupational health services and public health authorities is essential to ensure appropriate, equitable, and sustainable integration of workplace-based screening initiatives into organized regional ca

candidates.title: FCM-Encoder: a novel interpretable framework with vision-language reasoning for coronary artery disease and solitary pulmonary nodule classification.
candidates.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
candidates.abstract: Although modern machine-learning models attain strong predictive performance, their clinical adoption remains limited by a lack of transparency. This concern is particularly relevant in multimodal diagnostic pipelines, where the contribution of each modality to the final prediction is more difficult to discern. Relatively few studies integrate heterogeneous clinical and imaging data, where they typically employ decision- or feature-level fusion, and provide limited insight into the cross-modal interactions that underline the diagnostic decision. We propose a Fuzzy Cognitive Map Encoder (FCM-Encoder) framework for multimodal explainable classification. Imaging features extracted by a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) are mapped into low-dimensional concepts and combined with normalised clinical concept activations inside a unified FCM. The connections to the diagnostic output are initialised from the Spearman rank correlation of each concept with the label, and all interconnections are then refined by a particle swarm optimisation strategy enhanced with Lévy-flight exploration. Under 10-fold cross-validation, the framework reached 81.82% ± 4.51% accuracy for Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) from clinical variables and polar maps, and 93.39% ± 3.09% for Solitary Pulmonary Nodule (SPN) classification in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) from CT, PET, and clinical data. The ablation analysis confirmed that each component contributes to the overall performance, the image-encoder comparison showed that the selected encoder matches or exceeds substantially larger pretrained backbones, and the graph-baseline comparison demonstrated that the FCM-based reasoning surpasses graph neural networks. FCM-Encoder further links imaging concepts to clinical labels and generates clinically aligned narratives through a Vision-Language module.

candidates.title: Maximising Cancer Prevention and Early Detection in the Australian Cancer Plan: Where Are We Now and What Should Come Next?
candidates.abstract: Cancer accounts for three in 10 deaths in Australia, yet many cases are preventable or can be detected at an early stage. Maximising cancer prevention and early detection is one of the six strategic objectives of the 10-year Australian Cancer Plan. This perspective article reviews the current progress and challenges of reducing the cancer burden, along with future opportunities. It explores how to address modifiable risk factors, particularly tobacco smoking, alcohol use and sun exposure and the advances in screening programs for bowel, breast, cervical and lung cancers. It highlights the potential for risk-stratified and genomics-informed screening, emphasising the need to support participation through equitable and culturally safe approaches.

candidates.title: Decoding Lung Cancer with Artificial Intelligence: A Path to Personalized Diagnostics and Therapy.
candidates.journal: Journal of environmental pathology, toxicology and oncology : official organ of the International Society for Environmental Toxicology and Cancer
candidates.abstract: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) represents the majority of lung cancer cases and remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Early detection, accurate staging, and individualized therapy are crucial for improving patient survival. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have transformed NSCLC care through the automated analysis of imaging, pathology, and molecular datasets. Deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) models, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have demonstrated high accuracy in tumor detection, histologic classification, biomarker prediction (PD-L1, EGFR, KRAS) and prognosis assessment. Integration of the AI with whole slide imaging (WSI), computed tomography (CT), PET/CT and liquid biopsies enables non-invasive tumor characterization, early recurrence detection and prediction of treatment response. Multimodal AI approaches that combine imaging, genomic, and clinical data offer superior patient stratification and personalized treatment planning compared with traditional methods. Beyond diagnosis, AI facilitates therapeutic development through radiomics based nodule classification, multi-omics data interpretation, and drug discovery. Radiomics, in particular, extracts quantitative imaging biomarkers that capture tumor heterogeneity beyond human perception. The AI further supports clinical decision-making in surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapy, enhancing workflow efficiency. Despite challenges in data quality, interpretability, and clinical adoption, AI holds significant promise for advancing precision oncology and improving outcomes in NSCLC management.

candidates.title: Non-Small Cell Lung Carcinoma With Bilayered Architecture and TP53 Alteration: A Diagnostic Pitfall and a Potential Distinct Entity.
candidates.abstract: The presence of a continuous basal cell layer is generally regarded as a defining feature of bronchiolar adenoma/ciliated muconodular papillary tumor (BA/CMPT), and preservation of this bilayered architecture is commonly used as a surrogate marker of benign behavior. We report a 1.1-cm pulmonary nodule detected in a 75-year-old never-smoker that exhibited marked high-grade cytologic atypia in both luminal and basal cells. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated diffuse strong P53 expression and an increased proliferative index (Ki-67 approximately 10%). Targeted next-generation sequencing revealed a pathogenic TP53 mutation (p.A161T). Despite the intact basal layer, the diffuse high-grade cytology and shared strong P53 expression in both compartments indicate that this lesion represents a fully malignant carcinoma rather than a benign BA/CMPT. In practice, it can only be classified as non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), NOS, with a distinctive bilayered phenotype. This case emphasizes that a preserved basal cell layer does not always equate to benignity, and it highlights a rare tumor type that may mimic BA/CMPT, carrying a risk of underdiagnosis. Integrating cytology, immunophenotype, and molecular findings is crucial for correct classification.

candidates.title: Screening opportunity gap in COPD evaluation after low-dose CT findings: implications for risk-based spirometry in primary care.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-dose chest computed tomography (CT) frequently detects findings suggestive of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, the pathway from CT detection to physiological confirmation remains poorly characterized in real-world clinical practice. This study evaluated follow-up pathways after CT findings suggestive of COPD and assessed whether simple clinical factors could identify individuals at high risk of airflow limitation.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study analyzed data from a voluntary, self-paid, community-based low-dose chest CT screening program in Japan that was open regardless of age or smoking history. Among 34,425 examinations conducted from fiscal year 2015 through February 2025, 1,336 examinations referred for suspected COPD were analyzed. Follow-up pathways were categorized as no documented follow-up, follow-up without spirometry, and follow-up with spirometry. Two multivariable logistic regression models evaluated documented follow-up and spirometry use. Airflow limitation was defined as a post-bronchodilator FEV₁/FVC ratio < 0.70.
RESULTS: Among 1,336 examinations, 305 (22.8%) had no documented follow-up, 556 (41.6%) had documented follow-up without spirometry, and 475 (35.6%) had documented follow-up with spirometry. Among those who underwent spirometry, airflow limitation was identified in 298 (62.7%). Current smoking was associated with lower documented follow-up, whereas older age and greater cumulative smoking exposure were associated with spirometry use. Concurrent suspicion of lung cancer was associated with a lower likelihood of spirometry use. Airflow limitation rates increased according to simple clinical risk factors. Examinations with all three risk factors-age ≥ 70 years, pack-years ≥ 40, and respiratory symptoms-had an airflow limitation prevalence of 79.8%. Notably, 90 examinations without spirometry met these high-risk criteria.
CONCLUSION: In this community-based CT screening program, substanti

candidates.title: Intraoperative titanium clip localization versus preoperative medical glue localization for pulmonary nodules: a prospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative CT-guided percutaneous localization of pulmonary nodules is widely used in clinical practice but is often associated with localization-related complications. Intraoperative titanium clip localization may provide a safer localization strategy. This study aimed to compare the effectiveness and safety of these two approaches.
METHODS: This single-center prospective cohort study included 189 patients who underwent pulmonary nodule resection after localization between October 2023 and November 2025. Patients were divided into an intraoperative titanium clip localization group (n = 123) and a preoperative medical glue localization group (n = 66) based on the localization method. Localization success rate, localization-related complications, and perioperative outcomes were analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 252 pulmonary nodules were localized. The intraoperative group demonstrated a significantly higher localization success rate than the preoperative group (99.4% vs. 89.0%; OR, 18.07; 95% CI, 2.18-149.84; P = 0.007), along with a lower incidence of localization-related complications (0% vs. 30.3%; OR, 0.004). However, the duration of general anesthesia was longer in the intraoperative group (196.34 ± 54.46 vs. 162.76 ± 57.19 min; P = 0.001). There were no significant differences in postoperative drainage volume, postoperative complication rates, or length of hospital stay between the two groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative titanium clip localization demonstrated a higher localization success rate and a lower incidence of localization-related complications. It may have potential value for simultaneous localization of multiple pulmonary nodules. However, this approach was associated with a longer duration of general anesthesia.

candidates.title: PET Imaging of Infection, Inflammation, and Immune-mediated Disease: From Fluorodeoxyglucose to Pathogen-specific and Immune-targeted Tracers.
candidates.abstract: PET/computed tomography (CT) is an important tool for evaluating infectious, inflammatory, and immune-mediated diseases when conventional testing is inconclusive. This article reviews the clinical applications of fluorodeoxyglucose-PET/CT in fever of unknown origin, cardiovascular and musculoskeletal infections, large-vessel vasculitis, sarcoidosis, autoimmune disorders, and transplant rejection. Emphasis is placed on practical interpretation, characteristic imaging patterns, and factors affecting diagnostic accuracy, including patient preparation, myocardial suppression protocols, glucocorticoid therapy, and postoperative inflammation. Emerging PET approaches, such as immuno-PET, radiolabeled leukocyte PET, and bacteria-specific tracers, are also discussed, highlighting the shift toward more biologically specific imaging of infection, inflammation, and immune activity.

candidates.title: Real-World Experience With Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Natural Language Processing for Identification and Management of Incidental Lung Nodules.
candidates.abstract: BackgroundIncidental lung nodules (ILNs) are common, but adherence to guideline-recommended follow-up is variable, which may contribute to delayed diagnosis of malignancy. Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms using natural language processing (NLP) may improve identification, but their impact on clinical management and outcomes remains uncertain.ObjectivesThis study describes ILN identification, follow-up management, and timeliness of cancer treatment after implementation of an AI-enabled NLP platform at a large health system.DesignSingle-center retrospective observational study.MethodsAdults with ILNs identified on imaging between April 2023 and May 2024 were included. The pre-AI cohort was identified using diagnosis codes, while the post-AI cohort was identified using an NLP-based AI platform. Because these methods captured different populations, no formal comparative testing was performed, and outcomes were summarized descriptively.ResultsA total of 1,098 patients with ILNs were identified: 228 from 6,828 pre-AI imaging studies (3.3%) and 870 from 9,902 post-AI imaging studies (8.8%). Most pre-AI ILNs were identified on outpatient imaging (74%), while post-AI ILNs were identified in inpatient (35%), emergency department (26%), and outpatient (39%) settings. A follow-up recommendation was documented for 195 of 228 pre-AI patients (85.5%) and 563 of 870 post-AI patients (64.7%). Among these patients, completion was documented for 167 of 195 (85.6%) and 414 of 563 (73.5%), respectively. Malignancy was documented in 28 of 228 pre-AI patients (12.3%) and 15 of 870 post-AI patients (1.7%). Median imaging-to-biopsy time was 78 days pre-AI and 120 days post-AI; biopsy-to-treatment and imaging-to-treatment intervals were similar.ConclusionThe post-AI cohort included more identified ILNs and a greater proportion from acute-care settings than the historical pre-AI cohort. Because identification methods were not comparable, observed differences in documented malignancy dia

candidates.title: Multi-Backbone U-Net segmentation and interpretable hybrid deep learning classification for lung cancer detection in chest CT images.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and its early and accurate diagnosis from chest CT imaging is complicated by overlapping radiological features between benign and malignant lesions, as well as by the limited cross-institution validation and interpretability reported in much of the existing computer-aided diagnosis literature. This study evaluates the effectiveness of U-Net architectures integrated with different pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) backbones for automated lung segmentation and lung cancer classification in chest CT images, with an emphasis on rigorous, leakage-free validation and cross-institution generalizability relevant to clinical practice.
METHODS: A balanced internal dataset of 832 chest CT images (416 cancerous and 416 non-cancerous cases, NIDCH, Bangladesh) was preprocessed using Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and resized to 224 × 224 pixels. U-Net models with three CNN backbones (VGG16, ResNet50, and Xception) were implemented for lung segmentation, with pseudo-labels verified against expert-annotated masks. A standalone CNN and three hybrid classifiers combining CNN feature extraction with machine learning algorithms (Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting) were then evaluated, alongside a Vision Transformer baseline. All models were assessed using subject-level fivefold cross-validation, followed by fully independent external testing on a second, structurally distinct dataset (IQ-OTH/NCCD; 110 subjects) without retraining. Performance was measured using Dice coefficient, IoU, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC, with 95% confidence intervals and statistical significance testing.
RESULTS: For segmentation, U-Net with the Xception backbone achieved the best overall performance (Dice: 0.9581 ± 0.0104; IoU: 0.9163 ± 0.0167). For classification, the CNN + SVM hybrid model achieved the highest internal cross-validation ac

candidates.title: 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT for Detection of Locoregional Lymph Node Metastases in Gynecologic Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Detection of locoregional lymph node (LN) metastases is a critical prognostic factor in gynecologic squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is limited by insufficient specificity, potentially leading to overtreatment. We evaluated gallium-68 fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (68Ga-FAPI-04) positron-emission tomography (PET)/CT for the detection of locoregional LN metastases in this setting, using CT as comparator.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT scans of 15 patients with gynecologic SCC (nine cervical, six vulvar carcinomas; mean age 56.3 years, range=38-86 years) were analyzed. PET/CT and CT were read independently by two blinded readers. Histopathology and/or clinical and radiological follow-up (12-18 months) served as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was calculated on a patient-based level; maximum standardized uptake values (SUVmax) were compared using Welch's t-test and the Mann-Whitney U-test.
RESULTS: Histopathological confirmation was available in 12 patients; three were classified by follow-up. LN metastases were confirmed in five patients. 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT achieved a sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV) and accuracy of 100%. CT achieved a sensitivity and NPV of 100% but produced false-positive findings in three patients (specificity=70%, PPV=62.5%, accuracy=80%), caused by tattoo-associated lymphadenopathy, sarcoidosis and reactive nodal enlargement, none of which showed pathological tracer uptake. Metastatic LNs exhibited higher SUVmax (mean 23.2±6.0) than nodes false-positive on CT (mean 4.5±4.6; p=0.004 and p=0.036). Primary tumors were visualized in all patients undergoing initial staging; peritoneal nodules down to 7 mm were detected.
CONCLUSION: In this small cohort, 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT showed a higher observed specificity than contrast-enhanced CT for the detection of loco

candidates.title: Automated Opportunistic Bone Mineral Density Assessment at Low-Dose CT Lung Cancer Screening: Incident Vertebral Fractures and Mortality.
candidates.abstract: Background Low-dose CT (LDCT) for lung cancer screening enables opportunistic volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) assessment, but its prognostic value is unclear. Purpose To evaluate fully automated LDCT-derived vBMD for predicting vertebral fractures and its association with mortality in individuals who heavily smoke. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis included 55-74-year-old individuals who heavily smoked (≥30 pack-years) from the CT arm of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST), a multicenter randomized controlled trial of LDCT versus radiography (participants recruited August 2002 to April 2004). Automated SpineQ software (Bonescreen) was used to measure thoracic and lumbar vBMD (normal, ≥120 mg/cm3; low bone mass [osteopenia], 80 to <120 mg/cm3; osteoporosis, <80 mg/cm3) and vertebral fractures (Genant scale). The outcomes included 1- and 2-year incident vertebral fractures and 6-year mortality (active follow-up to 2009). Poisson and Cox models were adjusted for demographic variables, available comorbidities, and baseline vertebral fractures. Results The NLST included 26 722 participants in the CT arm, with 21 856 included in the present analysis (mean age, 61 years ± 5 [SD]; 12 854 male participants). The 2-year vertebral fracture incidence (n = 18 211 participants with 2-year LDCT) was 0.9% for those with normal bone mass, 2.0% for those with low bone mass (adjusted relative risk, 2.07 [95% CI: 1.70, 2.53]), and 5.9% for those with osteoporosis (adjusted relative risk, 3.40 [95% CI: 2.69, 4.30]). Mortality risk (n = 21 447 participants with completed follow-up [median, 6.65 years]) was associated with osteoporotic vBMD in men (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.24 [95% CI: 1.02, 1.50]). Conclusion Fully automated opportunistic assessment of spinal vBMD predicted vertebral fracture risk and was associated with mortality in men after adjustment. Individuals with osteoporotic vBMD who heavily smoked had a 2-year fracture incidence above the 5% treatment th

candidates.title: Diagnostic Performance of Lung-RADS Categories in Patients With Histopathologically Evaluated Pulmonary Lesions: A Retrospective Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) categories for predicting malignancy in a selected cohort of patients with pulmonary lesions who underwent histopathological evaluation.
METHODS: This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included patients with pulmonary lesions detected on computed tomography (CT) who underwent histopathological evaluation between January 2011 and February 2018, and their CT images were retrospectively classified according to Lung-RADS version 1.0. Patients were grouped by age and sex. Histopathologic examination was accepted as the gold standard test. Negative and positive results according to the Lung RADS guidelines and histopathological results were compared. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive, and negative predictive values were calculated as a result of this comparison.
RESULTS: A total of 161 patients were included, of whom 122 (75.8%) had malignant and 39 (24.2%) had benign histopathological findings. According to Lung-RADS, 151 patients (93.8%) were classified as positive and 10 (6.2%) as negative. Lung-RADS categories were significantly associated with histopathological outcomes ( P < 0.001), with malignancy rates increasing across categories. Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV were 99.2%, 23.1%, 80.1%, and 90.0%, respectively. Diagnostic performance was more favorable in older patients, particularly in the 55-80 age group (κ =0.407, P < 0.001), with similar findings observed in the 55-74 subgroup (κ =0.404, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort of patients undergoing histopathological evaluation, Lung-RADS demonstrated high sensitivity but limited specificity for predicting malignant pulmonary lesions. We believe that prospective studies conducted using multicenter, standardized protocols involving larger patient groups will yield more accurate data.

candidates.title: Environmental Exposure to Carcinogens and Cancer Incidence in Kazakhstan: Opportunities for Cancer Prevention.
candidates.journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kazakhstan is a large country in Central Asia with long history of uranium and asbestos mining and nuclear testing, whose health effects have not been fully analyzed.
OBJECTIVES: To study the geographical distribution of cancer rates in relation to toxic sites.
METHODS: We conducted an extensive review of publicly available datasets, administrative documents, and publications to assess past and active sources of exposure to carcinogens, and the geographic distribution of cancer incidence.
FINDINGS: Several past and ongoing sources of environmental exposures were identified. Cancer incidence is unevenly distributed, with the highest rates in the areas where nuclear testing was performed. The most frequently observed cancers are those of the lung, stomach, colorectum, and hematopoietic system. Among males, prostate cancer entered the list of the top cancers, while among females, breast, uterine, and cervical cancer were the most represented.
CONCLUSIONS: There are relatively small, densely populated areas that are heavily impacted by reactors, previous nuclear testing, uranium mines, chemical plants, and nuclear waste facilities. The geographic distribution of cancer rates reflects, in part, the location of the polluting sites, as well as personal exposure to behavioral risk factors, such as smoking and dietary habits. Aggressive preventive measures should be put in place for those cancers that are preventable through either screening or vaccination. Because of the many radon and uranium sites, lung cancer screening should be routinely offered to high-risk populations.

candidates.title: Transporting Lung Cancer Screening Effects From National Lung Screening Trial to a US Screening-Eligible Population.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: The National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) found that screening with annual low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces lung cancer (LC) mortality. Because studies have shown that the US population eligible for screening differs from NLST, we sought to quantitatively extend the NLST findings to this population.
METHODS: We reweighted individual-level NLST data using inverse odds weights (IOW) to the covariate distribution of a contemporary screening-eligible population from the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) data. In the IOW and unweighted NLST population, we estimated the LC-specific and all-cause mortality among individuals undergoing three annual screenings of LDCT compared with chest radiography, as well as false-positive rates in the LDCT arm only.
RESULTS: We included 53,454 NLST participants and 7,265,314 survey-weighted screening-eligible BRFSS respondents (unweighted sample of 15,779). The BRFSS population was older, more racially and ethnically diverse, and more likely to currently smoke and have respiratory comorbidities. We estimated similar benefits of screening on LC and all-cause mortality in the weighted versus unweighted NLST population (5-year LC risk difference [RD; 95% CI], -29 [-54, 4] v -23 [-44, 3]; all-cause RD [95% CI], -44 [-95, 8] v -37 [-66, -7] deaths per 10,000 screened). Estimated false-positive rates were higher in the weighted versus unweighted NLST population across three annual screenings.
CONCLUSION: We estimated similar mortality benefits and slightly increased false-positive rates from LDCT in the weighted versus unweighted NLST population. Our findings account for the potential differences within subgroups of interest but not variations in longitudinal adherence and diagnostic work-up between trial and clinical practice.

candidates.title: Early Clinical Evaluation of AI Triage of Chest Radiographs: Time to Diagnosis for Suspected Cancer and Number of Urgent CT Referrals.
candidates.abstract: AbstractLung cancer is the leading cause of cancer mortality in the United Kingdom. Early diagnosis and rapid access to treatment are associated with better outcomes but are dependent on prompt recognition of findings and the availability of a computed tomography (CT) scanner and reporting. In this clinical evaluation case study, we report the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to triage suspected cancer on chest x-rays to a "radiographer-led same-day CT pathway." We included 56,257 chest radiographs acquired before and after real-world AI deployment across a National Health Service trust comprising five hospitals in South West London over a 3-year study period between January 2022 and December 2024 (1 year preintervention and 2 years postintervention). The time from chest radiograph acquisition to CT report for cases with suspected lung cancer was reduced from 6.0 to 3.6 days, with the most significant reductions at centers with colocated CT and x-ray facilities and no significant increase in the proportion of CTs performed relative to chest x-rays. In detecting suspected cancer, the 14-feature AI triage model has an 82.5% sensitivity, a 90.5% specificity, a 14.6% positive predictive value, and a 99.6% negative predictive value for possible lung cancer on chest x-rays. Features such as focal airspace opacity and single pulmonary nodule returned the highest proportion of false-positive results, while pulmonary and mediastinal masses had a greater diagnostic yield. This work demonstrates how AI triage can be implemented for the rapid onward diagnosis of lung cancer and informs the deployment of triage systems for urgent cancer pathways in general.

candidates.title: Cancer Screening, Diagnosis, and Survival in California Prisons.
candidates.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cancer is the leading cause of death in prison. Limited literature suggests cancer screening rates in prison are low, but population-level screening data in prisons are scarce.
OBJECTIVE: To determine screening rates for 5 cancer types, identify individual and incarceration characteristics associated with receipt of screening, and characterize outcomes for screen-detectable cancers in California prisons.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study included individuals incarcerated in California state prisons who were eligible for breast, cervical, colorectal, liver, or lung cancer screening between January 1, 2014, and June 30, 2023. Incarceration data were linked to state cancer registry data from 2014 to 2021 to identify screen-detectable cancers diagnosed in the study population. Analyses were conducted between August 2024 and July 2025.
EXPOSURES: Receipt of screening within 3 months before a cancer diagnosis.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Receipt of cancer screening; screening rates; and cancer diagnosis, stage, and survival were calculated. Multivariable models evaluated characteristics associated with screening receipt and associations between screening receipt and stage at diagnosis and survival, with adjustment for demographic and incarceration characteristics.
RESULTS: The study included 106 352 incarcerated individuals (median [IQR] age at first eligibility, 50 [47-55] years; 86 559 males [81.4%]). By June 30, 2023 (data cutoff), 89.4%, 81.2%, 80.0%, 70.1%, and 76.0% of individuals were up-to-date with screening for breast, colorectal, cervical, lung, and liver cancer screening, respectively. Characteristics associated with higher likelihood of ever receiving screening included mental health service use, prison security level 3 or 4, recent change in primary care practitioner, and incarceration within the past year before screening eligibility. Of 812 patients with screening data, 92 (11.3%) were diagnosed with screen-detectable cancer

candidates.title: Low-Dose CT in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Techniques, Evidence, and Clinical Impact.
candidates.abstract: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) is essential for reducing potential radiation-associated risks, but increased noise and artifacts can compromise diagnostic confidence. This review examines how AI is reshaping LDCT by improving reconstruction, denoising, protocol optimization, and workflow integration. It outlines the evolution from FBP to IR and then to deep learning methods that better preserve anatomical detail while reducing noise. The review also considers emerging applications in photon-counting CT (PCCT) and discusses clinical use in screening, pediatric imaging, oncology, cardiac imaging, and emergency care. These developments may support safer imaging, improve consistency across studies, and reduce the need for repeat examinations. However, important challenges remain, including limited generalizability across scanners and patient populations, the potential loss of subtle findings, changes in quantitative imaging features, and the need for careful validation before widespread clinical adoption. Further research should focus on multicenter validation, task-based performance assessment, and integration into routine clinical workflows.

candidates.title: Deep Learning-Based Reconstruction in Ultra-Low-Dose CT of the Ankle and Foot: A Comparative Study with Hybrid Iterative Reconstruction.
candidates.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the quantitative and qualitative performance of ultra-low-dose CT with deep learning image reconstruction (DLR) compared to conventional hybrid iterative reconstruction (IR) in patients with ankle and foot fractures. Methods: A total of 32 patients (mean age, 54 ± 16 years) with ankle and foot fractures were included in this retrospective study. All patients underwent ultra-low-dose CT imaging (effective dose, 0.86 ± 0.11 μSv), and the same CT raw data were reconstructed using both DLR and hybrid IR. Image noise, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) were quantitatively measured, and image sharpness was evaluated using a no-reference perceptual sharpness metric. Subjective image quality was assessed by a board-certified radiologist and an orthopedic surgeon using a five-point scale. Results: DLR significantly reduced image noise (47.33 ± 6.60 HU) compared to hybrid IR (87.65 ± 12.48 HU), and significantly improved SNR (31.42 ± 5.81 for DLR vs. 19.15 ± 4.48 for hybrid IR) and CNR (50.59 ± 7.62 for DLR vs. 24.08 ± 3.81 for hybrid IR). Image sharpness was significantly (p = 0.001) improved with DLR (0.76 ± 0.09) compared to hybrid IR (0.59 ± 0.09). Subjective image analysis revealed enhanced visualization of trabecular architecture, superior delineation and integrity of cortical bone, and improved depiction of bony cortical lesions with DLR compared to hybrid IR. Conclusions: Ultra-low-dose CT with DLR offers a superior approach to enhance image quality, making it a valuable tool for clinical practice.

candidates.title: Opportunistic Cardiovascular Assessment During Lung Cancer Screening with Low-Dose Computed Tomography: A New Window for Prevention.
candidates.abstract: Population-based lung cancer screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) is expanding across Europe, including a publicly funded Polish programme starting in October 2026. Because screening-eligible individuals share substantial tobacco-related cardiovascular risk, LDCT also offers cardiovascular risk assessment without additional radiation. We conducted a narrative review of the PubMed literature published up to September 2026, prioritising guidelines, lung cancer screening cohorts and systematic reviews. We summarise the cardiovascular findings on non-contrast, non-electrocardiography (ECG)-gated LDCT: coronary artery, aortic valve, mitral annular and thoracic aortic calcification, ascending aortic dilatation, pericardial effusion, and pulmonary artery enlargement, as well as investigational cardiac volumetry, epicardial adipose tissue and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted quantification. We grade each finding by reportability, defined downstream action and supporting evidence, and align reporting thresholds with the European Respiratory Society/European Society of Thoracic Imaging (ERS/ESTI) statement on incidental findings. LDCT cannot replace dedicated cardiac imaging or establish haemodynamic diagnoses. The prognostic value of coronary and aortic valve calcification and of ascending aortic dilatation is established, whereas the evidence for mitral annular calcification and pulmonary artery enlargement is more limited; observational data indicate that reporting these markers changes preventive management, but whether this improves cardiovascular outcomes has not yet been demonstrated. Standardised reporting, proportionate thresholds, and coordinated pathways linking radiology, pulmonology, primary care and cardiology are needed to translate incidental cardiovascular findings into scalable prevention and should be evaluated in implementation studies.

candidates.title: Low-dose CT denoising using a diffusion prior via score distillation sampling.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces radiation exposure but amplifies noise, which can degrade diagnostic reliability. Recent studies have applied diffusion-based models to LDCT denoising and shown promising performance. However, many of these approaches require paired LDCT and normal-dose CT (NDCT) data or dose-specific retraining, and their reconstruction procedures are often strictly coupled to a predefined diffusion trajectory.
PURPOSE: This study proposes an optimization-based LDCT denoising framework that uses a pre-trained NDCT diffusion model as an image prior and can be applied across various dose levels without dose-specific retraining.
METHODS: We formulate LDCT denoising as an optimization problem guided by a pre-trained score-based generative model (SGM) trained only on NDCT images. The Poisson data fidelity term enforces consistency with the measured projection data, whereas the score distillation sampling (SDS) term acts as a regularizer that guides the reconstruction toward the NDCT distribution learned by the pre-trained SGM. The denoised image is obtained by iteratively optimizing a projection-domain residual variable using the combined Poisson data fidelity gradient and SDS-based regularization gradient.
RESULTS: The proposed method effectively suppressed noise while preserving fine anatomical structures across multiple dose levels using a single pre-trained diffusion model. Quantitative evaluations with respect to full-dose reference images and visual comparisons demonstrated competitive performance compared with supervised and self-supervised LDCT denoising baselines.
CONCLUSIONS: The results show that diffusion-based image priors can be leveraged across various low-dose levels within the proposed optimization-based denoising framework. Our work suggests that SDS-guided diffusion priors are a promising direction for LDCT denoising in data-limited settings.

candidates.title: AI-based automated body composition analysis from whole-body MRI and (PET-) CT: an intermodal comparison from same-day examinations.
candidates.journal: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To determine intermodal agreement of AI-derived volumetric body composition metrics between [18 F]FDG-PET/CT-derived low-dose CT and whole-body MRI (wb-MRI).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed same-day whole-body low-dose CT, obtained from [18F]FDG-PET/CT, and wb-MRI from consecutive multiple myeloma patients from the prospective GMMG-HD7- and GMMG-HD8-/DSMM-XIX-trials. An automated deep learning pipeline based on the TotalSegmentator model, and its MRI variant were used to segment skeletal muscle (SM), subcutaneous- (SAT) and abdominal visceral adipose tissue (VAT) from CT and MRI, respectively. Volumetric measures and single-slice estimates were derived. Agreement between CT- and MRI-based metrics was assessed using Pearson r, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Bland-Altman analyses.
RESULTS: Forty-two multiple myeloma patients with same-day PET/CT and wb-MRI were included. For AI-based volumetric body composition metrics, CT and MRI demonstrated high agreement (ICC > 0.95) across all SM, SAT and VAT. However, Bland-Altmann plots revealed systematic modality-related differences between MRI and CT: both SM (bias: -2582 ml, p < 0.0001) and VAT (bias: -211 ml, p < 0.0001) were significantly lower when extracted from MRI compared to CT, while for SAT, the difference was not statistically significant (bias: -263 ml, p = 0.1629). For AI-based single slice analysis, agreement remained high for SAT and VAT (ICC > 0.97), while being lower for SM (ICC 0.87). Bland-Altman plots showed that SM was systematically and significantly lower when obtained from MRI than from CT (bias: -18.4cm2, p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: Automated body composition measures from (PET-)CT and wb-MRI are highly concordant but show consistent intermodal biases that should be considered when pooling multimodal data or applying modality-agnostic thresholds.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

candidates.title: Prevalence of ECG-detected and previously unrecognized atrial fibrillation among older adults attending a family health center: a single-center cross-sectional screening study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an important and often unrecognized cause of ischemic stroke in older adults. The primary objective of this study was to determine the prevalence of AF detected by a single 12-lead ECG among adults aged ≥ 65 years attending primary care. Secondary objectives were the proportion previously unrecognized, thromboembolic risk and anticoagulant use, and associated characteristics.
METHODS: This single-center cross-sectional study enrolled consecutive consenting adults aged ≥ 65 years attending a family health center in Istanbul, Türkiye (May 2021-May 2022). Of 359 assessed, 2 with pacemakers were excluded, leaving 357. AF on the screening 12-lead ECG was diagnosed by the investigator and confirmed by a cardiologist; AF was classified as previously known when a prior diagnosis was reported and as previously unrecognized otherwise. The study-period anticoagulation threshold was defined as CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥ 2 in men and ≥ 3 in women. Prevalences are reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs); associations were examined with chi-square or exact tests and exploratory Firth penalized logistic regression.
RESULTS: AF was detected on the screening ECG in 42 participants (11.8%; 95% CI 8.8-15.5), with similar prevalence by sex. Prevalence differed across age groups (P=.034), with the highest estimate among participants aged ≥ 80 years (26.3%; 95% CI 15.0-42.0). Twenty-two of the 42 ECG-detected AF cases were previously unrecognized (52.4%; 6.2% of all screened participants, 95% CI 4.1-9.2). In an exploratory adjusted model, heart failure (aOR 5.71; 95% CI 1.81-18.00) and chronic lung disease (aOR 2.53; 95% CI 1.24-5.19) were associated with ECG-detected AF, whereas the age estimate was attenuated after adjustment (aOR 1.69 per decade; 95% CI 0.98-2.90). The mean CHA₂DS₂-VASc score was 3.64 ± 1.53, and 37 participants with AF (88.1%) met the study-period anticoagulation threshold. Twenty were not receiving anticoagulation at screening,

candidates.title: Association of SII and SIRI with anxiety and depression severity in patients with acute coronary syndrome: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
candidates.abstract: Emerging evidence indicates that inflammatory mechanisms may play a key role in linking psychological disorders to cardiovascular outcomes. This study aimed to explore the association between anxiety and depression levels and two inflammatory markers, the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) and the Systemic Inflammatory Response Index (SIRI), in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). This retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted on 1498 patients with ACS who underwent coronary angiography (CAG) in Rasht, Iran, between January 2022 and June 2023. SII and SIRI were calculated for all patients. Patients' psychological status regarding anxiety and depression was evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). All data analyses were conducted using SPSS version 22. The mean age of the patients was 58.49 ± 11.14 years, with males comprising 57.5% of the sample. Male participants exhibited significantly higher levels of anxiety and depression compared to females (P < .05). Individuals with comorbidities showed significantly lower anxiety scores (P < .05). Anxiety levels varied significantly based on CAG findings (P = .004). In multivariable ordinal logistic regression analyses, neither SII nor SIRI was significantly associated with depression severity (SII: OR = 1.029, 95% CI: 0.70-1.49; SIRI: OR = 1.012, 95% CI: 0.86-1.03) or anxiety severity (SII: OR = 0.906, 95% CI: 0.63-1.29; SIRI: OR = 1.005, 95% CI: 0.98-1.03). Systemic inflammation indices (SII and SIRI) did not show significant associations with anxiety or depression severity in cardiac patients, highlighting their limited utility as psychological predictors.

candidates.title: The application value of two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging technology in evaluating the functions of the left atrium and left atrial appendage in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation: A comparative cross-sectional study.
candidates.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with increased risk of stroke due to left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus formation. Two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging (2D-STI) may provide valuable insights into left atrial and LAA functional changes associated with thrombus formation. This study aimed to evaluate the functions of the left atrium (LA) and LAA in patients with non-valvular AF by using 2D-STI and explore echocardiographic parameters associated with the presence of LAA thrombus. In this comparative cross-sectional study, consecutive patients with non-valvular AF who were scheduled for radiofrequency ablation were screened. Finally, 68 eligible AF patients and 30 age-matched healthy controls were included. All AF patients underwent preoperative transthoracic echocardiography, transesophageal echocardiography, and two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging, and were classified according to the presence or absence of LAA thrombus detected by transesophageal echocardiography into the thrombus group (n = 32) and the non-thrombus group (n = 36). The healthy controls were included as a reference group for comparison of echocardiographic parameters. The left atrial appendage emptying velocity (LAAEV), left atrial global longitudinal strain (LAGLS), and LAA global longitudinal strain (LAAGLS) were measured and compared between groups. Compared with the control group, AF patients showed significantly reduced LAAEV, LAGLS, and left atrial appendage global longitudinal strain (all P < .05). In AF patients, the thrombus group had significantly lower LAAEV, LAGLS, and left atrial appendage global longitudinal strain compared to the non-thrombus group (all P < .05). Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that LAAEV and left atrial strain during reservoir phase were significantly associated with the presence of LAA thrombus. 2D-STI can quantitatively evaluate the functional changes of the LA and LAA. candidates.title: Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index is Associated With Tumor Size and Preoperative Cerebrovascular Events in Left Atrial Myxoma.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac myxomas are benign tumors associated with potentially serious cerebrovascular complications. The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is a readily available inflammatory marker; however, its relationship with tumor burden and cerebrovascular events in patients with left atrial myxoma remains unclear. This study investigated the associations of SII with tumor size and preoperative stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA).
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective study included 120 patients who underwent surgical resection of histopathologically confirmed left atrial myxoma between May 2014 and December 2025. Tumor size was assessed as the largest cross-sectional area measured by transesophageal echocardiography. SII was calculated from preoperative neutrophil, platelet, and lymphocyte counts. Correlation, multivariable regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Preoperative stroke/TIA occurred in 17 patients (14.2%). SII was positively correlated with tumor size (ρ = 0.602, p < 0.001) and remained significantly associated with tumor area after multivariable adjustment (β = 0.100 cm2 per 100-unit increase, 95% CI: 0.078-0.123; p < 0.001). Patients with larger tumors had a higher prevalence of preoperative stroke/TIA (21.9% vs. 5.4%, p = 0.016). Similarly, cerebrovascular events were more frequent in patients with high SII (≥840) than in those with low SII (32.4% vs. 6.0%, p < 0.001). Both SII (adjusted OR = 1.05 per 100-unit increase, 95% CI: 1.01-1.09; p = 0.021) and tumor size (adjusted OR = 1.80, 95% CI: 1.05-3.09; p = 0.033) were associated with preoperative stroke/TIA in multivariable analysis. SII demonstrated the highest numerical ROC area (AUC = 0.782), compared with the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (0.746), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (0.710), and tumor size (0.682).
CONCLUSIONS: SII was significantly associated with tumor size and preoperative cerebrovascular events in patients with

candidates.title: Machine Learning-Based Clustering of Clinical Phenotypes in Adults With Bicuspid Aortic Valve: A Large Single-Center Study.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is clinically heterogeneous, and the relationships among valve morphology, valvular dysfunction, and aortic involvement remain incompletely understood. We aimed to identify clinical phenotypes of adults with BAV by clustering multidimensional clinical data, primarily echocardiographic parameters.
METHODS: We retrospectively included adults with echocardiographically confirmed BAV at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2016 and December 2024. Data from the first echocardiographic examination and contemporaneous clinical records were extracted, and nine continuous and three categorical variables were entered into a two-step clustering model. Continuous and categorical variables were compared across clusters using the Kruskal-Wallis H test and chi-square test, respectively, followed by pairwise comparisons. The stability of the four-cluster solution was assessed using 100 bootstrap resamples; agreement was quantified with the adjusted Rand index (ARI) and Jaccard coefficients. Clustering was also repeated after separately excluding sex and valve dysfunction to assess the influence of these key variables on cluster structure.
RESULTS: A total of 6977 patients with echocardiographically diagnosed BAV were included. The median age was 53.0 years (interquartile range, 40.0-61.0), and 70.0% were men. Two-step clustering identified four clinical phenotypes that differed significantly in valve morphology, valvular dysfunction, aortic dimensions, left-heart remodeling, cardiac function, and surgical interventions (all p < 0.001): Cluster 1, a predominantly male, regurgitation-predominant phenotype with left ventricular dilatation; Cluster 2, a predominantly male, stenosis-predominant phenotype with concentric hypertrophy; Cluster 3, a male phenotype with no or mild valve dysfunction; and Cluster 4, a female phenotype characterized mainly by no or mild valve dysfunction with a tendency toward stenosis. The proportion undergoing subsequ

candidates.title: Association between hemoglobin A1c levels and coronary flow reserve in angina with nonobstructive coronary arteries: a retrospective observational study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) measures chronic glycemic levels, and its elevation is associated with vascular endothelial dysfunction and microcirculatory impairment, contributing to increased cardiovascular risk. In the assessment of angina with nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA), coronary flow reserve (CFR) reflects vasodilatory capacity of the coronary microvasculature and is associated with adverse cardiovascular events, whereas IMR quantifies microvascular resistance during hyperemia. However, the association between HbA1c levels and invasive microvascular indices in ANOCA remains unclear.
METHODS: This study included 104 patients with ANOCA who underwent invasive coronary physiological assessment. CFR and IMR were measured using the thermodilution method. Associations between admission clinical parameters, including demographic characteristics and laboratory variables (particularly HbA1c), and CFR or IMR were examined using univariate and multivariate analyses.
RESULTS: The study population had a mean age of 65.8 ± 13.0 years, 50.0% were male, mean HbA1c was 6.0 ± 0.7%, mean CFR was 4.3 ± 2.4, and mean IMR was 14.2 ± 8.8. Multivariate analysis demonstrated a significant negative association between HbA1c and CFR (β = -0.250, 95% CI: -1.619 to - 0.155, P = 0.018). In contrast, no significant association was observed between HbA1c and IMR.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with ANOCA, higher HbA1c levels were independently associated with reduced CFR but not with IMR. These findings suggest a potential association between chronic glycemic status and coronary vasodilatory function in ANOCA.

candidates.title: Late Discordance Between Right Ventricular Fractional Area Change and Free-Wall Longitudinal Strain After Cardiac Surgery Including Tricuspid Annuloplasty.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: This single-center retrospective study assessed preoperative-to-late postoperative changes in right ventricular (RV) indices in patients undergoing cardiac surgery including tricuspid annuloplasty, predominantly with concomitant mitral valve surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 63 patients with paired preoperative and late postoperative echocardiography after tricuspid annuloplasty. RV fractional area change (RVFAC), RV free-wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), and tissue Doppler tricuspid annular peak systolic velocity (S') were compared over time. RVFAC >35% and absolute RVFWLS >20% were classified as preserved.
RESULTS: Late echocardiography was performed at a median of 47 months. No statistically significant within-patient change in RVFAC was detected (37.9% to 37.4%; Hodges-Lehmann estimate, -1.0 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.0 to +0.7; p = 0.231), whereas RVFWLS decreased from 19.2% to 15.7% (median within-patient change, -3.1 percentage points; Hodges-Lehmann estimate, -3.7 percentage points; 95% CI, -5.3 to -2.3; p < 0.001); TAPSE and S' were also lower at late follow-up (both p < 0.001). At follow-up, 30 of 37 patients with preserved RVFAC had reduced RVFWLS.
CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing tricuspid annuloplasty, predominantly with concomitant mitral valve surgery, preserved RVFAC at late follow-up does not necessarily indicate preserved RV free-wall longitudinal deformation. RVFAC alone may be insufficient to characterize RV function at late postoperative follow-up in this setting.

candidates.title: Rethinking Left Ventricular Diastolic Dysfunction in Hypertension: The Interplay of Arterial Stiffness, Ventricular-Arterial Coupling, and Pulse Wave Velocity in HFpEF.
candidates.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for approximately half of heart failure cases and is closely associated with hypertension and left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD). This narrative review examines the relationship between diastolic function, arterial stiffness, and ventricular-arterial coupling in hypertensive heart disease. We summarize ventricular relaxation and filling and discuss echocardiographic measures, including E/e', left atrial volume, and left atrial reservoir strain, for assessing diastolic function and filling pressures. We then examine how aortic stiffening may increase late systolic load and contribute to ventricular remodeling and impaired relaxation. This review addresses four central questions: whether arterial stiffness represents an independent component of hypertensive left ventricular diastolic dysfunction; whether pulse wave velocity (PWV) is primarily a marker of vascular aging, ventricular afterload, or HFpEF risk; whether PWV provides incremental information beyond established echocardiographic markers; and how arterial stiffness could be integrated into contemporary HFpEF assessment. The available evidence supports arterial stiffness as a biologically plausible contributor to hypertensive ventricular remodeling and impaired diastolic reserve. However, current evidence does not establish echocardiographic global PWV (PWVg) as an independent diagnostic criterion or validated prognostic marker of clinical HFpEF. We therefore propose PWVg as a complementary, hypothesis-generating measure for vascular and ventricular phenotyping, to be interpreted alongside clinical assessment, natriuretic peptides, multiparametric echocardiography, and exercise or invasive hemodynamic testing when indicated.

candidates.title: [Surgical Case of Posterior Transposition of the Great Arteries with Bilateral Conus].
candidates.journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
candidates.abstract: A two-month-old girl presented with hyperpnea, a significant cardiac murmur, and severe hypoxemia. Transthoracic echocardiography at the referring hospital suggested congenital heart disease with highflow pulmonary hypertension, and she was referred to our institution for further evaluation. At our hospital, echocardiography demonstrated transposition of the great arteries (TGA) with a small ventricular septal defect (VSD), atrial septal defect, and patent ductus arteriosus. Detailed echocardiography revealed that the aorta was positioned slightly posterior and to the right of the pulmonary artery, with the presence of both subpulmonary and subaortic conus. The subaortic conus represented an atypical anatomical feature of posterior TGA. Based on these findings, a diagnosis of posterior TGA with bilateral conus was established. Aortic angiography demonstrated a Shaher type 9 pattern, in which the right coronary artery courses anterior to the aorta and the left coronary artery passes posterior to the pulmonary artery. At three months of age, she underwent an arterial switch operation. The Lecompte maneuver was not performed because the aorta was positioned posterior and to the right of the pulmonary artery (original Jatene procedure). An autologous pericardial patch was interposed along the left margin of the pulmonary artery bifurcation stump to shift the anastomotic site of the neo-pulmonary artery rightward, thereby preventing compression of the transferred coronary arteries. A small VSD intentionally left open as a fenestration in anticipation of a postoperative pulmonary hypertensive crisis. The postoperative course was uneventful.

candidates.title: Advanced Echocardiographic Phenotyping of Myocardial Recovery During VA-ECMO-A Scoping Review.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) provided temporary circulatory support in refractory cardiogenic shock but substantially altered ventricular preload, afterload, and native ejection. Consequently, conventional echocardiographic measurements obtained during support did not necessarily represent intrinsic myocardial contractility. This scoping review mapped conventional and advanced echocardiographic approaches used to characterize myocardial recovery and guide VA-ECMO liberation.
METHODS: PubMed, OpenAlex, and Crossref were searched from inception through September 20, 2026. Eligible studies included adults receiving VA-ECMO in whom echocardiography was used to assess myocardial recovery, flow-dependent cardiac performance, weaning readiness, decannulation outcomes, or transition to durable mechanical support. Citation searching supplemented the database searches. Study selection was reported according to PRISMA-ScR, and the search process was documented according to PRISMA-S. Data were synthesized descriptively because of substantial heterogeneity in populations, imaging protocols, flow-reduction strategies, and outcome definitions.
RESULTS: The searches identified 3,912 records, of which 2,834 remained after duplicate removal. Thirty-nine full-text reports were assessed, and 35 studies were included. Conventional measures, particularly left ventricular ejection fraction and left ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral, were frequently associated with successful weaning but were strongly influenced by ECMO-related loading conditions. Flow reduction commonly improved ejection fraction, longitudinal strain, native stroke output, and annular velocities without representing immediate biological myocardial recovery.
