candidates.title: Advancements in Artificial Intelligence for Enhanced Diagnosis and Prognosis in Cardiac CT: a Comprehensive Review and Future Perspectives.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Cardiovascular disease, with coronary artery disease (CAD) as its main culprit, remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Traditional diagnostic methods that focus on the degree of arterial narrowing (percent diameter stenosis, or %DS) can miss early signs of disease or the specific plaque features that indicate high risk. The purpose of this review is to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance the diagnostic and prognostic capabilities of cardiac computed tomography (CCT), and to address where AI can most meaningfully improve diagnostic accuracy, workflow efficiency, and patient care.
RECENT FINDINGS: AI is transforming cardiac CT across the entire imaging pathway. By applying AI algorithms, recent studies have refined the assessment of coronary artery calcium (CAC), improved plaque characterization, and detected subtle lesions that might evade traditional detection methods. AI further enables non-invasive assessment of ischemia (reduced blood flow), aids in the evaluation of myocardial infarction, analyzes adipose tissue surrounding the heart, improves image quality, and provides valuable prognostic insights for risk stratification. This comprehensive review explores the transformative potential of AI in cardiac CT, highlighting its role in accurate diagnosis, precise risk stratification, and personalized management of cardiovascular disease. Through collaboration between AI technology and clinical expertise, we envision a future where cardiac CT imaging is more powerful, efficient, and patient-centered, ultimately leading to improved outcomes in cardiovascular medicine. Continued standardization, external validation, and clinician education will be essential to realize this impact in routine practice.

candidates.title: Mitral valve disease in rheumatic heart disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid syndrome, and rheumatoid Arthritis.
candidates.abstract: Mitral valve disease occurs in rheumatic heart disease (RHD) and selected systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases, but similar lesions may have different underlying mechanisms. This structured narrative review examines epidemiological, mechanistic, imaging, and management evidence, distinguishing established pathways from incompletely validated mechanisms and hypotheses. In RHD, post-streptococcal valvulitis leads to fibrotic remodeling, commissural fusion, and chordal shortening, producing mitral stenosis, regurgitation, or mixed disease. A meta-analysis of 215,552 children and adolescents in endemic settings reported echocardiographically detected RHD in 24 per 1000. In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), typical findings include leaflet thickening, Libman-Sacks vegetations, and regurgitation; embolic complications may occur despite mild valve dysfunction. Among 508 clinically selected patients with SLE undergoing echocardiography, 27.4% had heart valve involvement and 11.2% had mitral involvement. Immunothrombotic mechanisms may contribute to these lesions, but direct validation in human valve tissue remains incomplete. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), a prospective cohort found an association with incident mitral regurgitation (adjusted hazard ratio 1.54, 95% confidence interval 1.32-1.81), but not mitral stenosis. Myocardial imaging findings do not establish a causal link to regurgitation. These findings support anatomy- and severity-based assessment in RHD, combined valvular and thromboembolic evaluation in SLE/APS, and assessment of conventional regurgitation mechanisms in RA. The framework informs clinical interpretation within existing guidelines, while proposed disease-specific mechanisms require further validation.

candidates.title: Off-pump subtotal pericardiectomy using ultrasonic aspirator in constrictive pericarditis.
candidates.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
candidates.abstract: A subtotal pericardiectomy was performed without the use of extracorporeal circulation due to the patient's advanced age and underlying liver cirrhosis. After exposure of the heart, both phrenic nerves were identified and carefully preserved. The pericardium was found to be massively calcified, with extensive involvement extending to the base of the aorta and the diaphragm. The pericardium was divided into multiple diamond-shaped sections, allowing controlled, stepwise resection and facilitating safe handling of the rigid, calcified tissue. Decortication was initiated at the right ventricle and proceeded gradually. The calcified pericardium was removed using a combination of an ultrasonic aspirator, a rongeur and electrocautery. Careful, controlled separation of the pericardium from the epicardium was performed throughout, addressing dense adhesions while preserving the underlying myocardium and epicardial vessels. The ultrasonic aspirator facilitated resection of the calcified tissue without harming the underlying structures. Resection was extended over the right atrium, right ventricle and anterior wall of the left ventricle up to the level of the phrenic nerves. Complete pericardiectomy was not achievable due to extensive adhesions and proximity to critical structures. Intraoperative echocardiographic imaging demonstrated immediate improvement in cardiac filling and function.

candidates.title: Sex Differences in the Association Between the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index and Coronary Lesion Severity in Acute Coronary Syndrome.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) correlates with increased coronary artery disease (CAD) prevalence and severity in acute coronary syndrome (ACS). The aim of this study was to evaluate the influence of sex on SII and its association with coronary stenosis in ACS.
METHODS: A total of 130 patients with ACS, who had performed coronary angiography, were enrolled. Gensini Score (GS) was used to reflect the degree of coronary stenosis. The association of SII and GS were studied.
RESULTS: The mean values of SII and GS were significantly higher (p = 0.048 and 0.001, respectively) in male individuals compared with female counterparts. There was a significant correlation between SII and GS (r = 0.306, p = 0.006) in male participants. However, the positive correlation between SII and GS was not found in female subjects. SII was independently associated with GS (B = 0.030, p = 0.007) after controlling for age, smoking, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in male participants. LDL-C (B = 11.741, p = 0.003), smoking (B = 39.018, p = 0.016) and age (B = 1.139, p = 0.030), but not SII (B = 0.027, p = 0.101) were found to be independently correlated with the degree of coronary stenosis in females.
CONCLUSIONS: SII was a associated marker for evaluating the extent of coronary lesions in male subjects with ACS, but not in female counterparts.

candidates.title: Suspected donor-vessel ischemia in a collateral-dependent right coronary artery occlusion presenting as a de Winter-like pattern with inferior ST-segment elevation: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The de Winter electrocardiographic pattern is a recognized equivalent of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and is most commonly associated with acute left anterior descending artery ischemia. Its coexistence with overt ST-segment elevation in another territory is uncommon and may create uncertainty in culprit-vessel identification. In patients with multivessel coronary disease and collateral-dependent myocardium, acute compromise of a donor coronary circulation may produce simultaneous but apparently discordant ECG manifestations.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 48-year-old man presented with worsening chest pain. The initial ECG showed a de Winter-like anterior morphology, characterized by upsloping J-point ST-segment depression followed by tall, symmetric T waves in leads V2-V4, together with ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVF. Urgent coronary angiography was delayed for approximately 4 h because the patient initially declined the procedure; aspirin, ticagrelor, and heparin were administered during this interval. At angiography, the left coronary circulation retained TIMI grade 3 antegrade flow but contained a critical proximal-to-mid left anterior descending artery lesion and severe distal left circumflex artery stenosis. The mid right coronary artery was completely occluded, with a blunt proximal stump and Rentrop grade 2 left-to-right collateral filling, strongly favoring a pre-existing RCA occlusion with chronic characteristics. Because the right coronary lesion was considered unlikely to be the acute culprit, emergency percutaneous coronary intervention was directed to the left anterior descending and distal left circumflex arteries. Inferior ST-segment elevation decreased markedly but incompletely after left coronary revascularization, with residual elevation most evident in lead III. The right coronary occlusion was successfully treated during a staged procedure 4 days later, after which the residual inferior ST-segment elevation decreased

candidates.title: ECT/18F-FDG PET-CT for myocardial viability assessment during VA-ECMO support in AMI-related cardiogenic shock: a case series and literature review.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Weaning patients from veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) after acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) depends on whether the injured left ventricle can recover. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is often impractical during ECMO support. Nuclear imaging may help, but its role in this unstable setting remains poorly defined.
METHODS: We report six consecutive male patients with AMI-CS and difficulty weaning from VA-ECMO who underwent myocardial perfusion emission computed tomography (ECT) and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission computed tomography (18F-FDG PET-CT) during active support. The case series is used as a clinical entry point for a focused literature review of ECT/SPECT and FDG PET in myocardial viability assessment after myocardial infarction.
RESULTS: Imaging was completed in all six patients 12-22 days after ECMO initiation. No transfer- or scan-related adverse event was documented in the available record. Four patients had large estimated left ventricular perfusion defects (54%, 63%, 66%, and 59%) and were managed toward left ventricular assist device support or heart transplantation. One patient with a 41% defect died after withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy because of hepatic failure. One patient with a small estimated defect (4%) was successfully weaned. Prior studies indicate that FDG uptake and perfusion-metabolism mismatch are associated with regional functional recovery after revascularization, but patient-level decisions depend on revascularization, ventricular remodeling, end-organ function, and whether imaging results can be acted on safely.
CONCLUSIONS: ECT/18F-FDG PET-CT was feasible in this small VA-ECMO case series and provided perfusion and metabolic information when MRI was impractical. The evidence supports its use as an adjunct to clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and end-organ assessment, not as a stand-alone threshold for weaning, LVAD, or transplantation de

candidates.title: [Diagnosis of amyloidosis].
candidates.abstract: Given the availability of highly effective treatment options, early diagnosis of cardiac amyloidosis is more important than ever. In many cases, the diagnosis can now be made non-invasively, provided that clinical suspicion is raised in a timely manner. Warning signs such as heart failure, bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, spinal stenosis, or an abnormal voltage-to-mass ratio on the ECG should prompt further investigation. Echocardiography allows for the detection of typical morphological and functional changes, while the simultaneous exclusion of monoclonal gammopathy via three simple laboratory tests determines the subsequent diagnostic pathway. If the laboratory findings are normal, SPECT/CT enables a non-invasive diagnosis of ATTR cardiomyopathy; however, if the imaging is negative and suspicion persists, a biopsy remains indicated. A cardiac MRI is particularly valuable when echocardiographic findings are inconclusive or there is suspicion of AL cardiomyopathy. New diagnostic approaches based on extracardiac manifestations and incidental findings on MRI also open the possibility of identifying affected individuals even before the onset of cardiac symptoms. Amyloid-binding PET tracers show promise for the future non-invasive diagnosis of both forms of amyloidosis, but still require prospective validation studies.

candidates.title: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement in bicuspid versus tricuspid aortic valves among patients with mixed aortic valve disease.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mixed aortic valve disease (MAVD), defined as the coexistence of significant aortic stenosis (AS) and aortic regurgitation (AR), presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Prior studies rarely distinguished bicuspid valve morphology in MAVD populations, and no study has evaluated long-term transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes between bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) patients in this setting. The aim is to investigate the clinical outcomes of BAV versus TAV morphology in patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR.
METHODS: Between March 2013 and December 2024, 610 MAVD patients undergoing TAVR were included. Patients with severe AS and concomitant presence of moderate or more severe aortic regurgitation were defined as the MAVD. Clinical outcomes, functional status and echocardiography were followed and compared.
RESULTS: A total of 610 patients were included in this study, 220 (36.1%) of whom were BAV morphology. BAV patients were younger (73 vs. 75 years, p < 0.001) and had a lower Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score (3.47% vs. 4.15%, p < 0.001) compared to TAV patients. The five-year mortality rate was lower in bicuspid than tricuspid patients (10.5% vs. 18.7%, log-rank p = 0.014), while Cox regression analysis did not indicate BAV as an independent predictor of five-year all-cause mortality after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] 0.75, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.47-1.22, p = 0.253). During the one-year follow-up after procedure, BAV patients exhibited a greater increase in AVA and LVEF (p for interaction = 0.012 and 0.011, respectively), and a greater reduction in mean gradient and peak velocity (both p for interaction < 0.001). Meanwhile, similar left ventricular reverse remodelling was found during follow-up (both p for trend < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In MAVD patients undergoing TAVR, bicuspid and tricuspid valve morphologies demonstrated comparable long-term clinical outcomes. BAV p

candidates.title: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the incidence and mortality of Takotsubo syndrome in Sweden, a report from the SWEDEHEART registry.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is often triggered by intense emotional or physical stress, with symptoms closely resembling those of acute myocardial infarction and heart failure. The COVID-19 pandemic caused unprecedented psychological, social, and economic stress, with TTS incidence and mortality either increasing or remaining stable. Previous studies have relied on single- or multicenter data, lacking the scope to provide national-level insights. This study aimed to fill the gap by investigating the incidence and outcomes of TTS across Sweden during two distinct periods: the pre-pandemic period (January 2015 to March 2020) and the pandemic period (April 2020 to December 2022).
METHODS: Using the nationwide Swedish Coronary Angiography and Angioplasty Registry, we assessed the incidence rate (IR) for all patients with TTS referred for coronary angiography in Sweden. We calculated incidence rate ratios (IRRs) both before and during the pandemic using quasi-Poisson regression, adjusted for age and sex. We evaluated 30-day and 1-year mortality using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, accounting for clustering within hospitals.
RESULTS: We identified 3,180 patients hospitalized with TTS during the study period: 69% (2,189) pre-pandemic and 31% (991) during the pandemic. The incidence of TTS was 10% lower during the pandemic compared to the pre-pandemic period (IRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.84-0.97, P = 0.008). The cohort's crude all-cause mortality rate was 2.73% at 30 days and 6.10% at 1 year, with no significant difference at 30 days (adjusted HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.69-1.78, P = 0.642) or one year (adjusted HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.75-1.46, P = 0.780). Compared with studies in other countries where incidence increased or remained unchanged, COVID-19 incidence was similar across the matching periods.
CONCLUSIONS: This nationwide observational study found a lower incidence of TTS during the pandemic compared to the pre-pandemic period, while mortality rates remained

candidates.title: Body-Size Indexation of Left Atrial Volume in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: Retrospective Reclassification and E/e' Concordance.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether associations between body mass index (BMI) and left atrial (LA) size differ when LA volume is expressed as absolute volume, indexed to body surface area (BSA), or indexed to height squared, and whether discordant classification is associated with E/e' in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).
METHODS: This retrospective observational study linked MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-IV-ECHO. The complete-indexation cohort comprised 1663 adults with a documented heart failure diagnosis, left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%, and required body-size and LA measurements. Multivariable models evaluated BMI associations with absolute LA volume, LAV/BSA, and LAV/height2. Discordance was defined as BSA-normal but height2-enlarged; adjusted E/e' was compared with the group normal by both methods.
RESULTS: BMI was positively associated with absolute LA volume (β = 0.345; 95% CI, 0.124-0.567), inversely associated with LAV/BSA (β = -0.329; 95% CI, -0.456 to -0.203), and positively associated with LAV/height2 (β = 0.156; 95% CI, 0.077-0.236). Discordant classification occurred in 389 of 1663 participants (23.4%). Adjusted E/e' was 1.630 higher (95% CI, 0.738-2.522) than in participants normal by both methods. The absolute reclassification proportion decreased to 9.6% with an alternative published height2 threshold.
CONCLUSION: Body-size normalization materially changed apparent LA enlargement in this selected HFpEF population. BSA-normal/height2-enlarged classification was associated with higher E/e', a noninvasive filling-related marker, but was threshold-dependent. These findings do not establish diagnostic superiority or prognostic benefit.

candidates.title: Longitudinal Remodeling and Network Architecture of the Proximal Aorta in Children and Adolescents With Marfan Syndrome.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortopathy is the main cardiovascular manifestation of Marfan syndrome, but the joint evolution of the different segments of the proximal aorta during pediatric growth remains insufficiently characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate longitudinal remodeling and the interindividual and intraindividual architecture of the proximal aorta in children and adolescents with Marfan syndrome.
METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of data from the Pediatric Heart Network Marfan trial. Participants aged <18 years at randomization with acceptable echocardiograms obtained at baseline and at 6, 12, 24, and 36 months were included. The aortic annulus, sinuses of Valsalva, sinotubular junction, and ascending aorta were analyzed using absolute diameters and Z-scores. Partial correlation networks were estimated, separating interindividual and intraindividual components. Uncertainty was assessed using participant-level bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: A total of 515 participants were included; 445 (86.4%) had five acceptable visits. From baseline to 36 months, all absolute diameters increased, whereas Z-scores decreased (-0.688 to -0.454; all p < 0.001). Exploratory age-stratified analyses showed larger decreases among participants aged 6-11 years. The interindividual network was stronger than the intraindividual network (global strength 1.783 vs 1.020; difference 0.763; 95% CI 0.526-1.101; p < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses using inverse-probability weighting and an alternative Pediatric Heart Network Z-score system showed the same overall pattern of declining Z-scores.
CONCLUSIONS: The proximal aorta shows a multisegment architecture in which organization across patients is stronger than within-patient coordination of change. Network findings complement, but do not replace, serial measurement of individual aortic levels, and their prognostic value requires independent validation.

candidates.title: Left Atrial Strain and Left Atrio-Ventricular Coupling in Heart Failure Patients with Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Wild-Type Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Wild-type transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTRwt-CA) is a cardiomyopathy characterized by myocardial and atrial stiffening.
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess left atrial (LA) function and left atrio-ventricular coupling index (LACI) in heart failure (HF) patients with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and evaluate their ability to discriminate ATTRwt-CA from non-amyloid LVH.
METHODS: We conducted a case-control study including 50 patients with ATTRwt-CA and 50 HF patients with hypertensive heart disease. LA reservoir strain (LARS), LA contraction strain (PACS), LA stiffness index (LASI), LA reservoir work (LAWr) and LACI have been measured. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed for interventricular septal thickness (IVS), relative wall thickness (RWT), age, sex, coronary heart disease (CAD) to mitigate confounding.
RESULTS: Before matching,  significant differences in IVS, RWT, age, sex, and CAD rates were observed between cases and controls. After PSM, LA functional indices remained significantly impaired in CA patients compared to controls. In the multivariate analysis, only LARS and LASI were independently associated with ATTRwt-CA. A LASI > 1.57 (AUC 0.87) and a PACS  ≤  6.0% (AUC 0.79) demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for identifying ATTRwt-CA, with reduced LARS ( ≤  14.0%) also providing significant discrimination. Incorporating LASI  into the AMYLI (AUC 0.91) and IWT scores (AUC 0.89)  significantly enhances overall diagnostic accuracy for ATTRwt-CA detection.
CONCLUSION: LA function and the atrio-ventricular coupling are more impaired in ATTRwt-CA patients compared to patients with HF alone; especially LARS and LASI are independent predictor for ATTRwt-CA and should be assessed in HF patients with LVH to detect CA.

candidates.title: Bicuspid Aortic Valve With Preserved Ejection Fraction: One-Year Changes in Ventricular and Atrial Mechanics.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Left ventricular (LV) dysfunction in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) disease may precede ejection fraction (EF) decline. We assessed 1-year changes in LV global longitudinal strain (GLS), left atrial (LA) strain and myocardial work in BAV with preserved EF.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 82 adults with BAV and sinus rhythm who had preserved LVEF (≥50%) at two echocardiograms 363 ± 15 days apart without interim surgery; 40 age- and sex-matched controls with tricuspid aortic valves were imaged once. Primary outcomes were changes in absolute GLS and LA reservoir strain (LASr); myocardial work, corrected for the transaortic gradient in aortic stenosis, was exploratory. Reader reproducibility was tested on stored images.
RESULTS: At baseline, patients had lower absolute GLS (17.8 ± 2.8% vs. 21.8 ± 1.0%) and LASr (38.5 ± 5.2% vs. 40.8 ± 3.4%) than controls (p < 0.001 and p = 0.004). At 1 year, mean LVEF and LV volumes did not change significantly, whereas absolute GLS decreased by 0.8% points (95% CI 0.5-1.1) and LASr by 2.4 points (1.7-3.0; both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Gradient-corrected global work index decreased by 47 mmHg% (27-68). The GLS decrease exceeded the intra-observer minimal detectable change in 22 patients (27%), versus an increase in 4 (5%). The GLS change was not significantly associated with valve lesion type or severity.
CONCLUSION: In selected patients with BAV who maintained preserved LVEF without valve or aortic surgery, LV GLS and LA reservoir strain decreased slightly over 1 year. Their clinical significance requires validation with longitudinal controls and test-retest data.

candidates.title: A rare late presentation of restrictive cor triatriatum sinister in a 14-year-old male mimicking refractory asthma.
candidates.abstract: Cor triatriatum sinister is an exceptionally rare congenital cardiac anomaly [1]. While restrictive forms are typically present in infancy or early childhood, survival into adolescence with a 2-3 mm fenestration is unusual [2, 3]. We report a 14-year-old male, misdiagnosed with refractory asthma for years, who presented with palpitations. Imaging and catheterisation revealed severe post-capillary pulmonary hypertension with echocardiographic evidence of right-sided chamber dilatation, D-shaped left ventricular configuration, moderate tricuspid regurgitation, and an estimated pulmonary artery pressure of 85 mmHg. Cardiac catheterisation showed PA pressure of 50/30 mmHg (mean 39 mmHg), PCWP of 28 mmHg, Qp/Qs of 1.14, and a favourable PVR/SVR ratio of 0.12, indicating reversibility. Successful surgical resection of a calcified membrane was performed via right anterolateral thoracotomy. This case underscores the importance of considering cor triatriatum sinister in adolescents with unexplained respiratory symptoms or wheezing and highlights the value of correlating echocardiographic evidence of obstruction with invasive haemodynamic assessment before surgery [4, 5].

candidates.title: Clot in Transit.
candidates.abstract: Clot in transit, defined as a mobile right heart thrombus, is a rare but life-threatening manifestation of venous thromboembolism. Its presence in acute pulmonary embolism is associated with high mortality and hemodynamic instability. Diagnosis relies primarily on echocardiography, with adjunctive roles for computed tomography and cardiac magnetic resonance. Management remains challenging due to the absence of randomized trials. Treatment options include anticoagulation alone, systemic thrombolysis, surgical embolectomy, and catheter-based interventions, with outcomes favoring active reperfusion in unstable patients. Multidisciplinary decision-making is essential, and ongoing research aims to clarify optimal strategies to improve survival in this high-risk population.

candidates.title: Prognostic value of Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio after percutaneous coronary intervention.
candidates.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) physiological indices have prognostic relevance. Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (μQFR) enables wire-free, rapid, single-view functional assessment, yet its long-term prognostic value after PCI remains incompletely established.
AIMS: We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of post-PCI μQFR for long-term adverse outcomes.
METHODS: This prespecified subgroup analysis of the FAVOR III China trial included 3,825 patients. All PCI-treated vessels with a reference diameter ≥2.5 mm and 50-90% diameter stenosis were analysed for offline post-PCI μQFR. The primary endpoint was 5-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; including death from any cause, myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven revascularisation).
RESULTS: Post-PCI μQFR was successfully analysed in 4,196 vessels from 3,455 patients, with similar distributions between the randomised treatment groups. At 5 years, a low post-PCI μQFR was associated with a higher incidence of MACE compared with the intermediate and high post-PCI μQFR tertiles (23.1% vs 19.0% vs 17.2%; p=0.001). Using the highest tertile (μQFR>0.95) as a reference, adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) were 1.08 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.87-1.34) for the intermediate tertile (0.92-0.95) and 1.30 (95% CI: 1.06-1.60) for the lowest tertile (μQFR ≤0.91). Using a receiver operating characteristic-derived cutoff, MACE occurred more frequently in patients with post-PCI μQFR <0.94 (22.3% vs 17.4%, aHR 1.23, 95% CI: 1.04-1.47; p=0.02) than in those with post-PCI μQFR ≥0.94. No significant interaction was observed between treatment strategy and post-PCI μQFR (p for interaction=0.23).
CONCLUSIONS: Post-PCI μQFR distributions were similar between treatment groups, but lower values were associated with higher 5-year adverse event risk without significant treatment interaction. Its limited binary discrimination supports use as a continuous metric for post-PCI physiological risk stratific

candidates.title: Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio.
candidates.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient).
AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment.
METHODS: Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell's C-index.
RESULTS: Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04794868).

candidates.title: A randomised non-inferiority trial of CCTA guidance versus IVUS guidance for PCI: rationale and design of the P4 clinical trial.
candidates.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
candidates.abstract: Intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes compared with angiography-guided PCI. Contemporary coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides comprehensive assessment of coronary anatomy, plaque characteristics, vessel dimensions, calcification, and lesion-specific physiology, enabling detailed procedural planning before catheterisation. The Precise Procedural and PCI Plan (P4) trial is a prospective, international, multicentre, randomised, open-label trial with blinded endpoint adjudication designed to determine whether a comprehensive CCTA-guided PCI strategy is non-inferior to intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes. Approximately 1,100 patients with chronic coronary syndromes or stabilised acute coronary syndrome, at least one coronary stenosis >70%, and fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA ≤0.80 are enrolled. Following central core laboratory confirmation of anatomical and physiological eligibility, patients are randomised 1:1 to CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI. Patients assigned to CCTA-guided PCI undergo standardised procedural planning and virtual PCI simulation, with CCTA integrated into the catheterisation laboratory using computed tomography-fluoroscopy synchronisation for intraprocedural guidance. In the IVUS-guided arm, PCI is performed with mandatory pre- and post-PCI IVUS assessment. The primary endpoint is target vessel failure at 12 months, defined as the composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven target vessel revascularisation. P4 will determine whether comprehensive, non-invasive CCTA-guided PCI planning is non-inferior to IVUS-guided PCI regarding 12-month target vessel failure while potentially improving procedural efficiency and standardisation. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05253677).

candidates.title: Distinct Doppler echocardiographic patterns of elevated left ventricular filling pressure in acute decompensated heart failure and AMI-related cardiogenic shock: a simultaneous Doppler-hemodynamic study.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Doppler echocardiography supports noninvasive hemodynamic assessment, but its interpretation may vary across acute heart failure syndromes. We compared Doppler filling patterns and their relationship with pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) and acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single-center observational study included 61 patients with ADHF (n = 34) or AMI-CS (n = 27) who underwent contemporaneous echocardiographic and invasive hemodynamic assessment. Transmitral inflow, pulmonary venous flow, and tissue Doppler indices were compared between groups and analyzed in relation to PCWP. Exploratory ROC analyses assessed discrimination of PCWP ≥ 18 mmHg.
RESULTS: Patients with ADHF had greater cardiac chamber enlargement and higher mean PCWP than those with AMI-CS (24.7 ± 8.4 vs. 18.0 ± 5.4 mmHg; p < 0.001). ADHF was characterized by higher E/A (2.8 ± 1.2 vs. 1.3 ± 1.2; p < 0.001), lower pulmonary venous S/D (0.7 ± 0.5 vs. 1.1 ± 0.5; p < 0.01), and higher average E/e' (21.0 ± 7.3 vs. 12.5 ± 4.7; p < 0.001). Deceleration time did not differ significantly. Average and septal E/e' correlated with PCWP in the pooled cohort but not within either group separately. Septal E/e' yielded AUCs of 0.868 (95% CI, 0.722-1.000) in ADHF and 0.762 (95% CI, 0.511-1.000) in AMI-CS.
CONCLUSIONS: ADHF and AMI-CS exhibit distinct Doppler filling profiles alongside differences in invasive filling pressure and cardiac remodeling. These findings support contextual interpretation of Doppler indices during bedside hemodynamic assessment of critically ill patients. The diagnostic value of syndrome-specific interpretation requires independent validation.

candidates.title: Prognostic value of cardiovascular magnetic resonance in acute myocarditis: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis of late gadolinium enhancement and narrative literature review of parametric mapping.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Limited data exist on the prognostic value of parametric mapping and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) in patients with acute myocarditis (AM). This meta-analysis aimed to investigate the prognostic value of LGE as assessed by using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with AM, including more recent evidence. Additionally, the prognostic value of CMR parametric mapping was narratively reviewed.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The systematic search was conducted in the PubMed and Scopus databases from inception to January 17, 2026 (PubMed) and January 20th 2026 (Scopus). 1296 records were found through the search. Finally, sixteen studies were included in this systematic review. Thirteen studies were included in the meta-analysis on association between LGE and clinical outcomes in AM. The composite endpoint was defined as MACE and/or one of the following endpoints: all-cause death, heart failure decompensation requiring hospitalization, heart transplantation, and recurrent AM. MACE was defined as a composite of cardiovascular death (including sudden death), sustained ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, complete atrioventricular heart block requiring a pacemaker, and cardiogenic shock. Five studies were reviewed for the prognostic value of parametric mapping parameters. After initial calculations, it appeared that studies using broader composite endpoints than only MACE introduced substantial heterogeneity. Therefore, we have additionally conducted analysis incorporating only eight studies with MACE as the endpoint.
RESULTS: The presence of LGE was associated with higher odds of the composite endpoint. candidates.title: Low-kV high-pitch one-scan aortic and coronary CT angiography using dual-source photon-counting CT: comparison with separate acquisition strategies.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with aortic diseases, coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is performed for preoperative evaluation of coronary artery disease, often in combination with CT angiography of thoracic and abdominal aorta (CTAO) within the same examination. A dual-source photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) offers advantages including improved dose efficiency and reduction of electronic noise, which might help maintain image quality even at low tube voltages. This study aimed to compare a low-kV one-scan CCTA/CTAO protocol with a low-kV dedicated CCTA followed by a higher-kV CTAO acquisition (separate-scan) regarding radiation dose and image quality.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included 42 patients who underwent CCTA and CTAO using PCD-CT for preoperative CAD screening for aortic disease: 19 had separate-scan, 23 had one-scan CCTA and CTAO. Image quality for CCTA was assessed using a four-point scale (excellent, good, fair, non-diagnostic). Image quality for CTAO was assessed using a five-point scale (excellent, good, moderate, poor, non-diagnostic).
RESULTS: Radiation dose was significantly lower in the one-scan group compared to the separate-scan group (mean total dose-length product, 175.8 ± 71.1 vs. 769.4 ± 212.1 mGy·cm; P < 0.001). For CCTA, subjective image quality scores were comparable between the two groups (P = 0.537), although the separate-scan group showed significantly higher objective CNR compared to the one-scan group (P =0.025). For CTAO, the subjective image quality was significantly superior in the one-scan group (P < 0.01), despite comparable CNR between the groups (P = 0.13). The proportions of good or excellent ratings were 97.1% and 98.4% for CCTA, and 85.1% and 91.3% for CTAO in the separate-scan and one-scan groups, respectively.

candidates.title: A Low HALP score is an independent predictor of coronary artery ectasia: a retrospective comparative study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to determine whether the hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score is independently associated with the presence and angiographic severity of coronary artery ectasia (CAE), and to assess its potential role as a diagnostic inflammatory-nutritional biomarker in this population.
METHODS: In this retrospective, single-center study, the hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) scores were calculated using routine laboratory parameters obtained at admission. Logistic regression models were constructed to identify independent predictors of CAE. Furthermore, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to determine the diagnostic performance of the HALP score, and the association between the HALP score and the angiographic extent of CAE was evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 628 patients (290 CAE, 338 controls), the median HALP score was significantly lower in the CAE group (4.14 vs. 4.99, p < 0.001). Multivariate analysis identified a lower HALP score as an independent predictor of CAE (OR: 0.752, 95% CI: 0.655-0.865, p < 0.001). A HALP score of 4.569 predicted CAE with 60.1% sensitivity and 57.2% specificity (AUC: 0.650). The score was not associated with the angiographic extent of CAE (p = 0.461).
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, a low HALP score is significantly and independently associated with the presence of coronary artery ectasia in patients without obstructive coronary artery disease, reflecting the underlying systemic inflammatory and nutritional milieu. This easily obtainable index may serve as a useful complementary biomarker for assessing inflammatory burden in CAE patients, although further large-scale prospective studies are warranted to confirm its prognostic and clinical utility.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. This study is a retrospective observational analysis and does not report the results of a health care intervention.

candidates.title: Disease Burden and Mortality of Ischemic Heart Disease in China from 2008 to 2036.
candidates.journal: Journal of epidemiology and global health
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: To examine long-term trends and population subgroup differences in ischemic heart disease (IHD) mortality and disease burden in China from 2008 to 2021, and to project future trends to inform targeted prevention.
METHODS: Using the China Cause-of-Death Surveillance Dataset (2008-2021), we calculated crude mortality rate (CMR), age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), potential years of life lost (PYLL), and potential years of life lost rate (PYLLR). Temporal trends were quantified using Joinpoint regression, with results expressed as the average annual percentage change (AAPC). Age, period, and cohort effects were assessed with an age-period-cohort (APC) model. ASMR from 2022 to 2036 were forecasted by ARIMA model.
RESULTS: In 2008, the CMR and ASMR for IHD in China was 70.98/100,000 and 79.32/100,000; In 2021, the CMR and ASMR was 143.70/100,000 and 89.12/100,000. From 2008 to 2021, the overall ASMR trend showed no statistically significant change (AAPC = 0.75%, P = 0.63), whereas PYLLR rose significantly (AAPC = 2.01, P < 0.001). IHD ASMR and PYLLR were higher in males than females (P < 0.001), in rural than urban (P < 0.001), and in the central region than eastern region and western region (P < 0.001). APC analysis identified age effect as the predominant driver of IHD mortality risk. ARIMA projections indicated that IHD ASMR would remain largely stable through 2036.
CONCLUSION: China's substantial IHD burden demands prioritized primary prevention targeting younger populations, older adults, males, and rural residents. Multisectoral IHD risk-factor interventions should be integrated into national health policy to curb the rising burden.

candidates.title: Efficacy and Safety of Evogliptin in Mild to Moderate Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis: The EVOID-AS Trial Rationale and Study Design.
candidates.abstract: The only treatment of severe aortic stenosis (AS) is aortic valve replacement. No medical therapy has been proven effective for preventing or delaying AS progression despite several clinical trials. The EVOID-AS trial is designed to evaluate the efficacy of evogliptin, a dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitor, at retarding the progression of aortic valve calcification and AS hemodynamic severity in patients with mild to moderate AS. In this trial, 580 patients with mild or moderate native calcific AS at 40+ clinical sites across the United States and Canada will be randomized in a 1:1 allocation to receive either evogliptin 10 mg or placebo once daily orally for 2 years. Clinical follow-up visits are scheduled at 3-month intervals; transthoracic echocardiography, aortic valve computed tomography calcium score, and laboratory testing are obtained at baseline, 1-year, and 2-year study visits. The primary end point is change in aortic valve calcification as measured by cardiac computed tomography at 2 years of therapy. Secondary end points are progression of AS hemodynamic severity by echocardiography during 2 years of therapy and time to aortic valve intervention. Secondary safety end points include incidence and severity of treatment-emergent or serious adverse events. Enrollment began in June 2022, and the study is expected to be completed in 2028. EVOID-AS is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized medical trial to modify the progression of calcific AS. This trial will contribute to the critical unmet clinical need of identifying an effective medical therapy to prevent or to delay the progression of AS. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05143177.

candidates.title: Ultrasound-based assessment of cardiac and hepatic dysfunction: current status and future directions.
candidates.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a systemic syndrome in which venous congestion and impaired perfusion can produce clinically important hepatic dysfunction. The term cardiohepatic syndrome (CHS) describes this bidirectional interaction, but cardiac and hepatic abnormalities are still often evaluated in parallel rather than as a connected hemodynamic process. Ultrasound is uniquely suited to an integrated assessment because it can characterize cardiac structure and function, systemic venous congestion, hepatic hemodynamics, tissue stiffness, and treatment-related change at the bedside. Conventional transthoracic echocardiography remains the foundation of evaluation, while three-dimensional echocardiography and speckle-tracking techniques improve quantification of right ventricular, atrial, and subclinical myocardial dysfunction. Abdominal Doppler ultrasound, venous congestion scoring, and liver elastography add complementary information, although liver stiffness must be interpreted cautiously because congestion, inflammation, cholestasis, and fibrosis can produce overlapping signals. Artificial intelligence may improve acquisition, measurement reproducibility, and multimodal data integration, but external validation and transparent reporting remain essential. This review summarizes contemporary evidence and proposes a practical, sequential pathway that combines echocardiography, venous Doppler findings, liver stiffness, laboratory biomarkers, and dynamic reassessment after decongestion. The central clinical principle is that CHS should be evaluated as a time-varying cardiohepatic phenotype rather than diagnosed from a single cardiac, hepatic, or biochemical measurement.

candidates.title: Hepatic steatosis assessed by transient elastography in patients with significant coronary artery disease: a cross-sectional study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and coronary artery disease (CAD) share metabolic risk factors, it remains unclear whether the anatomical severity of CAD predicts the severity of hepatic steatosis or fibrosis. This study aimed to estimate MASLD prevalence using FibroScan® in patients with angiographically confirmed significant CAD and generate preliminary effect size estimates for associations between metabolic parameters and angiographic severity (SYNTAX score) with MASLD severity.
METHODS: In this pilot cross-sectional study, we enrolled 55 consecutive patients with ≥ 70% coronary stenosis undergoing angiography at Farshchian Hospital, Hamadan, Iran (2018-2019). All participants underwent abdominal ultrasound and transient elastography (FibroScan®) for controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) within four weeks post-discharge. CAD severity was quantified using the SYNTAX score. Although modest in size (n = 55), post-hoc power analysis confirmed 98.7% power to detect the primary BMI-S3 steatosis association but only 12.3% power for SYNTAX-MASLD analyses.
RESULTS: Participants were predominantly male (61.8%) with mean age 61.1 ± 8.9 years. FibroScan® detected hepatic steatosis in 76.4% of patients that significantly higher than ultrasound detection (52.7%, P < 0.001). Critically, 50% of ultrasound-normal patients had steatosis by CAP. Severe steatosis (S3) occurred exclusively in patients with BMI ≥ 25 kg/m² (P = 0.002; 98.7% power). No significant association emerged between SYNTAX score severity (low/intermediate vs. high) and severe steatosis (35.3% vs. 25.0%; P = 0.570) or advanced fibrosis (2.0% vs. 0%; P = 0.927); however, the 12.3% power for this analysis renders findings inconclusive rather than evidence of true null effect.
CONCLUSIONS: In this study, MASLD prevalence was high and strongly associated with elevated BMI, while SYNTAX score associations could not be reliably

candidates.title: [Electrocardiographic signs of coronary occlusion not meeting STEMI criteria].
candidates.abstract: The authors describe the electrocardiographic signs of coronary occlusion that do not fall within the STEMI category. Since immediate coronary angiography is required for these patients as well, the ECG signs being presented have great clinical significance. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(44): 1759-1763.

candidates.title: Improvement in mitral regurgitation after alcohol septal ablation in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The primary mechanism of mitral regurgitation (MR) in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral leaflets due to septal hypertrophy narrowing the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), influencing leaflet movement and closure. Among patients undergoing alcohol septal ablation (ASA), the impact on- and underlying mechanism of MR remains less studied. The aim was to determine the prevalence of MR and changes in MR severity after ASA and analyze echocardiographic (ECHO) parameters associated with MR changes.
METHODS: All patients who underwent ASA at Karolinska University Hospital in Sweden, 2009-2021 (follow-up until 2025), were included in this retrospective cohort study. ECHO parameters were collected before ASA, at 1-year follow-up and at the latest follow-up registered. To evaluate differences in continuous values, Kruskal-Wallis test was used, and for categorical values, Fischer's exact test was used.
RESULTS: 154 patients were included (mean follow-up 4.0 ± 3.9 years). 14% (n = 21) had at least moderate MR at baseline, of which 90% (n = 19) improved to mild MR or less. The patients with improved (n = 19, 12%) or unchanged (n = 128, 83%) grade of MR showed greater reduction of LVOT peak pressure gradients (improved MR: 137.5 to 4.8 mmHg, unchanged MR: 57.0 to 25.0 mmHg) between baseline and last follow-up, compared with patients with increased MR grade (n = 7, 4.5%, 57.0 to 51.0 mmHg, p = 0.003).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with at least moderate MR before ASA, MR severity generally improved at follow-up, potentially due to septal reduction and LVOT enlargement, which may have reduced SAM.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

candidates.title: Right Ventricular Dysfunction and Ventriculo-Arterial Uncoupling in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Phenotype-Specific Review of Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Strategies.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for nearly half of all global heart failure cases. Historically viewed as a left-centric diastolic disorder, emerging evidence identifies right ventricular (RV) dysfunction and impaired ventriculo-arterial (RV-PA) coupling as central drivers of exercise intolerance, functional decline, and adverse clinical outcomes.
OBJECTIVES: This review synthesizes current evidence on the pathophysiological mechanisms, advanced diagnostic modalities, prognostic implications, and phenotype-specific therapies for RV dysfunction in HFpEF, advocating for a transition to systematic biventricular evaluation.
METHODS: A structured, PRISMA-informed search of PubMed and Scopus (2015-2024) identified 74 eligible studies evaluating RV structure, function, and hemodynamics in HFpEF cohorts.
RESULTS: RV dysfunction is prevalent in 19% to 33% of HFpEF patients and independently predicts all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalizations. Key pathophysiological drivers include post-capillary pulmonary hypertension, impaired RV lusitropy, systemic inflammation, and inter-ventricular dependence. Non-invasive markers notably speckle-tracking echocardiography, 4D-flow cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), and the TAPSE/PASP ratio enable early identification of subclinical RV-PA uncoupling. While traditional heart failure therapies show limited efficacy, emerging options including SGLT2 inhibitors, interatrial shunt devices, GLP-1 receptor agonists, and targeted pulmonary vasodilators demonstrate potential to preserve RV strain and restore hemodynamics across distinct clinical phenotypes.
CONCLUSIONS: RV dysfunction is a major prognostic marker in HFpEF. Routine inclusion of RV-PA coupling indices in diagnostic and risk-stratification algorithms is essential to guide precision-based, phenotype-guided management and improve clinical trajectories.

candidates.title: High Rates of Atrial Fibrillation among Inpatients with Heart Failure or Ischemic Stroke in Southwestern Uganda.
candidates.abstract: Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) affects over 37 million people worldwide, and its prevalence is projected to increase by 60% by 2050. Addressing AF is critical in Uganda and elsewhere in sub-Saharan Africa, where data are lacking despite the high prevalence of AF risk factors, comorbidities, and sequelae. Objectives: To evaluate AF prevalence among inpatients with acute heart failure or acute ischemic stroke in Uganda. Methods: Between November 4, 2024 and November 30, 2025, we recruited a cohort of inpatients at the Regional Referral Hospital in Mbarara, Uganda with either acute heart failure or acute ischemic stroke. We collected baseline clinical data and hospital outcomes, performed a transthoracic echocardiogram, and equipped participants with a 24-hour Holter monitor. A multivariable logistic regression model was fitted for a primary outcome of AF detection. Results: Among 250 individuals, mean age was 61.7 years (SD 20.5), of whom 175 (70.0%) were women. 123 (49.2%) had acute heart failure; 127 (50.8%) had acute ischemic stroke. Holter monitors detected AF in 105 (42.0%), with a mean AF duration of 11.0 hours (IQR 1.0-21.9) with a bimodal distribution. Mean stroke risk (CHA2DS2VA) was 3.5 (SD 1.6). Factors associated with AF included increasing age in years (OR 1.04, 95% CI 1.02-1.06) and left atrial volume index (mL/m2) (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.01-1.03). Conclusions: We found high rates of AF among inpatients with acute heart failure or acute ischemic stroke, comparable to studies from the United States and Europe. These findings highlight the need to address AF in Uganda, with improved screening using long-term monitors, updated treatment protocols, and broadened access to cardiac care.

candidates.title: Association between coronary artery calcium score and myocardial ischemia assessed by stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring effectively stratifies cardiovascular risk, and stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) accurately detects myocardial ischemia. We aimed to investigate the prevalence and factors associated with myocardial ischemia on CMR in patients with CAC, and to assess the clinical impact of myocardial ischemia following CMR.
METHODS: This study included 215 patients aged ≥18 years who underwent CAC scoring for risk stratification, followed by stress CMR between 2013 and 2026. The prevalence and predictors of myocardial ischemia were investigated. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess the association between CAC scores and myocardial ischemia. Additionally, subsequent clinical management following CMR was determined.
RESULTS: The mean age was 69.3 ± 9.1 years (60.9% male). The average 10-year PREVENT risk score was 18.6 ± 8.7%. Overall, myocardial ischemia was present in 26.0% of patients (56/215): 17.1% in the CAC 300-999 Agatston units (AU) group (14/82) and 41.6% in the CAC ≥ 1,000 AU group (42/101). CAC score was the only independent predictor of myocardial ischemia (adjusted OR 1.07, 95%CI 1.03 - 1.10; p < 0.001 per 100 AU). Across clinical risk score categories and diabetes status, CAC score was consistently associated with myocardial ischemia, with no significant interactions observed (all p for interaction >0.05).The number of ischemic segments increased with increasing CAC scores (p < 0.001). ROC analysis demonstrated an optimal cutoff threshold of CAC ≥ 1,093 AU for detecting myocardial ischemia (AUC 0.75, p < 0.001). The clinical impact of stress CMR included medication changes in 37.2% of patients, while 18.1% underwent invasive procedures.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CAC scores undergoing stress CMR, the prevalence of myocardial ischemia was approximately one-fourth and was associated with higher CAC scores. Stress CMR may influence clinical management in this populatio

candidates.title: Clinical Impact of Multiple-Clip Implantation for Residual Mitral Regurgitation After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual moderate or greater mitral regurgitation (MR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is strongly associated with adverse clinical outcomes. However, the prognostic impact of implanting additional clips in patients with significant residual MR after the first clip remains uncertain. We evaluated the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of multiple-clip implantation for significant residual MR following placement of the initial clip.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 826 patients with moderate or greater residual MR on intraprocedural transesophageal echocardiography after placement of the first clip during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair at the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center from 2014 to 2023. Patients were categorized into single-clip (n=113) and multiple-clip (n=713) groups. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization at 1 year.
RESULTS: Procedural technical success and complication rates were comparable between groups. The multiple-clip group demonstrated greater MR reduction and higher transmitral pressure gradients at discharge, 30 days, and 1 year. At 1 year, the composite end point occurred less frequently in the multiple-clip group than in the single-clip group (16.8% versus 29.2%; P=0.002), along with greater and more sustained improvement in New York Heart Association functional class. In subgroup analyses, multiple-clip implantation consistently reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with moderate as well as moderate-severe/severe residual MR.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with significant residual MR after implanting the first clip, multiple-clip implantation improved MR reduction and 1-year outcomes without increasing complications. Even in moderate residual MR, additional clips were associated with more favorable clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: Impact of Balloon-Expandable Valve Asymmetry on Heart Failure Post Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain.
METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed. Valve asymmetry was quantified using a fluoroscopic asymmetry index (%), defined as [(longest/shortest balloon-expandable valve height)-1]×100. The primary end point was 2-year HF hospitalization.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 99 patients (17%) experienced HF hospitalization. As a continuous variable, asymmetry index (%) was not independently associated with 2-year HF (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1% increase, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.06]). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated no significant linear or nonlinear association (overall P=0.71; P for nonlinearity=0.89), although the risk curve suggested increased HF risk beyond moderate valve asymmetry. Exploratory threshold analysis identified an asymmetry index cutoff of 7.48%. Patients above this threshold had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those below it (23.6% versus 15.8%; log-rank P=0.043), despite comparable rates of impaired valve performance at discharge. Valve asymmetry >7.48% remained independently associated with late HF occurring beyond 30 days after TAVR (adjusted HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.10-2.60]).
CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopic assessment of balloon-expandable valve expansion identified patients with marked valve asymmetry at increased risk of late HF after TAVR, despite preserved early valve performance. These findings support the potential value of intraprocedural valve geometry assessment for long-term risk stratification and warrant further investigation.

candidates.title: 15O-water PET-detected myocardial ischaemia and CT-derived FFR: Predicting the functional significance of anatomical stenosis.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. While coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical assessment of coronary stenoses, its ability to determine their functional significance is limited. Computed tomography-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) has emerged as a non-invasive method for lesion-specific ischaemia assessment. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of CT-FFR using 15O-water positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging as the reference standard.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively reviewed 193 patients who underwent hybrid CCTA and 15O-water PET at Kuopio University Hospital between 2017 and 2022. Patients with low-to-moderate pretest probability of CAD in whom CAD could not be ruled out by CCTA were eligible. After exclusions, 165 patients were included. CT-FFR values were calculated using a research prototype algorithm and compared with PET-derived perfusion abnormalities. In the overall cohort, CT-FFR showed moderate diagnostic performance, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.672-0.740. In a subgroup of 83 patients with high-quality CCTA and stenosis >50%, diagnostic performance improved substantially (AUC 0.836). Using a CT-FFR threshold of 0.80, sensitivity and specificity were 85% and 87%, respectively.
CONCLUSION: In an unselected clinical population referred for PET perfusion imaging after CCTA, CT-FFR did not significantly improve diagnostic performance compared with CCTA alone. However, in patients with high-quality CCTA and obstructive coronary stenoses, CT-FFR demonstrated good accuracy for identifying functionally significant disease, supporting its role as a complementary non-invasive diagnostic tool.

candidates.title: The impact of defects of the atrial septum on procedural complexity, complications, and outcomes of transvenous lead extraction.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with defects of the atrial septum (DAS) undergoing transvenous lead extraction (TLE) may be at increased risk of systemic embolism due to transient right-to-left shunting. However, data on the prevalence and clinical relevance of DAS in patients undergoing TLE remain limited.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 3637 patients undergoing TLE between 2006 and 2024 with complete preprocedural assessment of the atrial septum and at least 3 years of follow-up. We evaluated the prevalence of DAS and its association with procedural complexity, major complications, and survival.
RESULTS: DAS was identified in 3.71% of patients. Patent foramen ovale was present in 2.45%, secundum atrial septal defect in 1.15%, and both defects in 0.08%. Most defects were small, with predominant left-to-right shunting. Patients with DAS more frequently had lead-related infective endocarditis and vegetations on transesophageal echocardiography (p < 0.001). TLE procedures in patients with DAS were more complex, with longer extraction times and more frequent use of advanced extraction tools. Despite higher predicted procedural risk, the incidence of major complications, including stroke, was low. DAS was not associated with increased in-hospital, 30-day, 1-year, or 3-year mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large TLE cohort, DAS was uncommon and associated with greater procedural complexity, but not with a higher incidence of major complications or worse long-term survival. Clinically apparent systemic embolic events were rare.

candidates.title: Single-center clinical analysis of anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery (AAOCA) in children: a multimodal imaging approach to risk stratification.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to analyze the clinical characteristics of pediatric patients with Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery (AAOCA), explore the application of multimodal imaging in risk stratification, and establish individualized diagnosis and treatment protocols for this population.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study was performed on children diagnosed with AAOCA at Wuhan Children's Hospital between January 2015 and April 2026. Clinical manifestations, multimodal imaging findings, therapeutic strategies, and long-term outcomes were comprehensively analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 58 AAOCA patients confirmed by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were enrolled. Initial transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) yielded false-negative results in 24 patients (41.4%). Twenty-seven patients underwent single-photon emission computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (SPECT-MPI, MPS), among whom 6 had normal perfusion and 21 showed perfusion defects. Seven patients with positive MPS findings received surgical correction, including 2 patients with L-AAOCA( 1 coronary angioplasty and 1 coronary unroofing) and 5 patients with R-AAOCA; all treated with coronary unroofing. No patients with negative MPS results underwent surgery, indicating that negative MPS findings perhaps provide limited valuable evidence to avoid unnecessary coronary revascularization. Two patients developed massive postoperative pericardial effusion and recovered after pericardiotomy and drainage; the remaining 5 surgical patients experienced no perioperative complications. All surgical patients were discharged after full recovery and received 3 months of aspirin antiplatelet therapy. Non-surgical patients were instructed to restrict strenuous physical activity and followed up for 3 months to 3 years. Follow-up CCTA or TTE revealed normal coronary ostia without stenosis in all patients.
CONCLUSION: Clinical manifestations of pediatric AAOCA vary widely across age groups

candidates.title: Echocardiographic markers for left atrial stiffness and left atrial conduction delay in patients with silent paroxysmal atrial fibrillation compared to age-matched controls.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: To study left atrial stiffness index (LASI) and left atrial activation time (LA-AT) changes in an older population with silent paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) compared to age-matched control.
METHODS: Individuals with newly diagnosed PAF and a randomly selected age-matched control group without AF were enrolled from STROKESTOP2-study. All participants had NT-proBNP levels 125-900 ng/L. TTE examinations were analyzed retrospectively offline using dedicated software. Besides conventional echocardiographic measurements, LA-AT was obtained by measuring the time delay between the onset of the P-wave on ECG and tissue Doppler Á peak wave in lateral LA wall. LASI was calculated as the ratio of left ventricular filling (E/é) to peak atrial longitudinal strain (PALS).
RESULTS: Mean age was 76 ± 0.3 years. The PAF group (n = 67) presented significant increase of LASI (0.41 (0.29-0.60) vs. 0.32 (0.29-0.43), P = 0.001) and prolonged LA-AT (170 (140-180) ms vs. 140 (120-144) ms, P < 0.001) compared to controls (n = 94). Subgroup analysis in participants with normal LA volume index (LAVI) ≤ 34 ml/m2, LASI and LA-AT remained significantly increased/prolonged in PAF (N = 27) compared to controls (N = 72). NT-proBNP-levels did not differ between PAF (228 (181-348) ng/L) and controls (216 (156-317) ng/L) (P = 0.18). ROC curve analysis identified thresholds LASI > 0.54 and LA-AT > 139 msec for discrimination of silent PAF.
CONCLUSION: Indices reflecting LA stiffness and atrial conduction delay were significantly elevated in recently diagnosed PAF patients. LASI and LA-AT thresholds might non-invasively detect early atrial remodeling without structural enlargement in elderly patients with high risk of PAF and mildly increased NT-proBNP levels.

candidates.title: Coxiella burnetii infective endocarditis involving a valved right ventricle-to-pulmonary artery conduit after Rastelli repair in an adolescent: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coxiella burnetii is an important cause of blood culture-negative infective endocarditis (IE). Pediatric C. burnetii endocarditis is rare, particularly in patients with prosthetic cardiovascular materials.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 13-year-old boy with pulmonary atresia who had undergone Rastelli repair followed by replacement with a valved right ventricle-to-pulmonary artery (RV-PA) conduit presented with recurrent fever and a mobile intraconduit mass. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) showed a vegetation in the pulmonary valve/conduit region, and cardiac computed tomography (CT) confirmed a corresponding filling defect without periconduit abscess or pseudoaneurysm. Blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected C. burnetii, while indirect immunofluorescence assay (IFA) showed positive phase I and phase II IgG antibodies. The conduit vegetation and blood detection of C. burnetii fulfilled major imaging and microbiological criteria, respectively, under the 2023 Duke-International Society for Cardiovascular Infectious Diseases criteria. An individualized regimen of doxycycline, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX), and hydroxychloroquine was followed by clinical improvement and reduction in lesion size during hospitalization.
CONCLUSIONS: C. burnetii should be considered in children with prosthetic cardiovascular materials who present with persistent fever and negative conventional blood cultures. Molecular testing, serology, and multimodality cardiac imaging can support diagnosis and early follow-up.

candidates.title: Stress hyperglycaemic ratio is independently associated with intramyocardial haemorrhage in STEMI patients: a cardiac magnetic resonance study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) often results in microvascular injury, including intramyocardial haemorrhage (IMH), despite successful reperfusion. This study explored whether the stress hyperglycaemic ratio (SHR) is independently associated with IMH in STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI).
METHODS: We screened 650 consecutive STEMI patients who underwent pPCI at the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University (2019-2024). After exclusions, 508 patients were included in the final analysis. SHR was calculated as admission glucose (mmol/L) divided by estimated average glucose from HbA1c converted to mmol/L: ([28.7 × HbA1c (%) - 46.7] ÷ 18). IMH was evaluated with cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging performed within 3-7 days post-pPCI using T2*-mapping sequences. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of IMH, and Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed the predictive performance of SHR.
RESULTS: Higher SHR was independently associated with IMH. Among 508 patients, IMH was present in 179 (35.2%). Patients with IMH had significantly higher SHR (0.87 vs. 0.81, p < 0.001). After adjusting for age, sex, WBC count, and haemoglobin, an elevated SHR remained independently associated with IMH (adjusted OR 1.18; 95% CI 1.07-1.29; p = 0.001). ROC analysis showed an AUC of 0.625 (95% CI 0.577-0.673, p < 0.001), indicating modest predictive ability, with an optimal cutoff of 0.86 (sensitivity 59.2%, specificity 63.8%).
CONCLUSIONS: SHR is independently associated with IMH in reperfused STEMI patients and may warrant further investigation as a research tool for risk stratification in future studies. These findings support cardiometabolic research in STEMI management strategies.

candidates.title: Cardiac PET Imaging in Coronary Artery Disease: Myocardial Perfusion and Flow Reserve Assessment.
candidates.abstract: PET myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) provides excellent diagnostic and prognostic performance for ischemic heart disease. It offers multiparametric evaluation of myocardial perfusion, left ventricular function at rest and peak stress, coronary calcium (on PET/computed tomography scanners), and myocardial blood flow, which can diagnose epicardial and microvascular coronary disease, stratify risk, and guide management patients with known or suspected ischemic heart disease. The purpose of this article is to deliver a practical approach of PET MPI techniques and interpretation.

candidates.title: Acute pericarditis caused by Kocuria kristinae with successful withdrawal from hemodialysis: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Kocuria kristinae is a commensal skin bacterium that occasionally acts as an opportunistic pathogen. However, it is rarely associated with pericardial infection. This report describes the case of a 47-year-old male patient with dialysis-dependent acute kidney injury (AKI) complicated by massive inflammatory pericardial effusion, in whom K. kristinae was isolated. The patient developed a severe heatstroke, which was followed by AKI, subsequently requiring hemodialysis. Approximately 1 month later, the cardiothoracic ratio increased markedly, and echocardiography revealed substantial pericardial effusion. Anti-inflammatory therapy, comprising non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, colchicine, and prednisolone, elicited a poor response, given no improvement in the effusion. Ultrasound guidance was used for pericardiocentesis, resulting in drainage of 1050 mL of pale-yellow, exudative fluid with neutrophil predominance. K. kristinae was subsequently identified using the VITEK 2 system. The vancomycin dosage was determined based on the susceptibility results. Following the implementation of drainage and antimicrobial therapy, pericardial effusion decreased, venous congestion was alleviated, and urine output increased. These interventions may have contributed to renal recovery and the discontinuation of hemodialysis on day 102. Clinicians should regard K. kristinae isolated from pericardial fluid as a possible contaminant notwithstanding a clinically compatible setting. This case suggests that a massive pericardial effusion with venous congestion can delay renal recovery in severe AKI, whereas successful pericardial drainage facilitates recovery of urine output and withdrawal from hemodialysis.

candidates.title: Multimodality Imaging and Pathology of an Incidentally Discovered Right Atrial Myxoma Arising from the Crista Terminalis.
candidates.abstract: Cardiac myxomas are the second most common benign cardiac tumor in adults. Most arise from the interatrial septum in the left atrium. Although most patients present with cardiac or embolic symptoms, some lesions are detected incidentally at imaging performed for unrelated indications. This case report describes the incidental discovery of a right atrial mass partially visualized at CT of the abdomen and pelvis during workup for cholecystitis. Subsequent multimodality imaging demonstrated a right atrial mass arising from the crista terminalis, which was confirmed to be a myxoma at pathologic examination. This case highlights an atypical origin and location of a common cardiac tumor incidentally detected at abdominal imaging.

candidates.title: Prognostic Impact of Late Gadolinium Enhancement on Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events and Time-Varying Attenuation of Risk in Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the prognostic value of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) extent for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) patients and characterize the dynamic pattern of its risk effect over time.
METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled patients who underwent Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) between 2020 and 2024, with MACE (cardiac death, heart failure re-hospitalization, or sustained ventricular arrhythmia) as the endpoint. Patients were stratified by MACE occurrence. Schoenfeld residual testing showed borderline deviation of the proportional hazards (PH) assumption for LGE extent (LV mass percentage). Thus, a time-dependent Cox model (Extended Cox PHs Model) with an LGE extent × follow-up time interaction term was built to assess dynamic hazard ratio changes, and independent MACE risk factors were identified.
RESULTS: Among 173 DCM patients (age 47 ± 15 years, 105 males), 46 (26.6%) experienced MACE after a mean follow-up of 27 ± 16 months. The time-dependent Cox model identified LGE extent (baseline HR: 1.243, 95% CI: 1.162-1.329, p < 0.001), the LGE extent × time interaction (HR: 0.993, 95% CI: 0.989-0.997, p = 0.001), and LV end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVi; HR = 1.008, 95% CI: 1.003-1.014, p = 0.001) as independent MACE predictors. Notably, the risk effect of LGE extent demonstrated time-dependent attenuation.
CONCLUSION: LV LGE extent and LVEDVi independently predict MACE in DCM patients. The early prognostic value of LGE extent suggests a critical time window for early fibrosis intervention.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiogram Screening for Detection of Low Ejection Fraction in Routine Care: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
candidates.journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) is common and treatable but often undiagnosed, especially in early stages with non-specific symptoms. AI applied to standard ECGs offers low-cost screening for low ejection fraction (EF), yet its real-world impact on diagnosis remains unclear.
