METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs assessed AI-ECG screening for low EF in clinical practice. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261287652). Databases (PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central, Google Scholar) were searched from inception to January 18, 2026, for RCTs comparing AI-ECG screening to usual care in adults without known heart failure undergoing routine ECGs. The primary outcome was new low EF (≤ 50%) confirmed by echocardiography. Secondary outcomes included echocardiography referral rates, positive predictive value, and cardiology referral rates. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs were calculated using a random-effects model.
RESULTS: Three RCTs were included (two individual and one cluster) with 37,467 participants. After adjusting for clustering, AI-ECG screening significantly improved detection of new low EF diagnoses compared to usual care (RR 1.36, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.64; p = 0.002; I2 = 0%), with a number needed to screen of 204. No significant difference was found in echocardiography referral rates (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.09; p = 0.55; I2 = 36%). The PPV of the AI tool ranged from approximately 20% to 34% across studies.
CONCLUSION: AI-ECG screening added to routine care improves low EF detection without substantially increasing echocardiography referrals. These findings support AI-ECG for earlier LVSD detection in at-risk populations, though further validation across diverse AI platforms is warranted.

candidates.title: Above-Threshold Ambulatory Systolic Pressure and Left Ventricular Mass in Chronic Kidney Disease: Does AUC Add Beyond Mean Pressure?
candidates.abstract: Above-threshold ambulatory systolic blood pressure (SBP) area under the curve (AUC) captures both the magnitude and duration of SBP above daytime and nighttime reference values. We examined whether this measure provided information about left ventricular mass index (LVMI) beyond daytime and nighttime mean SBP. In this cross-sectional study, 212 Chinese adults with non-dialysis chronic kidney disease (CKD) underwent ambulatory blood pressure monitoring and echocardiography. Daytime AUC above 135 mmHg and nighttime AUC above 120 mmHg were entered jointly. Together, daytime and nighttime AUC were significantly associated with LVMI (P < 0.001; adjusted R2 = 0.345). From the 25th to the 75th percentile, adjusted LVMI was 3.46 g/m2·7 higher for daytime AUC and 5.56 g/m2·7 higher for nighttime AUC. AUC attributable to daytime and nighttime mean SBP accounted for 89.7% of the cohort-average above-threshold burden. The remaining AUC not captured by those period means was not significantly associated with LVMI after adjustment for daytime and nighttime mean SBP (0.69 g/m2·7 per interquartile range; 95% confidence interval, -2.00 to 3.37). Above-threshold AUC was associated with greater LVMI but added limited information beyond daytime and nighttime mean SBP in this cohort.

candidates.title: Admission Albumin-Corrected Anion Gap and Subsequent Tricuspid Regurgitation Velocity Elevation After COPD Exacerbation.
candidates.abstract: Admission albumin-corrected anion gap (ACAG) may reflect metabolic stress during an acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), but its relationship with subsequent pulmonary vascular abnormalities is unclear. This study included 294 adults hospitalized with AECOPD between January 2022 and November 2024 in a single-center retrospective cohort. Participants had baseline tricuspid regurgitation velocity (TRV) <3.4 m/s and at least one follow-up echocardiogram. The primary endpoint was first detected TRV ≥3.4 m/s within 12 calendar months after discharge. During available follow-up, 105 participants (35.7%) reached the endpoint and 12 died before detection. Each 5 mmol/L higher ACAG was associated with an adjusted odds ratio of 2.17 (95% CI, 1.51-3.11) and a cause-specific hazard ratio of 1.66 (95% CI, 1.34-2.05). A sensitivity analysis using TRV >3.4 m/s identified 99 events and gave an adjusted odds ratio of 1.90 (95% CI, 1.32-2.75). Adding ACAG to the clinical reference model increased the cross-validated area under the curve from 0.803 to 0.829; the extended-model calibration slope was 0.823. Among participants without a detected event, the last readable echocardiogram occurred a median of 323 days after discharge. Admission ACAG was associated with subsequent TRV elevation and provided modest additional discrimination in this cohort. Its availability in routine admission testing makes it a candidate for further evaluation in post-exacerbation risk assessment, with prospective external validation needed before clinical application.

candidates.title: Microvascular Obstruction After Reperfusion in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Structured Narrative Review.
candidates.abstract: Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI) restores epicardial coronary flow in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but microvascular and tissue-level reperfusion may remain impaired. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-defined microvascular obstruction (MVO) and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) both mark severe reperfusion injury but reflect distinct tissue processes. This structured narrative review synthesizes evidence on MVO mechanisms, multimodal phenotypes, and interventions. Available evidence implicates interacting contributions from distal embolization, endothelial barrier and vasomotor dysfunction, pericyte-mediated capillary constriction, immunothrombosis, and tissue edema. IMH reflects more extensive microvascular destruction with erythrocyte extravasation. Angiography, electrocardiography, invasive physiology, angiography-derived indices, echocardiography, and CMR assess different pathophysiologic levels. Discordance between modalities is therefore not necessarily contradictory. Across trials, improvements in surrogate endpoints have often not translated into long-term clinical benefit, partly because of mechanistic heterogeneity and misaligned treatment timing and endpoints. A conceptual, reperfusion-centered T- to T5 research framework is proposed for serial within-patient assessment. It links early physiology, inflammatory and thrombotic biomarkers, acute-phase CMR, and long-term remodeling. Future trials should align mechanistic enrichment, intervention timing, and endpoint selection to establish a continuous evidence chain from target engagement to clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: Atrial fibrillation is independently associated with impaired myocardial perfusion.
candidates.abstract: A characteristic feature of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) is impaired myocardial blood flow (MBF). Previous studies have shown that atrial fibrillation (AF) is also associated with reduced hyperemic MBF. However, it is unknown whether an independent association exists between AF and MBF in symptomatic patients with suspected obstructive CAD. We studied 874 patients at Kuopio University Hospital (Finland) who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and [15O]H2O myocardial perfusion positron emission tomography due to suspected obstructive CAD in 2017-2023. The final cohort comprised 31 AF patients and 120 propensity score-matched sinus rhythm (SR) patients. The matching criteria were age, sex, body mass index, number of traditional risk factors for CAD (0-5), calcium score, and total CCTA status (i.e., the overall severity of CCTA findings). Global hyperemic MBF was lower in AF patients than in SR patients (median 1.9 mL/g/min [IQR 1.4-2.6 mL/g/min] vs. 3.0 mL/g/min [IQR 2.4-3.6 mL/g/min], p < 0.001). Impaired hyperemic MBF (< 2.3 mL/g/min in ≥ 1 segment) was more frequent in AF patients (n = 25/31, 81%) than in SR patients (n = 50/120, 42%, p < 0.001). Furthermore, the presence of AF was independently associated with reduced hyperemic MBF in three multivariate general linear models (p < 0.001 in each model). To summarize, AF was independently associated with impaired hyperemic MBF in patients with suspected obstructive CAD. This association should be considered in clinical practice when interpreting the results of myocardial perfusion imaging in patients with AF.

candidates.title: Association of Blood Heavy Metal Concentrations with Angiographic Coronary Artery Disease in a Consecutive Single-Center Cardiac Catheterization Cohort.
candidates.abstract: Environmental heavy metal exposure is increasingly recognized as a potentially important but underappreciated contributor to cardiovascular disease, yet its relationship to directly observed coronary artery disease (CAD) remains poorly defined. In this single-center cohort of 52 consecutive adults undergoing cardiac catheterization at an urban Chicago tertiary care center, we paired elemental exposure profiles with direct angiographic assessment in a racially diverse, socioeconomically vulnerable population. While no individual metal independently explained obstructive CAD, circulating metal exposure patterns were more revealing: Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression demonstrated that increasing overall metal burden was associated with worse coronary phenotypes, suggesting that environmental exposures may act collectively rather than in isolation. Lead and mercury emerged as the strongest contributors and were enriched relative to National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) reference populations. Taken together, these findings offer early but meaningful evidence that environmental toxicant burden may represent an underrecognized layer of cardiovascular risk, particularly in urban communities where industrial history, aging infrastructure, and socioeconomic disadvantage intersect. This work highlights the importance of viewing cardiovascular disease not only through the lens of traditional risk factors, but also through the environments in which patients live.

candidates.title: Composite Haematological and Nutritional Indices Show No Evidence of Improved Long-Term Mortality Discrimination Beyond Their Own Components in Non-ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
candidates.abstract: Background and Objectives: Composite indices from routine inflammatory, haematological and nutritional measurements are widely reported as prognostic markers after acute coronary syndromes, but whether they add information beyond their components is uncertain. Materials and Methods: In 30-day survivors of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) undergoing coronary angiography at a single centre, thirteen composite indices and six prespecified components were evaluated for five-year all-cause mortality using ROC analysis, Cox regression and the change in Harrell's C-index (ΔC) over a study clinical model. Each index was also compared with a freely weighted model of its own constituents and with a reference model adding CRP and albumin. Results: Among 561 patients (median follow-up 5.48 years), 94 died, 86 within five years. Composite-index AUCs ranged from 0.616 to 0.689; none exceeded CRP alone after multiplicity correction. Eight indices were nominally associated with mortality after adjustment (hazard ratios 1.26-1.38 per 1 SD), but every bootstrap confidence interval for ΔC over the clinical model included zero. Fixed indices and freely weighted constituents performed similarly (cross-validated ΔC -0.0089 to +0.0053), with one small exploratory difference favouring the fixed MLR ratio. Adding CRP and albumin raised the C-index from 0.7720 to 0.7826; over this reference, no estimable composite showed evidence of association (all p ≥ 0.19). Conclusions: In 30-day survivors of NSTEMI, composite indices showed no evidence of improved long-term mortality discrimination over a study-specific clinical model and contained no information beyond their measured constituents. Their independent associations may largely reflect information already present in the components. Small gains cannot be excluded; the findings do not establish equivalence.

candidates.title: Non-Invasive Assessment of Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction: From Flow Quantification to Clinical Decision Making.
candidates.abstract: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a major mechanism of myocardial ischemia and adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients with angina or dyspnea, both in the absence and in the presence of obstructive coronary artery disease. Because the coronary microcirculation cannot be visualized directly with routine angiography, diagnosis depends on physiological assessment. Non-invasive imaging has moved beyond relative perfusion analysis toward quantification of resting and hyperemic myocardial blood flow and flow reserve. Positron emission tomography (PET) remains the most extensively validated non-invasive method and provides robust absolute flow measurements with strong prognostic evidence. Quantitative stress cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) is rapidly maturing, combining high-resolution perfusion mapping with ventricular and tissue characterization without ionizing radiation. Transthoracic Doppler echocardiography offers an accessible, radiation-free estimate of coronary flow velocity reserve, whereas myocardial contrast echocardiography can assess myocardial blood volume and replenishment kinetics. Dynamic cadmium-zinc-telluride single-photon emission computed tomography and stress computed tomography perfusion extend flow quantification to more widely available platforms, although standardization and outcome validation remain less developed. Across modalities, interpretation requires attention to the adequacy of vasodilator stress, resting hemodynamics, diffuse epicardial atherosclerosis, scar, and technical factors. A reduced flow reserve is not synonymous with isolated microvascular disease and cannot identify acetylcholine-provoked vasospasm. This review provides a clinically oriented framework for selecting, performing, interpreting, and reporting non-invasive CMD testing; examines the evidence, strengths, and limitations of each modality; and defines situations in which invasive coronary function testing remains necessary. Future progress will d

candidates.title: Evaluation of Diastolic Dysfunction in Pituitary Adenomas: A Comparative Single-Center Study Among Acromegaly, Prolactinoma, and Nonfunctioning Pituitary Adenomas.
candidates.abstract: Background and Objectives: Pituitary adenomas may be associated with metabolic and cardiovascular abnormalities, but comparative evidence across subtypes is limited. We compared cardiometabolic and echocardiographic profiles, left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD), and carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) among patients with prolactinoma, acromegaly, or nonfunctioning pituitary adenoma (NFPA) and healthy controls and investigated factors associated with LVDD. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional comparative study included 214 participants evaluated between 2016 and 2018: 91 with prolactinoma, 26 with acromegaly, 45 with NFPA, and 52 healthy controls. Participants underwent clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, and CIMT assessment. LVDD was diagnosed and graded according to the 2016 American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) and European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging (EACVI) recommendations. Factors associated with LVDD were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Results: The mean age was 41.3 ± 12.4 years, and 64.5% of participants were women. Acromegaly was associated with the highest fasting glucose, HbA1c, insulin, and homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) values (all p < 0.001) and, compared with controls, a higher left atrial volume index (LAVI) and average E/e' ratio and lower left ventricular ejection fraction (despite preserved ejection fraction), E/A ratio, and lateral e' velocity. CIMT was higher in NFPA than in prolactinoma. LVDD was present in 21.5% of the cohort and in 5.8%, 19.8%, 46.2%, and 28.9% of the control, prolactinoma, acromegaly, and NFPA groups, respectively (p < 0.001); 84.8% of cases were grade I. Increasing age was independently associated with LVDD (OR 1.265 per year, 95% CI 1.155-1.385; p < 0.001), and diagnostic group was independently associated with LVDD overall (p = 0.004). Compared with controls, adjusted LVDD odds were higher in prolactinoma (OR 10.9, 95% CI 1.34-89.68),

candidates.title: Unravelling the Diagnosis of Normal-Flow Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis: The Role of Multimodality Imaging.
candidates.abstract: Normal-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis is one of the most deceptive presentations of aortic stenosis. It leaves clinicians uncertain whether they are facing true severe disease or a measurement artefact. This often reflects a discordant grading pattern, in which many patients ultimately prove to have moderate disease. This diagnostic paradox arises from a combination of measurement errors, geometric assumptions, and genuine hemodynamic complexity, and cannot be resolved by echocardiography alone. A structured multimodality imaging strategy integrating calcium score evaluation on cardiac computed tomography, tissue characterisation on cardiac magnetic resonance and, when necessary, invasive hemodynamic assessment is the only reliable path to diagnostic certainty and appropriate therapeutic decision-making. Together, these modalities form a coherent sequential algorithm that moves from the non-invasive to the invasive, from the hemodynamic to the biological, and from uncertainty to actionable clinical decision. This review provides an updated, critical appraisal of each imaging tool and its respective strengths and pitfalls.

candidates.title: Urinary Bisphenol A Levels Are Associated with Vascular Injury in Mexican Patients with Coronary Artery Disease.
candidates.abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a leading cause of death worldwide and is associated with standard modifiable cardiovascular risk factors (SMuRFs); however, additional factors may contribute to its development. Bisphenol A (BPA), an endocrine-disrupting chemical has been associated with cardiovascular alterations. We investigated BPA's possible association with classic risk factors and vascular injury biomarkers in Mexican patients with CAD. Adult patients underwent quantitative coronary angiography and SYNTAX score assessment and were classified as having obstructive (OD) or non-obstructive (NOD) disease. SMuRFs, lipid profile, VCAM-1, MMP-2, MMP-9, and uBPA were determined. Data were analyzed using correlation analysis, Welch's t-test, ANOVA, and adjusted multiple linear regression. Eighty-nine patients aged 30-85 years were evaluated. OD patients had higher uBPA levels (3.46 ± 2.04 ng/mL) than NOD patients (1.25 ± 1.08 ng/mL), and uBPA levels differed according to the number of diseased arteries and diseased artery segments. uBPA was positively associated with MMP-2, MMP-9, SYNTAX score, percentage of stenosis, number of diseased arteries, diseased artery segments, and SMuRFs, and negatively associated with HDLc. SYNTAX score was associated with MMP-2, MMP-9, VCAM-1 and low HDLc levels. Our findings support uBPA levels are associated with vascular injury in Mexican patients with coronary artery disease.

candidates.title: Fibrin Clot Properties in Aneurysmal Coronary Artery Disease: CARE-ANEURYSM Study.
candidates.abstract: Coronary artery ectasias and aneurysms (CAEAs) are present in up to 5% of patients undergoing coronary angiography. Recent studies indicated an independent association between CAEA and the risk of myocardial infarction but the underlying mechanisms have not yet been elucidated. We evaluated the relationship between CAEA and fibrin clot properties in 60 consecutive CAEA subjects and 60 clinically/angiographically matched controls enrolled across three tertiary centers. Fibrin clot permeability coefficient (Ks), clot lysis time (CLT), and levels of 3-nitrotyrosine, an oxidative stress marker, were assessed. Among patients with CAEA, 52 (86.7%) were male, the median age was 66.0 (59.5-74.1) years, and 30 (50.0%) had concomitant coronary artery disease. Compared with controls, CAEA subjects had 14% lower Ks (p = 0.036), 25% longer CLT (p = 0.001), and 21% higher 3-nitrotyrosine levels (p = 0.002). Multivariable regression analysis showed an association of CAEA with lower Ks, longer CLT, and higher 3-nitrotyrosine levels (all p < 0.05). In CAEA patients, 3-nitrotyrosine levels correlated with Ks (r = -0.31, p = 0.016) and CLT (r = 0.27, p = 0.037). With increasing CAEA peak-to-reference diameter ratio, Ks decreased (p-trend = 0.017), and 3-nitrotyrosine levels increased (p-trend = 0.002). In conclusion, we found that CAEA is independently associated with unfavorably altered fibrin clot properties, reflected by denser clot structure and reduced susceptibility to fibrinolysis. Our findings suggest that oxidative stress may contribute to unfavorable modification of fibrin clot properties in CAEA. With an increase in CAEA size, there is an increase in oxidative stress and worsening of the fibrin clot phenotype (CARE-ANEURYSM, NCT05183373).

candidates.title: Case 351: Thalamic Dementia Secondary to Dural Arteriovenous Fistula.
candidates.abstract: A 76-year-old man with a medical history of diabetes, hypertension, and dilated cardiomyopathy developed new symptoms of confusion, repeated falls, and urinary incontinence over the course of 3-4 months, which worsened over a 2-week period, leading to presentation at the emergency room. His partner reported that before this, he had no memory or movement disorders, but now he was experiencing memory lapses, such as forgetting his mother's recent death, and functional cognitive problems, including an inability to remember how to perform tasks that were previously simple for him, such as dosing his insulin with meals. At presentation, the patient was awake and alert, oriented to his name and location but not to the date. Full neurologic examinations, including of the motor and sensory systems and cranial nerves, were normal. There were no signs of meningism, no fever or leukocytosis, and no history of recent travel. Serum electrolyte panel and thiamine levels were normal, and he had no history of alcohol or drug abuse. Initial evaluation included noncontrast CT of the head, the results of which prompted multiphasic CT angiography of the head including parenchymal phase imaging and admission for observation and monitoring with serial noncontrast CT of the head. The patient's symptoms worsened during his hospital stay. He also developed facial twitching, increased drowsiness, and seizure episodes. He was therefore evaluated with noncontrast MRI of the brain and then digital subtraction angiography with external carotid artery and internal carotid artery contrast agent injections.

candidates.title: [Multimodality imaging in heart failure: phenotyping and clinical decision-making].
candidates.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a global health priority traditionally managed based on ejection fraction (EF). However, EF is now recognized as insufficient to represent the pathophysiological complexity and clinical heterogeneity of the syndrome. Modern diagnostics have shifted toward multimodality imaging, acting as an integrated platform for phenotyping. Transthoracic echocardiography remains the first-line tool, evolving into a multiparametric approach that includes global longitudinal strain, right ventricular-arterial coupling assessment, and congestion monitoring via lung ultrasound and venous excess ultrasound. Cardiac magnetic resonance is the gold standard for tissue characterization, which is crucial for etiological definition and arrhythmic risk stratification through fibrosis identification (late gadolinium enhancement). Cardiac computed tomography is essential for coronary anatomy evaluation and procedural planning, while nuclear imaging (single-photon emission computed tomography/positron emission tomography) provides unique insights into metabolism, inflammation, and sympathetic innervation. Integrating these modalities, guided by clinical questions, enables personalized therapeutic management, tracking of disease trajectories (such as improved HF), and optimization of clinical decision-making.

candidates.title: Pulmonary embolism mimicking myocardial ischemia in an Emergency Department.
candidates.abstract:
PRESENTATION: A man in his seventies presented with sudden central chest pain radiating to both arms with diaphoresis. Observations, ECGs, and serial troponins were normal.
DIAGNOSIS: Targeted history revealed previous unilateral calf pain and recent long-haul travel. D-dimer was elevated and CT pulmonary angiography confirmed multiple segmental and sub segmental pulmonary emboli without right heart strain.
TREATMENT: Therapeutic anticoagulation was commenced and later transitioned to apixaban for six months.
DISCUSSION: This case highlights the need for structured history taking and avoidance of diagnostic anchoring in emergency chest pain assessment.

candidates.title: Myocardial injury patterns on cardiac magnetic resonance: diffuse myocardial damage with prominent septal involvement in adults with severe myocarditis requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Patients with myocarditis suffering from cardiogenic shock may benefit from extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). However, the characteristics of myocardial injury in these patients are unclear. Using cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), we aimed to investigate cardiac changes in survivors with severe myocarditis treated with ECMO.
METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted at the First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University in Nanjing, China, from July 2018 to July 2022. Patients with severe myocarditis who underwent CMR within 30 days after discontinuing ECMO were included in this study.
RESULTS: In total, 22 patients (median age: 33 years) were included. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) was detected within the interventricular septum (IVS) in all patients. The mean T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) values showed similar distribution patterns to LGE. In an exploratory post-hoc age stratification based on the cohort median age of 33 years, we observed that several quantitative CMR parameters (mean ECV, minimum ECV, maximum ECV, mean T1, maximum T1, and minimum T2) were numerically higher in the older subgroup (p < 0.05). Myocardial injury was widespread in patients with severe myocarditis receiving ECMO.
CONCLUSIONS: Survivors of severe myocarditis who required ECMO support presented diffuse myocardial injury as the dominant pattern on early post-weaning CMR examination, with the interventricular septum showing notably prominent lesions among all myocardial segments.

candidates.title: The diagnostic value of cardiovascular magnetic resonance in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited studies compare the clinical applications and diagnostic values of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) versus echocardiography in individuals with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM).
OBJECTIVE: This study was performed to evaluate the diagnostic value of CMR in patients with HCM.
METHODS: A retrospective study without prospective follow-up was performed on the data from 100 patients diagnosed with HCM from July 2018 to December 2021. All patients underwent echocardiography, CMR scans, and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE). Various parameters of CMR were measured and compared to those of echocardiography to evaluate the diagnostic value of CMR in the diagnosis of HCM.
RESULTS: CMR classified the patients into 6 major types based on the location of myocardial hypertrophy involvement: ventricular septal HCM (n = 43); apical HCM (n = 30); basal septal HCM (n = 4); mid-ventricular HCM (n = 13); mass‑like HCM (n = 1), and diffuse HCM (n = 9). There were 4 patients with symmetric HCM, 96 with asymmetric HCM, 41 with obstructive HCM, and 59 with non-obstructive HCM. The diagnostic accuracy rate of CMR and echocardiography for HCM was 100% and 61%, respectively, with a missed diagnosis rate of 39% (39/100). LGE showed delayed enhancement, which manifested as patchy or focal enhancement within the hypertrophied myocardium. The delayed enhancement area was limited to the hypertrophied myocardial region. CMR + LGE showed myocardial fibrosis at the apex in 62 patients. Echocardiography alone detected 17 patients apical HCM.
CONCLUSION: The combination of CMR with clinical symptoms may aid in the diagnosis and classification of HCM, as well as in the characterization of myocardial fibrosis. CMR appears to be superior to echocardiography in detecting missed CMR diagnoses. Further study is required to validate these findings.

candidates.title: Echocardiographic Assessment of Prognosis and Treatment Benefit After Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) can achieve substantial mitral regurgitation (MR) reduction in appropriately selected patients, yet outcomes after technically successful intervention remain heterogeneous. This variability has prompted interest in echocardiographic markers of limited treatment benefit. However, adverse prognosis after TEER and absence of benefit attributable to TEER are fundamentally different concepts, and most available imaging studies evaluate the former rather than the latter.
METHODS: This state-of-the-art review summarizes evidence on echocardiographic assessment of prognosis and treatment response across the mitral TEER pathway, integrating baseline multichamber phenotyping, procedural and immediate hemodynamic assessment, longitudinal imaging, and evidence from randomized trials of TEER in secondary MR.
RESULTS: Baseline left ventricular remodeling and myocardial dysfunction, left atrial disease, pulmonary hypertension, right ventricular dysfunction and right ventricular-pulmonary arterial uncoupling, and tricuspid regurgitation identify greater cardiovascular disease burden and residual risk after TEER. Procedural assessment extends beyond residual MR to include transmitral pressure gradient, forward flow, and left atrial hemodynamics, whereas serial imaging characterizes subsequent ventricular, atrial, pulmonary, and right-heart trajectories. Persistent structural or hemodynamic abnormalities and absence of reverse remodeling should not be equated with irreversible disease or therapeutic futility. Randomized subgroup analyses in secondary MR have not consistently demonstrated significant treatment-effect modification by several adverse echocardiographic phenotypes; however, these analyses were not adequately powered to exclude clinically meaningful interactions. Moreover, COAPT excluded patients with extreme ventricular remodeling, markedly elevated pulmonary pressures, or advanced RV dysfunction, limiting genera

candidates.title: [Myocardium global longitudinal strain and peripheral blood neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio for predicting MACE risks following percutaneous coronary intervention for first-time acute myocardial infarction: a prospective cohort study].
candidates.journal: Nan fang yi ke da xue xue bao = Journal of Southern Medical University
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the combined predictive value of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)‑derived global longitudinal strain (GLS) and peripheral blood neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with first-time acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort study, 134 patients with first-time AMI (99 male and 35 female patients aged 33-83 years, mean 60.19±11.7 years) were enrolled between June, 2022 and July, 2025. All the patients underwent PCI and were followed up via outpatient visits or telephone for a median of 538 days post-discharge. The patients were divided into non-MACEs (n=103) and MACEs groups (n=31) for comparison of baseline clinical parameters.
RESULTS: Baseline comparisons revealed that the MACEs group had a significantly older age, higher white blood cell count, neutrophil count, NLR, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and NT-proBNP, and lower monocyte counts (all P<0.05) with had higher Gensini scores and incidences of anterior wall infarction, more frequent left anterior descending artery culprit lesions, but fewer right coronary artery lesions and lower rates of TIMI low-risk chest pain (P<0.05). In patients with MACEs, CMR findings revealed significantly higher frequencies of late gadolinium enhancement, end-systolic volume index, paradoxical motion, and aneurysmal wall formation, decreased left ventricular ejection fraction, and reduced infarct-segment and global radial, circumferential, and longitudinal strains (P<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified NLR and GLS as independent predictors for MACEs. ROC curve analysis demonstrated that both GLS (AUC=0.825) and NLR (AUC=0.820) alone had predictive ability for MACEs, but their combination significantly increased the AUC to 0.921 (P<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: CMR-derived GLS and peripheral blood NLR are both strongly associated with post-PCI prognosis

candidates.title: Impact of Recurrent Mitral Regurgitation Following Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair on Long-Term Outcomes.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual mitral regurgitation (MR) after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is a major determinant of outcome. However, the prognostic impact of recurrent mitral regurgitation (recMR) after initially successful M-TEER remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the association between recMR after successful M-TEER and long-term mortality across degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR) and functional mitral regurgitation (FMR).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 461 consecutive patients with MR undergoing successful M-TEER (residual mitral regurgitation ≤2+ at discharge) between 2008 and 2021. recMR was defined as ≥1-grade increase in mitral regurgitation severity at follow-up compared with discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Among 461 patients with MR undergoing M_TEER (mean age 75.0 ± 9.1 years; 60.7% male [280 of 461]; 29.3% [135 of 461] had DMR), recMR occurred in 31.7% (146 of 461) (FMR in 31.9% [104 of 326]; DMR in 31.1% [42 of 135]). The median follow-up time was 3.44 years (Q1-Q3: 1.51-3.99 years). In a 12-month landmark analysis, absence of recMR was associated with improved survival (log-rank, P = 0.0088). At 4 years, all-cause mortality was 44.8% (95% CI: 38.7%-50.3%) in patients without recMR and 56.3% (95% CI: 47.2%-63.9%) in those with recMR. In multivariable Cox regression, recMR independently predicted higher mortality (HR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.06-1.93; P = 0.019). The survival difference was significant in patients with DMR (log-rank, P = 0.014) but not with FMR (P = 0.11).
CONCLUSIONS: recMR is common and independently associated with increased mortality after M-TEER, with a more pronounced effect in patients with DMR. Identification of patients at risk may inform closer surveillance and timely reintervention.

candidates.title: Periprocedural Pulmonary Hypertension and Outcomes After Mitral Valve Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is common in patients undergoing mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), but the prognostic significance of periprocedural PH changes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between periprocedural PH patterns and clinical outcomes after M-TEER and to identify predictors of residual and new-onset PH.
METHODS: The OCEAN-Mitral registry prospectively enrolled 3,764 patients with severe mitral regurgitation treated with M-TEER. Among 3,484 patients with paired echocardiographic tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) data, PH was defined as TRPG >31 mm Hg. Patients were classified as having no PH, normalized PH, new-onset PH, or residual PH according to pre- and postprocedural PH status. The primary endpoint was 2-year cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of residual and new-onset PH.
RESULTS: No PH was observed in 1,432 patients (41.1%), normalized PH in 763 (21.9%), new-onset PH in 298 (8.6%), and residual PH in 991 (28.4%). The 2-year incidence of the primary endpoint differed significantly across groups (17.6%, 18.1%, 27.2%, and 27.6%, respectively; P < 0.001). Normalized PH showed outcomes comparable to no PH (adjusted HR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.78-1.24). In contrast, new-onset PH (HR: 1.46; 95% CI: 1.10-1.93) and residual PH (HR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.13-1.68) were independently associated with adverse outcomes. Severe tricuspid regurgitation, baseline TRPG >50 mm Hg, and tricuspid annular dilation predicted residual PH, whereas residual mitral regurgitation and postprocedural transmitral gradients >5 mm Hg predicted new-onset PH.
CONCLUSIONS: Periprocedural PH dynamics provide robust risk stratification after M-TEER, identifying low-risk patients with PH normalization and high-risk subsets with residual or new-onset PH, requiring closer surveillance and procedural optimization. Registration Treatment a

candidates.title: Safety and Effectiveness of a Novel Laser-Based Intravascular Lithotripsy System for Coronary Calcium: FRACTURE Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) has emerged as a promising option to modify calcium.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a novel laser- and optic-based quad-emitter IVL system in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions.
METHODS: FRACTURE was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm trial. The primary safety endpoint was 30-day freedom from major adverse cardiac events (MACE; composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization). The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success (successful stent delivery with a final residual stenosis <50% and freedom from in-hospital MACE). Both endpoints were evaluated against prespecified performance goals. An optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy was performed.
RESULTS: A total of 420 patients (mean age: 71.2 ± 9.01 years; 74.0% male) were enrolled. Median calcified length was 34.4 mm (Q1-Q3: 21.3-52.5 mm). Among 106 patients with OCT, at the site of maximum calcification, the calcium arc was 271.89° ± 77.35° and the median thickness was 0.88 mm (Q1-Q3: 0.72-1.11 mm). OCT confirmed calcium fracture in 67% of lesions; the median minimal stent area was 6.51 mm2 (Q1-Q3: 4.85-7.78 mm2), and stent expansion was 94.2% ± 19.4% at the site of maximum calcification. The primary safety endpoint of 30-day freedom from MACE was 93.3% (373/400; with lower bound of 95% CI of 90.8%, exceeding the 86.2% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). The primary effectiveness endpoint of procedural success was 93.7% (374/399; with lower bound of 95% CI of 91.3%, exceeding the 85.8% performance goal [P < 0.0001]).
CONCLUSIONS: The quad-emitter IVL system is a safe and effective option to modify severe calcified coronary lesions and facilitate stent implantation.
REGISTRATION: (Modification of Coronary Calcium With Laser Based Intravascular Lithotripsy for Coronary Artery Disease [FRACTURE]; NCT06181240).

candidates.title: Morphology-Dependent Dose-Response of Intravascular Lithotripsy on Coronary Calcium Fracture.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) uses ultrasonic acoustic pressure waves to modify calcification to enable optimal balloon and stent expansion in calcified lesions. However, the dose-response relationship for creating fractures within calcified lesions of different calcium morphologies is unknown.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the dose-dependent effects of IVL on calcium fracture overall and in the setting of calcification arc <180° vs ≥180°.
METHODS: Micro-computed tomography images were acquired before and after 10, 20, 40, 60, 80, and 120 pulses of IVL treatment (Shockwave Medical) in an ex vivo study of 5 cadaveric human hearts (15 coronary lesions). A total of 30 cross-sections of micro-computed tomography (2 sections per lesion) were analyzed for this study.
RESULTS: Cumulative fracture occurrence increased progressively with the number of IVL pulses delivered, with fractures observed in 33% of sections after 10 pulses, 50% after 40 pulses, and 60% after 120 pulses. Calcification arc ≥180° exhibited a higher fracture occurrence compared with arc <180° (P = 0.028). After adjustment for pulse number, calcification arc ≥180° was associated with significantly higher fracture counts compared with arc <180° (rate ratio = 6.1, P = 0.003).
CONCLUSIONS: Fracture occurrence following IVL increased with cumulative pulse delivery and differed significantly according to calcification concentricity. Calcification arc ≥180° demonstrated a higher and earlier likelihood of fracture occurrence than arc <180°, independent of pulse number. These findings establish a clear dose-dependent relationship between IVL pulse delivery and fracture formation and highlight calcification concentricity as a key determinant of fracture response.

candidates.title: Mechanical Aortic Valve Replacement in Congenital Heart Disease Using the SJM Valve.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mechanical aortic valve replacement (mAVR) with the St. Jude Medical (SJM) prosthesis is an established treatment. However, data on prosthesis-related adverse events in patients with congenital heart disease (CHD) and aortic valve pathology are scarce.
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, observational study included all CHD patients aged ≤ 45 years who underwent mAVR with an SJM prosthesis between 1993 and 2020. Survival and valve-related complications, including thromboembolism, bleeding, endocarditis, stenosis, regurgitation, and reoperation, were assessed. Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed to estimate time-dependent freedom from events.
RESULTS: A total of 54 patients (mean age at surgery: 21 ± 9 years; 80% male) with a mean follow-up of 8.9 ± 6.6 years were included. Survival was 95.5% at 5 years and 91.9% at 10 and 15 years postoperatively. Relevant, interestingly often only transient, valvular dysfunction defined as peak gradient ≥ 50 mm Hg and/or ≥ moderate regurgitation occurred in 22% of patients. Freedom from prosthesis explantation was 97.4% at 5 and 10 years and 93.1% at 15 years. Freedom from anticoagulation-related events at 5, 10, and 15 years was 95.3%, 88.9%, and 84.9%, respectively. Freedom from prosthetic valve endocarditis was 97.4% at 5 years, 94.7% at 10 years, and 90.4% at 15 years.
CONCLUSION: SJM mechanical aortic valve replacement in pediatric and young adult patients with CHD demonstrated favorable midterm survival, low reoperation rates, and acceptable prosthesis-related morbidity. Prosthetic valve dysfunction was frequently transient and rarely required reoperation, supporting SJM valves as a durable option with appropriate prosthesis sizing, anticoagulation, and long-term follow-up.

candidates.title: Exploring cardiac kinetic energy in children with atrial septal defects: a case-control study.
candidates.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
candidates.abstract: Kinetic energy (KE) of intracardiac blood flow constitutes an important part of the heart's energy expenditure and can be quantified using four-dimensional (4-D) flow cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). Pediatric patients with atrial septal defect (ASD) have volume-loaded right ventricles and underfilled left ventricles due to left-to-right shunting, which could make ASD a useful model to study such altered ventricular loading conditions in congenital heart disease to explore related pathophysiological changes to KE. To characterize ventricular KE in children with ASD before and after treatment, we matched patients to controls. We recruited 22 patients with ASD (8 males, median/[IQR]: 8.5/[5-12] yr) and performed repeat CMR in 16/22 (72.7%) at means ± SD: 7.7 ± 1.7 mo following treatment. Left ventricular (LV) and right ventricular (RV) KE were assessed by 4-D flow CMR. Results were compared with 11 controls. Before treatment, RV peak diastolic KE was higher in patients with ASD compared with controls (P = 0.02) and normalized afterward (P = 0.42) with abolishment of diastolic ASD streaming. Indexed for ventricular volume at the time of peak KE (iKE), RV peak systolic and peak diastolic iKE decreased among repeatedly assessed ASD after treatment (both: P < 0.01), suggesting altered RV energetics not only attributable to RV volume changes. After treatment, RV iKE was comparable between patients and controls (systolic: P = 0.18; diastolic: P = 0.87). Within the ASD group, LV peak systolic KE increased with increased LV volumes after treatment (P < 0.01), whereas LV peak diastolic KE did not change (P = 0.09). How the different RV and LV peak diastolic KE responses reflect different diastolic ventricular remodeling warrants further investigation.NEW & NOTEWORTHY During systole, RV peak KE among patients with ASD decreased after treatment independent of peak RV volumes, whereas LV peak systolic KE increased after ASD treatment due to improved LV filling conditions. candidates.title: EchoNext-Mini: A Dataset and Baseline AI Model for Detecting Structural Heart Disease from Electrocardiograms.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Structural heart disease (SHD) screening has traditionally been limited to echocardiography, limiting access and impacting patient outcomes. We recently published EchoNext, an artificial intelligence (AI) model for detecting structural heart disease from electrocardiograms (ECGs), creating new opportunities for screening.
METHODS: In this work, we describe the EchoNext-Mini dataset and model. The EchoNext-Mini dataset is a deidentified subset of the EchoNext dataset consisting of 100,000 ECGs from NewYork-Presbyterian/Columbia University Irving Medical Center, along with corresponding echocardiogram-derived SHD diagnoses and demographic information. Using this dataset, we trained the EchoNext-Mini model, an AI model to detect structural heart disease from ECG waveforms with the same architecture as the original EchoNext model.
RESULTS: The EchoNext-Mini dataset contains 100,000 ECGs from 36,286 patients along with 11 SHD diagnosis labels. Overall, 52% of ECGs are positive for any SHD, with the most common diagnoses being elevated left ventricular wall thickness (24%), heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (24%), and pulmonary hypertension (19%). The EchoNext-Mini model achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 82.0 (80.9-83.1), 95% confidence interval (CI), a sensitivity of 70.1 (68.3-71.9), 95% confidence interval (CI), and a specificity of 77.9 (76.5-79.4) in detecting SHD from ECG waveforms, versus an AUROC of 85.2 achieved by the original EchoNext model. AUROCs in detecting subdiagnoses of structural heart disease range from 73.4 (71.9-75.1; left ventricular wall thickness ≥1.3 cm) to 86.6 (84.9-88.2; right ventricular systolic dysfunction).
CONCLUSIONS: We have made the EchoNext-Mini model and dataset publicly available to enable further research in AI understanding of ECGs. The size of the dataset and prevalence of varied labels enables a wide range of research. The EchoNext-Mini model achieves performance

candidates.title: TARGET-AI: A Foundational Approach for the Targeted Deployment of Artificial Intelligence Electrocardiography in the Electronic Health Record.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) applied to electrocardiograms (ECGs) offers promise for structural heart disease (SHD) screening, yet clinical integration remains challenged by high false-positive rates and a lack of tailored deployment strategies.
METHODS: We developed TARGET-AI, a multimodal approach that integrates longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) with ECGs to define patient phenotypes and support targeted SHD screening opportunities. TARGET-AI uses an EHR foundation model applied to 118 million events from 159,322 individuals, to generate temporal patient-level embeddings and identify screening candidates, and a contrastive vision-language model trained on 754,533 ECG image-echocardiogram report pairs, to detect distinct SHD subtypes with tunable characteristics. We evaluated this in 5198 individuals referred for a transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) within 90 days of an ECG (temporal validation) and in geographically distinct cohorts, including 33,518 UK Biobank participants undergoing protocolized ECG and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and an inpatient cohort of 3628 patients from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC)-IV database with ECG-TTE pairs. We compared discrimination metrics between targeted and untargeted strategies, with bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals excluding zero considered significant.
RESULTS: The TARGET-AI ECG model discriminated 26 SHD subtypes, including left ventricular systolic dysfunction (area under the receiver operating curve [AUROC] of 0.90), severe aortic stenosis (AUROC of 0.85), and elevated right ventricular systolic pressure (AUROC of 0.82). Compared with untargeted screening, targeted screening in the temporal validation set (n=5198) was associated with a significant increase in F1 scores (median: 0.25; range: 0.09 to 0.75) and a decrease in the number of false positives (median: -303; range: -715 to -77) across 26 SHD labels. candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Auscultation to Identify Left Ventricular Dysfunction - Development and External Validation in Prospective Multicenter Studies.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular dysfunction (LVD) is common and associated with adverse prognosis, even in asymptomatic individuals. Early treatment improves outcomes, underscoring the need for efficient strategies to identify patients who may benefit from echocardiographic evaluation. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an AI auscultation method to detect LVD among patients referred for clinically indicated echocardiography.
METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter study, adult patients referred for echocardiography were enrolled to undergo digital auscultation at four standard auscultation sites with simultaneous single-lead ECGs. LVD was defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) less than or equal to 40% on concurrent echocardiography. An ensemble model combining a transformer-based network and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network was trained on multicenter data and externally validated. The model's performance was compared with a seven-cardiologist reader substudy and clinical logistic regression models incorporating clinical variables, single-lead ECG-derived features, and B-type natriuretic peptide levels.
RESULTS: The multicenter training cohort included 2359 patients (mean age, 69.7±13.5 years; 40.4% female; 8.9% with reduced LVEF). The external validation cohort of 964 patients (mean age, 68.6±15.4 years; 38.9% female; 7.6% with reduced LVEF) was obtained from another independent multicenter registry. The four-site AI auscultation outperformed ECG-only models and the clinical logistic models, achieving an area under the receiver operator curve (AUROC) of 0.926 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.911 to 0.939) in the training cohort. In the external validation cohort, AUROC was 0.904 (95% CI, 0.876 to 0.930) and sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 86.3%, 74.2%, and 75.1%, respectively. In a 100-patient reader substudy, AI auscultation outperformed cardiologist consensus in accuracy (82.0% vs. 62.0%; P=0.004). Model p

candidates.title: Vessel Dependent Myocardium at Risk on Coronary CT Angiography Validated Against Dynamic CT Myocardial Perfusion Imaging.
candidates.abstract: Accurate assignment of myocardial territories supplied by individual coronary arteries on coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is essential for estimating myocardium at risk. Validation of coronary-based myocardial segmentation has been limited by co-registration challenges with perfusion imaging as the reference standard. By reconstructing coronary angiograms directly from the dynamic CT myocardial perfusion imaging (CT-MPI), we ensured inherent co-registration between coronaries and perfusion maps. Vessel-specific myocardial territories were assigned using a minimum cost path (MCP) and validated against MBF-derived perfusion defects from the same acquisition. In 22 patients with 27 well-defined ischemic territories MCP-assigned territories showed moderate spatial overlap with CT-MPI-derived hypoperfusion (Dice coefficient 0.72 ± 0.13) with strong surface area correlation (r = 0.81, p < 0.001). Agreement was highest in the left anterior descending (LAD) territory. MCP-based tessellation using inherently co-registered CCTA and CT-MPI enables accurate vessel-specific myocardium-at-risk assessment and offers a promising platform for anatomical-functional integration in coronary disease.

candidates.title: First-trimester Cardiac Assessment in Fetuses With Increased Nuchal Translucency: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the independent and incremental value of a standardized first-trimester binary cardiac assessment for screening severe congenital heart disease (CHD) in fetuses with increased nuchal translucency (NT).
METHOD: This single-center retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included 223 singleton fetuses with NT ≥ 3.0 mm at 11-13+ 6 weeks of gestation who underwent prenatal screening at our hospital between January 2019 and December 2023. First-trimester binary cardiac assessment was performed through blinded review of archived ultrasound images. Clinical and screening variables, including NT thickness and pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP-A), were collected. Missing serum marker data were addressed using multiple imputation. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were used to assess the predictive and diagnostic performance of the cardiac assessment alone and in combination with conventional screening indicators. The DeLong test was used to compare the baseline model (NT + PAPP-A) with the incremental model (NT + PAPP-A + cardiac assessment).
RESULTS: A positive first-trimester cardiac assessment was independently associated with severe CHD (adjusted OR = 4.02, 95% CI: 1.09-14.87). In the primary imputed analysis, the baseline model (NT + PAPP-A) had an AUC of 0.840 (95% CI: 0.772-0.912), and the incremental model adding cardiac assessment had an AUC of 0.879 (95% CI: 0.812-0.945); however, the DeLong test did not show a statistically significant difference (p = 0.243). The cardiac assessment showed particularly high sensitivity for left-sided obstructive cardiac malformations (90.0%).
CONCLUSION: A standardized first-trimester cardiac assessment is independently associated with severe CHD in fetuses with thickened NT. Adding it to NT thickness and maternal PAPP-A did not significantly improve model discrimination in this retrospective cohort, although the AUC increased numerically. Prospective mult

candidates.title: Assessing Calcified Coronary Lesions to Guide Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: From Angiography to Intracoronary Imaging.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Coronary artery calcification is a leading cause of stent failure and a strong predictor of adverse outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Accurate characterization of calcium burden, depth, and morphology is central to procedural planning, targeted treatment, and better outcomes. This review summarizes the contemporary armamentarium for imaging calcified coronary lesions, from coronary angiography and computed tomography to advanced intracoronary imaging, and how it facilitates treatment. Methods: We synthesized evidence from landmark studies, validated imaging scoring systems, registries, and current guideline and consensus documents addressing the assessment and imaging-guided treatment of coronary calcification. Results: Invasive angiography shows poor diagnostic accuracy for coronary calcium detection, characterization, and quantification. Coronary CT angiography noninvasively quantifies calcium (Agatston score and three-dimensional volume) and supports preprocedural planning, although it may overestimate calcium volume. Intravascular imaging by means of intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) and optical coherence tomography (OCT) effectively detects coronary calcium. Their use is associated with improved clinical outcomes compared with sole angiographic guidance. The addition of near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS-IVUS) characterizes lipids within calcified plaque and high-risk calcified nodules. OCT provides the highest spatial resolution and uniquely measures calcium thickness and longitudinal calcium length, while the utilization of artificial intelligence further enhances calcium assessment. Integration of these modalities into a morphology-based, imaging-guided approach facilitates calcium detection and modification and supports PCI optimization. Conclusions: Intravascular imaging, along with coronary CT angiography, has transformed the assessment of calcified coronary lesions. Combining their strengths enables precise, lesi

candidates.title: Cardiac Computed Tomography in Infective Endocarditis: A Radiological Perspective on Structural Complications and Emerging Diagnostic Technologies.
candidates.abstract: Background: Infective endocarditis (IE) remains a life-threatening disease associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography are the first-line imaging modalities, but their diagnostic performance may be reduced in patients with prosthetic valves, intracardiac devices, previous cardiac surgery, extensive calcification, or suspected periannular extension. Cardiac computed tomography (CT) provides complementary high-resolution anatomical information and has gained increasing importance within contemporary multimodality diagnostic pathways. Scope: This Review critically examines the current role of cardiac CT in IE, including acquisition and reconstruction strategies, lesion-specific imaging findings, applications in native, prosthetic, transcatheter, and device-related infection, extracardiac assessment, and preoperative planning. Comparative observations regarding echocardiography and selected multimodality techniques are integrated where directly relevant. Emerging applications of spectral CT, photon-counting detector CT, deep learning reconstruction, radiomics, and artificial intelligence are appraised according to four levels of evidence: clinically validated IE applications, preliminary IE-specific evidence, indirect cardiovascular evidence, and conceptual applications. Main Findings: Cardiac CT is particularly valuable for detecting and anatomically characterizing periannular complications, including abscesses, pseudoaneurysms, fistulous tracts, inflammatory extension, and prosthetic dehiscence. Multiphase electrocardiography (ECG)-gated acquisition improves the assessment of dynamic valvular and prosthetic abnormalities. Transesophageal echocardiography remains more sensitive for small or highly mobile vegetations, leaflet perforation, regurgitant jets, and intracardiac flow abnormalities, demonstrating that the two techniques are complementary rather than interchangeable. Cardiac CT also contributes to coro

candidates.title: Incremental Value of Cardiovascular CT in Neonates and Infants with Congenital Heart Disease: An Integrated Multimodality Imaging Approach.
candidates.abstract: Background: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is the first-line imaging modality in neonates and infants with congenital heart disease (CHD), whereas cardiovascular computed tomography (CCT) is generally reserved for selected questions that remain unresolved after echocardiography. We evaluated the incremental diagnostic contribution of CCT within this multimodality imaging pathway. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients aged <1 year with CHD who underwent CCT after multidisciplinary review because TTE was inconclusive or additional anatomic definition was required for surgical planning. The primary endpoint was the incremental anatomic information provided by CCT beyond TTE. Secondary analyses included diagnostic performance against operative findings, acquisition characteristics, radiation exposure, contrast administration, and procedural safety. Results: Twenty-six patients were included; 14 (53.8%) were neonates. CCT was requested most frequently to assess coronary anatomy (9/26, 38.5%), followed by the pulmonary veins (4/26, 15.4%), aortic arch (3/26, 11.5%), and pulmonary arteries/MAPCAs (4/26, 15.4%). CCT provided additional anatomic characterization in 14/26 patients (53.8%), predominantly involving extracardiac vascular structures, and was discordant with TTE regarding the unresolved target anatomy in 12/26 (46.2%). Against the operative findings, TTE accuracy was 96.2% for intracardiac abnormalities, 41.2% for extracardiac abnormalities, and 11.1% for coronary abnormalities; corresponding CCT accuracy was 100%, 94.1%, and 100%. CCT directly informed the surgical approach in two patients with total anomalous pulmonary venous drainage. All examinations provided sufficient image quality to address the specific clinical question for which CCT was performed, and no contrast-related adverse events occurred. candidates.title: Prognostic Value of Plaque Burden Beyond Stenosis Severity in Patients with Stable Chest Pain Undergoing Coronary CT Angiography.
candidates.abstract: Introduction: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a noninvasive test for suspected coronary artery disease (CAD), but the prognostic value of integrating plaque burden into CAD-RADS 2.0 has not been fully evaluated. We aimed to assess whether the high-risk CAD-RADS 2.0 category, which combines stenosis severity and segment involvement score (SIS), provides prognostic information beyond stenosis severity in patients with stable chest pain. Methods: We retrospectively included 563 consecutive patients with stable chest pain who underwent CCTA between 2017 and 2022. CAD-RADS 1.0 categories and CAD-RADS 2.0 plaque burden grades were assigned by experienced radiologists. High-risk CAD-RADS 2.0 was defined as CAD-RADS ≥ 3 or any CAD-RADS with P-SIS ≥ 3. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Given the limited number of events, multivariable analysis was restricted to clinically justified parsimonious Cox proportional hazards models. A model including age, sex, and significant stenosis was compared with a model including age, sex, and the high-risk CAD-RADS 2.0 category. A formally nested extended model additionally included severe-to-extensive plaque burden. Results: Over a median follow-up of 51.2 months, 41 patients (7.3%) experienced MACEs. Among patients with non-obstructive CAD (CAD-RADS 1-2), 29 of 477 (6.1%) experienced MACEs, and 85.4% of these events occurred in patients with severe or extensive plaque burden (P3-P4). After adjustment for age and sex, significant stenosis was not associated with MACEs, whereas the high-risk CAD-RADS 2.0 category was independently associated with MACEs (HR 2.88, 95% CI 1.07-7.75; p = 0.036). Addition of plaque burden to a model including age, sex, and significant stenosis increased the Harrell C-index from 0.760 to 0.772 and significantly improved model fit (likelihood-ratio χ2 = 5.41; p = 0.020). candidates.title: Vulnerable Coronary Plaques on CT Angiography: Imaging Biomarkers, Artificial Intelligence, and Emerging Technologies for Risk Stratification.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Increasing evidence has demonstrated that many acute coronary events originate not from severely obstructive lesions but from structurally unstable atherosclerotic plaques. Consequently, the identification of vulnerable plaques has become a major objective in contemporary cardiovascular imaging. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) has evolved from a modality primarily focused on luminal stenosis assessment into a comprehensive non-invasive technique capable of evaluating plaque morphology, composition, and overall coronary atherosclerotic burden.
RESULTS: Our review summarizes current evidence regarding the role of CCTA in the detection and characterization of vulnerable coronary plaques. Particular emphasis is placed on imaging biomarkers associated with plaque instability, including low-attenuation plaque, positive remodeling, spotty calcifications, and the napkin-ring sign, which have been consistently linked to an increased risk of adverse cardiovascular events. Advances in quantitative plaque analysis have further enhanced the ability of CCTA to assess plaque burden and monitor disease progression. Emerging technologies are rapidly expanding the capabilities of coronary CT imaging. Spectral CT techniques and photon-counting detector CT offer improved tissue characterization and enhanced visualization of plaque components. In parallel, artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms are enabling automated plaque detection, segmentation, and risk prediction, facilitating more precise and reproducible analysis of large imaging datasets.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite these advances, limitations remain, including restricted spatial resolution for microstructural plaque assessment and the limited ability of conventional CT to directly evaluate biological processes such as inflammation. Future developments integrating advanced CT technologies, artificial inte

candidates.title: Heart failure with supranormal ejection fraction: is it the new Ariadne's string?
candidates.abstract: Heart failure with supranormal ejection fraction (HFsnEF) is an emerging and incompletely characterized phenotype within the heart failure (HF) spectrum. Although no universally accepted LVEF threshold for HFsnEF has been established and different definitions have been used across published studies, for the purposes of this review HFsnEF is operationally defined as HF with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) > 65%. Importantly, a supranormal LVEF should not be interpreted as evidence of enhanced ventricular performance. Patients with HFsnEF may exhibit smaller left ventricular (LV) volumes, concentric remodeling, increased myocardial stiffness, impaired longitudinal deformation, reduced stroke volume and preload reserve, and elevated filling pressures, particularly during exercise. HFsnEF is unlikely to represent a single disease entity; rather, it encompasses heterogeneous pathophysiological substrates and clinical phenotypes, including hypertensive and cardiometabolic remodeling, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), and other conditions associated with hyperdynamic ventricular function. Accordingly, the diagnostic evaluation should extend beyond recognition of an elevated LVEF and systematically identify the underlying phenotype and potentially treatable causes through comprehensive echocardiography, myocardial deformation imaging, cardiac magnetic resonance, disease-specific testing, and exercise or invasive hemodynamic assessment when indicated. Therapeutic evidence specific to HFsnEF remains limited. No randomized clinical trial has specifically evaluated conventional HF pharmacotherapy in a population prospectively defined by LVEF > 65%; therefore, evidence for conventional HF and cardiometabolic therapies is derived predominantly from broader HFpEF populations or subgroup analyses and should be regarded as indirect rather than definitive evidence for HFsnEF.
