candidates.title: Valve-in-valve transcatheter mitral valve replacement via totally endoscopic endoclamp-assisted approach after failed bioprosthetic mitral valve: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Endoscopic Endoclampassisted MViV can expand the armamentarium for complex redo mitral surgery, offering excellent early clinical and haemodynamic results in selected patients. A 50 year-old man with heavy alcohol and tobacco use and two previous mitral operations (repair, then bioprosthetic replacement eight years earlier) presented with progressive dyspnoea (NYHA III). Transthoracic and transoesophageal echocardiography revealed severe mixed stenosis/regurgitation of a 33 mm Medtronic Mosaic bioprothesis. No endocarditis was found preoperatively. After shared decisionmaking, minimally invasive videoassisted right minithoracotomy under endoaortic balloon occlusion (Endoclamp®) was planned. Intraoperatively, the degenerated valve was firmly embedded in the native annulus and could not be safely explanted. A 29 mm SAPIEN 3 Ultra transcatheter heart valve was therefore deployed inside the surgical frame under direct vision on cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Postdeployment echocardiography showed a mean gradient of 8 mmHg without paravalvular leak or LVOT compromise. The patient was extubated on postoperative day 2; aside from temporary difficulties in respiratory weaning, recovery was uneventful, and he was discharged home on day 9.

candidates.title: Safety and tolerability of rapid vericiguat initiation and titration alongside GDMT optimization in HFrEF: a prospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) remains challenging to manage, particularly in Asian populations. Although vericiguat may complement guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), the safety and tolerability of rapid initiation and titration in Chinese patients with HFrEF require further evaluation.
METHODS: This single-center, prospective, single-arm, self-controlled cohort study included 140 patients who received at least 1 dose of vericiguat 5 mg and constituted the treated population; 133 had evaluable 14-day titration and short-term safety data. Patients were monitored for dose-titration success, blood pressure, renal function, electrolytes, hepatic function, hemoglobin, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) over 14 days. Echocardiography was performed at 12 and 20 weeks.
RESULTS: The mean age was 61.5 ± 14.2 years, and baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was 32.87 ± 8.51%. On a treated-population basis, 131 of 140 patients (93.6%) achieved the target vericiguat dose of 10 mg by day 14; among patients with evaluable titration data, 131 of 133 (98.5%) achieved target-dose uptitration. Median NT-proBNP decreased by 44.0% from baseline to day 14 (p < 0.001), without clinically notable blood pressure changes on the day after vericiguat initiation. At 20 weeks, LVEF increased by 8.26% (p < 0.001), accompanied by reductions in left ventricular diastolic diameter and left atrial diameter. No significant renal, hepatic, or electrolyte safety signals were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Rapid initiation of vericiguat 5 mg alongside GDMT optimization showed acceptable short-term safety and tolerability in Chinese patients with HFrEF. These findings support further randomized controlled trials to clarify the independent contribution of vericiguat to cardiac remodeling.

candidates.title: Thymic-thoracic ratio combined with cardiac axis as a rapid primary screening index for fetuses with conotruncal anomalies: based on sequential cross-sectional scanning.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Conotruncal anomalies are complex and variable and difficult to diagnose. The aim of this study is to investigate the diagnostic value of thymic-thoracic ratio (TT ratio) and Cardiac Axis(CAx) in rapid screening of fetal conotruncal anomalies.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective case-control study was conducted on fetuses from January 2021 to December 2024. Fetal CAx and TT ratio were routinely measured. The Mann-Whitney U test and the Kruskal-Wallis test were used to compare the data. Curve estimation and Pearson correlation were performed to assess the correlation between CAx and TT ratios and gestational age within the group. Logistic regression analysis and ROC curves were conducted.
RESULTS: A total of 91 fetuses with conotruncal anomalies were identified and compared with 104 fetuses with non-conotruncal anomalies and 127 fetuses with normal structures. Compared with the normal group, the TT ratio was significantly reduced in the conotruncal anomalies group (P < 0.001), and the CAx significantly skewed to the left (P < 0.001). In the non-conotruncal anomalies group, only the CAx deviation was significantly different (P < 0.001). Logistic regression analysis revealed that both TT ratio and CAx serve as indirect indicators of conotruncal anomalies, with the area under the ROC curve for the combined prediction model, including TT ratio and CAx, being 0.875. Measurement results demonstrated good consistency both between and within observer groups.
CONCLUSIONS: CAx and TT ratio present distinct manifestations in fetuses with conotruncal anomalies. Their combined use yields potential diagnostic performance for rapidly identifying fetuses with conotruncal anomalies.

candidates.title: Genetic Insights Into Cardiomyopathy With Restrictive Phenotype: Implications for Diagnosis and Personalized Care.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype is uncommon, genetically heterogeneous, and difficult to distinguish from advanced hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy. We aimed primarily to determine the diagnostic yield and spectrum of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants among patients with an echocardiographically defined restrictive phenotype; genotype-imaging and survival comparisons were prespecified exploratory analyses.
METHODS: We screened 568 patients with cardiomyopathy who underwent whole-exome sequencing and comprehensive echocardiography. Thirty-three met the operational definition of restrictive phenotype. Variants were classified. Genotype-imaging associations and survival were analyzed exploratorily.
RESULTS: Among the 568 patients, 33 exhibited a restrictive phenotype: 7 had restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM), 20 had hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype (HRCM), and 6 had dilated cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype (HDRCM). Variant carriers had a smaller aortic sinus diameter. In addition, MYBPC3 variant carriers had greater ventricular wall thickness and more frequent septal hypertrophy. Both the HRCM and HDRCM groups showed hypertrophic features, with interventricular septal hypertrophy occurring more frequently in the HDRCM group. The estimated 5-year survival was 54.5%, and survival did not differ significantly according to genetic-variant status.
CONCLUSIONS: Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were frequent in this single-center cohort with restrictive physiology and were associated with selected imaging features. These exploratory findings support integrated genetic and echocardiographic evaluation.

candidates.title: Tricuspid Chordae Tendineae Rupture Detected After Repair of a Delayed Traumatic Left Ventricular Aneurysm: A Case Report.
candidates.journal: The American journal of case reports
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND Delayed traumatic cardiac rupture complicated by secondary tricuspid chordae tendineae rupture is an exceedingly rare clinical entity. We report this case to describe the temporal sequence of events from blunt myocardial contusion to left ventricular aneurysm formation and rupture, followed by secondary tricuspid chordae tendineae rupture. While the precise mechanism linking these events remains to be determined, we propose a potential pathophysiological connection. CASE REPORT A patient presented with rupture of a posterior left ventricular aneurysm 54 days after a fall from a height. The patient was emergently placed on venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) for circulatory support and subsequently underwent surgical repair of the aneurysm. Postoperative echocardiography revealed new-onset tricuspid chordae tendineae rupture, prompting elective mechanical tricuspid replacement. Histopathological examination of resected valve tissues revealed chronic degenerative changes. To our knowledge, this is the first report documenting this temporal sequence of delayed left ventricular aneurysm rupture followed by tricuspid chordal rupture after surgical repair. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights the importance of continued clinical and echocardiographic vigilance after severe blunt cardiac injury, particularly for detecting late-emerging structural complications such as aneurysm formation and valvular dysfunction. It also illustrates the potential utility of VA-ECMO as a critical bridging strategy to stabilize patients with traumatic cardiac rupture before surgical repair. The observed temporal association between aneurysm repair and subsequent tricuspid chordal rupture is noted, though the exact causal relationship and underlying mechanism remain uncertain.

candidates.title: Combined Prognostic Value of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance-Derived Myocardial Extracellular Volume and the Fibrosis-4 Index in Patients With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is increasingly recognized as a multisystem metabolic-inflammatory syndrome. We investigated the comparative and complementary prognostic value of cardiac magnetic resonance-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and the Fibrosis-4 index for predicting adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
METHODS: Between 2017 and 2019, 250 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction underwent assessment of myocardial ECV by cardiac magnetic resonance and hepatic fibrosis using the Fibrosis-4 index. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable Cox regression and discrimination analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 1190 days, 75 patients (30.0%) experienced the primary outcome. Both ECV (hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 1.08-1.17]; P<0.001) and the Fibrosis-4 index (HR, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.02-1.22]; P=0.015) independently predicted the primary outcome. Patients with concomitantly elevated ECV and Fibrosis-4 index had a markedly increased risk of adverse events compared with those with low values of both markers. ECV-based models demonstrated superior discrimination compared with Fibrosis-4-based models (concordance index, 0.732 versus 0.663; P=0.011). Addition of ECV to the Fibrosis-4 model significantly improved discrimination, whereas addition of the Fibrosis-4 index to the ECV model improved reclassification (continuous net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement) but not discrimination.
CONCLUSIONS: Both myocardial ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index independently predict adverse cardiovascular outcomes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Although ECV provides greater prognostic discrimination, combined assessment of ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index identifies a subgroup at particularly hig

candidates.title: PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR).
METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed.
RESULTS: At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all P>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (P=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points; P=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all P>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (P=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points; P=0.087).

candidates.title: Albuminuria as a Clinical Marker of Subclinical Myocardial Dysfunction in Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subclinical myocardial dysfunction is common in diabetes and may precede clinically overt heart failure by several years. Albuminuria reflects systemic microvascular injury, but its relationship with the severity of myocardial dysfunction in patients with diabetes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether adults with diabetes and albuminuria have greater echocardiographic evidence of subclinical myocardial dysfunction than those with diabetes and normoalbuminuria.
METHODS: Four electronic databases were searched from inception to March 2026 for observational studies comparing adults with diabetes and albuminuria with those with normoalbuminuria. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects models were used to pool mean differences in global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', left ventricular mass index, e', and ejection fraction. Adjusted regression coefficients and odds ratios were also synthesized, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.
RESULTS: Eighteen reports representing 17 independent cohorts were included, with eight contributing to quantitative synthesis. Absolute GLS was significantly lower in patients with albuminuria (MD, -1.38 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.13 to -0.63; P < 0.001; I² = 82%). A greater strain deficit was observed from microalbuminuria to macroalbuminuria, although formal trend analysis was not possible. E/e' was higher in albuminuric patients (MD, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.18-2.24; P = 0.021), whereas ejection fraction did not differ. Albuminuria remained independently associated with impaired strain (pooled β = 1.06; 95% CI, 0.44-1.68) and higher odds of subclinical dysfunction (OR = 5.55; 95% CI, 3.43-8.98).
CONCLUSIONS: Albuminuria identifies patients with diabetes who have greater subclinical systolic and diastolic myocardial impairment despite preserved ejection fraction. Urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio may he

candidates.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease phenotypes and 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease: a prospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of lean metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease remains uncertain. We evaluated 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in lean versus non-lean MAFLD.
METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 193 adults with MAFLD and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-defined obstructive coronary artery disease at Thong Nhat Hospital, Vietnam. Lean MAFLD was defined as a body mass index <23 kg/m² and non-lean MAFLD as a body mass index ≥23 kg/m². The primary outcome was the first expanded major adverse cardiovascular event (eMACE) within 365 days, including ischemia-driven coronary revascularization. Planned first percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) after baseline CCTA was included. Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 115 patients (59.6%) experienced eMACE. The eMACE rate was higher in lean than in non-lean MAFLD (86.2% vs 54.9%, P=0.002). Among these cases, recorded components were revascularization (108), myocardial infarction (13), unstable angina (26), acute heart failure (1), stroke (0), and cardiovascular death (0); components overlapped. These counts do not establish first-event attribution. Lean MAFLD remained associated with eMACE after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary artery disease (adjusted HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.32-3.26, P=0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with MAFLD and obstructive coronary artery disease, lean MAFLD was associated with a higher 1-year hazard of eMACE than non-lean MAFLD, after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary disease. The small lean group and inclusion of planned revascularization limit extrapolation to non-revascularization events, confirmation in larger cohorts is needed.

candidates.title: Frequency and Risk Factors of Cancer Therapy-Related Cardiac Dysfunction in Patients Receiving Chemotherapy: A Prospective Cohort Study at a Tertiary Centre.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is an increasingly recognised consequence of contemporary oncological treatment. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is insensitive to subclinical myocardial injury, and locally validated thresholds for global longitudinal strain (GLS) are lacking in Vietnamese patients.
OBJECTIVES: To determine the frequency and risk factors of CTRCD in patients receiving chemotherapy, and to validate a localised GLS threshold and a biomarker-based surveillance strategy for early detection.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study of 235 patients at Cho Ray Hospital (September 2023-December 2025). Patients were assessed at baseline and every three months with two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (GLS), high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-TnT) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). CTRCD was defined by international consensus criteria. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis; as the outcome was common, associations were quantified as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) estimated by modified Poisson regression.
RESULTS: CTRCD occurred in 82 patients (34.9%). Incidence was highest with anthracyclines (41.2%) and HER2-targeted therapy (37.2%). A relative GLS reduction ≥12.1% predicted CTRCD with 73% sensitivity and 83% specificity. hs-TnT achieved a 100% negative predictive value (NPV), and combining GLS with hs-TnT in parallel retained a 100% NPV. Hypertension (RR 2.50, 95% CI 1.78-3.50), coronary artery disease (RR 2.47, 95% CI 1.82-3.35) and dyslipidaemia (RR 2.10, 95% CI 1.49-2.97) were associated with CTRCD. HFA-ICOS stratification was strongly predictive, with a stepwise increase in risk up to the very-high-risk category (RR 18.6, 95% CI 7.94-43.6 versus low risk; 100% event rate).
CONCLUSIONS: CTRCD affected one-third of patients. A locally validated GLS threshold combined with hs-TnT enables early, resource-efficient

candidates.title: Quantifying the Functional Effect of Transmural Interpolation Strategies on Atrial Wave Propagation Using a Custom Open-Source Pipeline.
candidates.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) management increasingly relies on patient-specific computational modeling to simulate arrhythmia mechanisms and optimize ablation strategies. However, predictive reliability is strongly influenced by accurate reconstruction of myocardial fiber architecture, which governs electrical anisotropy. Because patient-specific atrial fiber orientations cannot currently be acquired reliably in vivo using diffusion tensor magnetic resonance imaging (DT-MRI), alternative computational mapping strategies are required. This protocol presents a comprehensive, open-source pipeline for constructing patient-specific 3D models of the human left atrium with explicit transmural fiber reconstruction from high-resolution clinical computed tomography (CT) data. The methodology extends the Universal Atrial Coordinate (UAC) framework into the volumetric domain by solving the Laplace-Dirichlet problem to derive a continuous transmural coordinate. This enables transfer of atlas-based fiber orientations and subsequent interpolation across the atrial wall. Linear and threshold-based transmural interpolation strategies are quantitatively compared, and their effects on fiber orientation and macroscopic wavefront propagation are evaluated. Across all six models, the mean angular deviation between interpolation methods was 8.06 ± 1.13°. Electrophysiological simulations demonstrate that the choice of interpolation delayed activation in Region 1 by 2.0 ± 0.6 ms, corresponding to 6.1 ± 1.5 ms (p = 0.031 for both comparisons). The open-source pipeline and patient-specific CT-based atrial models provide a reproducible framework for evaluating the functional effects of transmural fiber reconstruction strategies.

candidates.title: From Slices to Volumes: Comparing 2D, 2.5D, and 3D Residual Networks for Pulmonary Nodule Malignancy-Risk Classification
candidates.abstract: Purpose: To compare 2D, 2.5D, and 3D residual networks for pulmonary nodule malignancy-risk classification and evaluate momentum-contrast pretraining, mild augmentation, and exclusion of indeterminate ratings. Methods: A retrospectively prepared LIDC-IDRI cohort contained 2,654 nodules labeled benign, indeterminate, or malignant using median radiologist ratings. Patient-disjoint splits comprised 1,876 training, 382 validation, and 396 test nodules. Representations included one axial slice, five neighboring slices, and a local CT volume. Each track evaluated a randomly initialized baseline, momentum-contrast pretraining followed by fine-tuning, and supervised training with mild augmentation. Checkpoints were selected by validation Macro-F1. The 2D experiments used three seeds; 2.5D and 3D results were single-run estimates. A separate binary experiment excluded indeterminate nodules. Results: Augmented models achieved test Macro-F1 values of $0.6134\pm0.0075$ for 2D, $0.6537$ for 2.5D, and $0.5403$ for 3D; the 2D uncertainty denotes population standard deviation across seeds. Corresponding accuracies were $0.6128$, $0.6869$, and $0.5455$. Augmentation improved Macro-F1 within every track, whereas the tested pretraining recipes reduced it. Binary Macro-F1 values were $0.8227$, $0.8664$, and $0.7554$, respectively. Conclusion: Augmented 2.5D achieved the highest observed performance. Differences in preprocessing, optimization, capacity, and replication limit attribution to dimensionality. Labels reflect radiologist-assessed malignancy risk rather than pathology-confirmed cancer. Code and experimental results are available at https://github.com/CT-DeepLearning-Team/CT-2D-2.5D-3D-DeepLearning.

candidates.title: CMDiff: Left Atrial Scar Segmentation from 3D LGE MRI Using Conditional Mask Diffusion Model: A Feasibility Study
candidates.abstract: Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) cardiac MRI enables non-invasive assessment of left atrial (LA) scar, an imaging marker associated with atrial fibrillation ablation outcome. However, automatic scar segmentation is hindered by low contrast, the thin atrial wall, scarce labels, and extreme class imbalance. Conditional diffusion offers iterative mask generation, but its suitability for sparse 3D LA scar segmentation remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose Conditional Mask Diffusion (CMDiff), which predicts clean masks using a dynamic-encoder-conditioned 3D sinusoidal UNet. We compared CMDiff with a deterministic baseline on identical cases in five-fold cross-validation of 60 scar-labelled public LASCARQS subjects, with 48 training and 12 held-out cases per fold. CMDiff achieved a scar DSC of 0.47 $\pm$ 0.08, HD95 of 12.89 $\pm$ 6.39 mm, and ASD of 1.91 $\pm$ 0.96 mm, compared with deterministic baseline values of 0.51 $\pm$ 0.08, 10.86 $\pm$ 5.39 mm, and 1.58 $\pm$ 1.03 mm, respectively. Under the same implementation, clean-mask prediction performed substantially better than the noise-prediction configuration evaluated in this study. Thus, CMDiff was technically feasible but did not improve segmentation performance: DSC was lower, and both HD95 and ASD were higher. Direct mask diffusion therefore provides an analytical alternative, but not a competitive performance advance for this task. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/jizhang02/CMDiff.

candidates.title: Selective Event Evidence and Persistent Temporal Priors for Event-Based Point Tracking
candidates.abstract: Event cameras enable tracking under fast motion and challenging illumination. However, stable long-term point tracking remains challenging: event activity is sparse and varies with scene content and motion, complicating correspondence, while trajectory estimates can drift over long sequences. Together, these challenges motivate a tracker that selectively uses informative event evidence and retains trajectory constraints across temporal windows. We propose Selective Event Evidence and Persistent Temporal Priors (SEPT), an event-only framework for tracking any point (TAP) over long sequences. SEPT introduces two complementary modules: Task-Adaptive Event Evidence Modulation (TEEM) and Persistent Trajectory Prior (PTP). Using only tracking supervision, TEEM learns a bounded reliability field that weights the event tensor across space, time, and channels before feature extraction. PTP carries geometric information across overlapping windows by marginalizing a fixed local quadratic trajectory model with a Schur complement. Its visibility-aware correction refines overlap coordinates, while a clipped terminal velocity initializes coordinates at newly exposed timestamps. SEPT builds on the ETAP architecture. SEPT is trained exclusively on synthetic EventKubric data and evaluated on five datasets across TAP and feature tracking. Results show that SEPT outperforms the retrained ETAP baseline in average Jaccard for TAP and in feature age and expected feature age for feature tracking; it also surpasses several methods combining event and frame inputs on EC and EDS. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/sssxxxkkkk/SEPT.

candidates.title: FREE-LIVO: Physically Decoupled Yet Tightly Coupled LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry
candidates.abstract: LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry (LIVO) integrates complementary LiDAR, camera, and IMU measurements to achieve robust state estimation. However, most existing methods assume a fixed relative pose and accurate time synchronization between sensors. Toward modular and heterogeneous robotic systems, this paper presents FREE-LIVO, a tightly coupled odometry method that requires neither a rigid LiDAR-camera rig nor LiDAR-camera time synchronization. The proposed method uses a pretrained image feature matcher to establish correspondences between a camera image and a dense LiDAR intensity image generated from a single LiDAR scan using a generative model. From the resulting 3D point-to-pixel correspondences, we construct reprojection factors that directly constrain LiDAR and camera poses at different acquisition times. These factors are jointly optimized in a single factor graph together with constraints from point cloud registration, visual feature tracking, and the IMU measurements associated with each sensor. On six sequences from the public M3DGR dataset, FREE-LIVO achieves an average absolute trajectory error (ATE) RMSE of 0.45 m without provided LiDAR-camera extrinsic parameters and exhibits minimal accuracy degradation under time synchronization errors of up to 0.5 s. Furthermore, experiments with the LiDAR and camera mounted on separate robots demonstrate that the method can jointly estimate the trajectories of independently moving sensors.

candidates.title: CardioDrift: Automatic Cardiac Motion Tracking on a 3D Atlas Mesh via Shape-aware Coherent Point Drift with Slice Shift Correction
candidates.abstract: Automatic cardiac motion tracking from cine cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging is essential for quantifying myocardial motion abnormalities associated with cardiovascular disease. Existing methods fall into two groups: those that represent motion without anatomical correspondence across subjects and therefore limit inter-subject motion assessment; and those that represent motion with globally corresponding points, which typically require a time-consuming and error-prone semi-automatic step to fit a cardiac atlas to the subject space. To address these limitations, this study proposes CardioDrift, a fully automatic, atlas-based probabilistic framework that represents subject-specific cardiac motion on a 3D atlas mesh with globally corresponding points. The Coherent Point Drift (CPD) formulation is generalised to jointly register the atlas surfaces of multiple cardiac regions to the anatomically corresponding contours extracted from cine CMR segmentation maps throughout the cardiac cycle. Slice-shift correction is embedded in the same probabilistic model, estimating slice-wise translations that suppress the misalignment artefact limiting atlas-fitting accuracy. Evaluation on 1301 randomly selected UK Biobank subjects and the M&M dataset, CardioDrift attains Dice similarity coefficients (DSCs) of $92.23\pm8.70\%$, $82.11\pm7.56\%$, and $88.69\pm4.13\%$ for the left ventricle (LV), myocardium (Myo), and right ventricle (RV), exceeding the strongest baseline on every distance and overlap metric of both datasets.

candidates.title: Semantic Prior-Guided Incomplete Cross-Modal Retrieval with Noisy Labels
candidates.abstract: Cross-modal retrieval (CMR) aims to bridge the semantic gaps between modalities by learning shared representations. Unfortunately, due to the dynamism and inconsistencies in real-world data acquisition, multimodal datasets frequently encounter severe modality incompleteness. Existing incomplete CMR methods adhere to a label-driven paradigm, relying heavily on categorical annotations as the semantic benchmark. However, label noise is difficult to avoid and often coexists with modality incompleteness. To address this challenge, we propose a novel semantic prior-guided framework for incomplete cross-modal retrieval with noisy labels, termed SPIRN. Specifically, SPIRN uses fixed semantic priors as a consistent reference for robust representation learning, noisy-label handling, and missing-modality completion. Based on this reference, Semantic Priors Guidance (SPG) establishes a stable category-level semantic space, Quality-aware Robust Learning (QRL) dynamically evaluates sample quality to distinguish clean samples from noisy ones and handles noise via reverse learning, Prior-guided Global Label Calibration (PGLC) rectifies corrupted annotations for refined supervision, and Confidence-driven Selective Imputation (CSI) recovers missing modalities from a cross-modal memory bank while filtering unreliable imputations with an increasing threshold. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first framework to jointly tackle the dual challenges of modality incompleteness and label noise in the CMR community. Extensive experiments on four widely used benchmark datasets demonstrate that SPIRN outperforms 11 state-of-the-art methods in various scenarios involving both missing modalities and noisy labels.

candidates.title: TAQ-MOTR: Tracking-Aware Detection Query Formation for End-to-End Multiple Object Tracking
candidates.abstract: Tracking-by-propagation (TBP) methods perform end-to-end multi-object tracking by propagating track queries across frames, jointly handling detection and identity association without heuristic post-processing while naturally modeling temporal information. However, as detection and association are tightly coupled, detection queries in TBP are expected to discover currently untracked objects and provide complementary current-frame evidence for challenging tracks whose queries and identities are retained. Existing methods largely inherit detection-query formation from single-frame detection and construct such queries before the decoder with little awareness of trajectory states. Consequently, currently untracked objects may be missed, while challenging tracked objects with reduced visibility under occlusion may lack complementary evidence, causing association failures or duplicate responses. To address these issues, we propose TAQ-MOTR, a tracking-aware detection query formation framework that employs a pre-decoder Hybrid Query Generator (HQG) to fuse current-frame image features, track memory, and learnable memory. By conditioning detection queries on trajectory states, TAQ-MOTR adapts them to \rev{the discovery of currently untracked objects and tracked-object complementation We further introduce a training-only auxiliary detection branch whose one-to-one label assignment is decoupled from that of the main tracking branch, providing additional detection supervision to strengthen the shared HQG and decoder for the discovery of currently untracked objects. TAQ-MOTR improves performance on DanceTrack, SportsMOT, and BFT, achieving 72.0 HOTA, 63.1 AssA, and 76.6 IDF1 on the DanceTrack test set. Code is available at https://github.com/Magicmiya/TAQ-MOTR

candidates.title: Open-Source Framework for the Visualization, Quantification, and Analysis of 4D Flow and High-Dimensional Magnetic Resonance Images
candidates.abstract: Background: Four-dimensional (4D) flow cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) captures 3D anatomy and blood velocity across the cardiac cycle, but current post-processing software is closed, varies across platforms, and sits outside open-source image-computing frameworks. We developed an open-source framework for the import, visualization, and quantification of 4D flow and other high-dimensional CMR within SlicerHeart, an extension for 3D Slicer. Methods: Import 4D Flow reads vendor DICOM, applies preprocessing, and stores velocities as a time-resolved vector field; Analyze 4D Flow provides measurement planes, streamline and Doppler-like visualization, segmentation propagation, and quantification. Underlying both, we extended the Insight Toolkit to store five- and higher-dimensional arrays. Flow quantification was compared with a commercial package (cvi42) and 2D phase contrast in 13 patients with congenital heart disease across 108 paired regions of interest (Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients, ICCs). Consensus-recommended processing methods were also implemented as an open-source library with an automated test suite of analytic and CFD phantoms and clinical acquisitions. Results: The modules integrate with 3D Slicer's segmentation, registration, and rendering tools and export velocity fields and geometry for computational modeling. Agreement with cvi42 was close: forward volume bias -0.1 mL (95% limits of agreement 2.2 to -2.3; ICC 0.997), effective volume per minute bias -0.015 L/min (0.21 to -0.24; ICC 0.994). Against 2D phase contrast, forward volume bias (-2.2 mL) and mean absolute percentage error (21.8%) matched cvi42 (-2.1 mL; 21.3%). Conclusions: This open, extensible framework brings 4D flow CMR into an established image-computing ecosystem and agrees closely with a commercial reference; every step can be inspected, reproduced, and improved.

candidates.title: MCP-Net: Real-Time Coronary Perception Network and Topological Analysis for Robotic Guidewire Navigation
candidates.abstract: Coronary guidewire navigation during percutaneous coronary intervention requires continuous interpretation of vessel anatomy, guidewire position, and target stenosis under two-dimensional X-ray fluoroscopy. While existing approaches commonly address vessel segmentation or device localization as separate tasks, a robotic system requires a more structured perception of the coronary scene to support downstream navigation. In this work, we present a simulation-driven framework centered on a Multi-Task Coronary Perception Network (MCP-Net) for robotic guidewire navigation, integrating coronary vessel segmentation, vascular topology extraction, and roadmap generation. Starting from three-dimensional coronary CT angiography, we generate simulated fluoroscopy images containing vascular structures, simulated guidewires, stenotic lesions with varying severity, and diverse vascular geometries, together with simulation-derived ground truth. MCP-Net jointly performs coronary vessel segmentation, guidewire-tip localization, and stenosis localization from a single fluoroscopic frame. These predictions are subsequently converted into a structured vascular graph containing centerlines, bifurcations, endpoints, branch directions, and branch angles. By associating the predicted stenosis with this graph, the framework generates a roadmap from the automatically selected graph root toward the target lesion. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can jointly recover coronary perception targets and transform them into an interpretable vascular representation suitable for downstream robotic navigation.

candidates.title: Towards Myocardial Infarction Diagnosis: An Investigation into Machine Learning and Deep Learning Algorithms using ECG Data
candidates.abstract: Myocardial Infarction (MI) is a severe and potentially fatal cardiac condition caused by myocardial injury due to ischemia, and timely detection can substantially reduce its mortality. Electrocardiography (ECG) is the primary diagnostic modality for MI, but manual interpretation is susceptible to human error. In this work, we propose Visionary V2, a multi-step, adaptive filtration method for ECG signal normalization, and use it to study machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches to MI detection on the PTB Diagnostic ECG Database using all 15 available leads. On statistical features extracted from the filtered signals, such as the R-R interval, a Bagging ensemble of decision trees reaches 96.6% accuracy, compared with 87.7% when the signals are processed with BioSPPy. We further generate an image dataset from the filtered signals, on which a custom ResNet-50 misclassifies only 1 of 7,000 validation images and a custom CNN reaches an F1 score of about 98.7%. Finally, we apply LIME, Grad-CAM and Integrated Gradients to verify that the image models attend to the ECG waveform rather than the background. These results indicate that careful signal normalization combined with ML and DL models can support fast and accurate automated MI screening.

candidates.title: Investigating AI's potential in risk-stratifying lung cancer screenings for extending screening intervals and reducing workload: A retrospective analysis of a tertiary hospital cohort
candidates.abstract: Objective: We aimed to 1) evaluate whether AI algorithms could identify a very low-risk sub-population Lung-RADS 1/2 cases suitable for a safe switch to biennial screening, and 2) externally validate Sybil, an imaging-based deep learning lung cancer risk prediction tool. Materials and methods: We gathered all lung cancer screenings (LCSs) from a tertiary safety-net hospital (n=3120, up to September 2024), manually extracted relevant clinical data, and analyzed Sybil's performance across various subgroups, with a specific focus on Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases. We simulated LCS interval extension using Sybil and the Brock model risk scores calibrated on a subset of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST). Confidence intervals were obtained through bootstrapping. Results: The median follow-up was 2.3 years (interquartile range 1.5-3.1), with a total 6-year cancer incidence rate of 2.3% (72/3120). Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases comprised 90.5% of our scans. Sybil's overall area under the curve (AUC) ranged from 0.819 to 0.912; while its 2-year AUC for Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases was 0.746. In the screening interval extension simulation, calibrating for a 30% shift to biennial screening translated into 33.8% of negative screens in our data being safely extended using Sybil, with no delayed cancers. The Brock model demonstrated an AUC of 0.513 on our data, with a sensitivity of 18.2% using the 1.5% threshold. Conclusion: Sybil has the potential to safely extend LCS intervals for low-risk individuals, reducing radiology workload and opening spots for life-saving new screenings.

candidates.title: AI-Based MRI Radiomics for Preoperative Detection of Tumor Deposits in Rectal Cancer: A Bivariate Diagnostic Accuracy Meta-analysis
candidates.abstract: Background: In rectal cancer (RC), tumor deposits (TDs) are clinically important as they are associated with a negative impact on prognosis and affect risk stratification as well as management plans. MRI radiomics combined with artificial intelligence (AI) has been explored for non-invasive preoperative TDs detection. However, results vary across studies; therefore, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to pool their diagnostic test accuracy (DTA). Methods: This systematic review and DTA meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Diagnostic Test Accuracy and reported in adherence to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies (PRISMA-DTA). Databases were screened for DTA studies of MRI-based radiomics predicting TDs in adult RC patients with histopathology as reference. Results: Nine studies (2589 patients) were identified. Across included studies, the bivariate meta-analysis showed pooled sensitivity of 0.765 (95% CI 0.714 - 0.809) and specificity of 0.790 (95% CI 0.750 - 0.825), with overall AUC of 0.845 and very low heterogeneity (I2 = 7.3%). In validation datasets, diagnostic performance remained consistent (AUC 0.806), with pooled sensitivity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809) and specificity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809). For MRI modality, T2 weighted image (T2WI) showed higher sensitivity (0.745) than T2WI plus diffusion weighted image (DWI) (0.697), while T2WI+DWI had higher specificity (0.809 vs 0.737) and AUC (0.829 vs 0.796), with no significant subgroup differences (p[≥]0.192). Models combining radiomics with clinical/radiological variables achieved significantly higher sensitivity (0.842 vs 0.657, p<0.001) and higher AUC (0.827 vs 0.752), with comparable specificity. candidates.title: Interpretable ECG manifolds link longitudinal electrical phenotypes to heart-failure risk in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
candidates.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) produces heterogeneous electrical phenotypes whose continuous organization, longitudinal evolution and clinical relevance remain poorly defined. We developed complementary variational-autoencoder representations to map HCM ECG morphology relative to physiological variation and characterize within-subject change. Using 5,194 normal-reference ECGs and 2,594 longitudinal visits from 650 individuals with HCM, we found that HCM overlapped the physiological manifold but extended towards its periphery, while an HCM-oriented manifold largely reorganized shared electrical modes. Mixed-effects models identified longitudinal drift in selected phenotypic axes. A lateral/frontal QRS-force coordinate remained time-dependent after censoring septal reduction therapy, atrial fibrillation and pacing, and lower values were associated with subsequent heart-failure risk in baseline and time-updated analyses. A time-conditioned change VAE identified four interpretable within-subject modes aligned with longer-term trajectories. Sarcomeric genotype was associated with phenotype position but not trajectory rate.

candidates.title: EIT-based non-invasive measurements correlate with pulmonary arterial pressure in patients
candidates.abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate associations between electrocardiogram (ECG)-referenced timing markers derived from electrical impedance tomography (EIT) and invasively measured mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) in patients with cardiovascular disease. ApproachEIT, ECG and pulmonary artery pressure were recorded in seven patients during a protocol combining apnoea and phenylephrine administration. Four waveform landmarks were considered: the maximum, the maxima of the first and second derivatives, and the tangent intersection. Their delays from ECG R waves defined eight markers across the heart and lung regions. Within-patient Pearson and Spearman correlations were calculated against unsmoothed invasive mPAP. Main resultsAcross 56 patient-marker combinations, the mean absolute Spearman coefficient was 0.74. Absolute coefficients reached 0.70 in 40 combinations and 0.80 in 27. Each patient had at least one marker with an absolute coefficient above 0.79. The lung second-derivative timing marker exceeded 0.90 in four patients, more often than any other marker, but showed weaker associations in the remaining three. Associations were positive in 25 combinations and negative in 31. Their strength and direction varied across patients and landmarks. SignificanceThese exploratory findings support studying regional EIT timing as a non-invasive correlate of pulmonary haemodynamics. Validation in independent recordings is required before using these markers to estimate pressure. EIT timing markers are associated with PAP changes in patients; however, there is significant variation between patients.
